item.title: Mexican Killers Of Australian, US Surfers Sentenced 158 Years
item.description: Brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33 respectively, and their friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast when they were shot dead in Baja California state during an attempted robbery. They were camping in a remote beachside area near the city of Ensenada when they were attacked on April 27, 2024. Their bodies were found days later, dumped in a cliff-top well, with gunshot wounds to their heads. The callousness of their killings shocked Ensenada, a surfing mecca that attracts people from around the world. Judge Raul Hernandez ruled last week that the three Mexican defendants, identified only by their first names — Jesus Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Angel Jesus — acted with premeditation. On Friday they were sentenced to 158 years and nine months each. Prosecutors had requested damages of more than $100,000, but the judge ruled against it and said any compensation would have to be pursued through civil proceedings. “There can never be justice for the loss of a son, but we are grateful that these men will never hurt anyone else,” Rhoad’s mother Page said after learning the verdict. This undated handout photo released by the Baja California State Attorney General’s Office (FGE) shows Jesus Gerardo “N,” alias “El Kekas,” one of three men convicted of murdering two Australian tourists and their American friend in 2024 in Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. (Photo by HANDOUT / BAJA CALIFORNIA STATE ATTORNEY GENERAL’S OFFICE (FGE) / AFP) This undated handout photo released by the Baja California State Attorney General’s Office (FGE) shows Irineo “N”— one of three alleged killers of two Australian tourists in 2024 in Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. (Photo by HANDOUT / BAJA CALIFORNIA STATE ATTORNEY GENERAL’S OFFICE (FGE) / AFP) ‘Such cruelty’ The Robinsons’ parents had travelled to Mexico from Australia for the month-long trial and left after the verdict. They had spoken movingly in court about their loss. “It’s hard for a parent to lose a son, and we lost two sons,” Martin Robinson said. Debra Robinson said what hurt the most was that her sons “were treated with such cruelty” in their final hours. The families of the victims followed the sentencing hearing via video link. The former girlfriend of Jesus Gerardo, who is accused of leading the attack, was sentenced to 20 years in prison in November. She admitted to goading her boyfriend into stealing the pickup’s tyres. She said her ex-boyfriend had sneered at the surfers’ pleas for their lives and bragged about items he robbed from them. A 9mm and a .45 calibre pistol were used in the attack. Rhoad’s fiancée, Natalie Weirtz and mother Page addressed the court by video link. Weirtz called for the accused to “be punished so that no other family suffers the same pain.” Baja California is one of Mexico’s most violent states, plagued by organised crime and drug trafficking, although cartel activity does not usually affect tourists. (Photo by HANDOUT / BAJA CALIFORNIA STATE ATTORNEY GENERAL’S OFFICE (FGE) / AFP) This undated handout photo released by the Baja California State Attorney General’s Office (FGE) shows Irineo “N”— one of three alleged killers of two Australian tourists in 2024 in Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. (Photo by HANDOUT / BAJA CALIFORNIA STATE ATTORNEY GENERAL’S OFFICE (FGE) / AFP) ‘Such cruelty’ The Robinsons’ parents had travelled to Mexico from Australia for the month-long trial and left after the verdict. They had spoken movingly in court about their loss. “It’s hard for a parent to lose a son, and we lost two sons,” Martin Robinson said. Debra Robinson said what hurt the most was that her sons “were treated with such cruelty” in their final hours. The families of the victims followed the sentencing hearing via video link. Weirtz called for the accused to “be punished so that no other family suffers the same pain.” Baja California is one of Mexico’s most violent states, plagued by organised crime and drug trafficking, although cartel activity does not usually affect tourists. Other foreign visitors have been targeted in attacks on Mexico’s Pacific coast. Two Australian surfers, Dean Lucas and Adam Coleman, were murdered in 2015 while travelling through the northwestern state of Sinaloa. Their bodies were later burned. item.title: Frattesi turned down Juventus to return to Lazio
item.description: Frattesi turned down Juventus to return to Lazio Davide Frattesi will come up against Juventus this weekend knowing he could have been lining up for the Bianconeri, after turning them down in the summer to rejoin Lazio. According to TuttoMercatoWeb , Juventus made an attempt to bring the midfielder to Turin during the transfer window. The former Inter man instead opted to return to the club where he grew up, taking on a bigger role at the Stadio Olimpico. ROME, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Davide Frattesi of SS Lazio celebrates after scoring an opening goal during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Genoa CFC at Stadio Olimpico on August 30, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) Frattesi chose Lazio over Juventus move That decision gives Juventus-Lazio an extra edge for the 27-year-old, with both sides chasing places near the top of the Serie A table. Since his return, Frattesi has quickly become one of the key figures in the Biancocelesti midfield. He also has a happy history against the Old Lady. As Il Messaggero recalls, Frattesi scored the opening goal of Sassuolo’s 2-1 win in Turin in October 2021, a strike he has since described as one of the most emotional of his career. BOLOGNA, ITALY – AUGUST 24: Davide Frattesi of Lazio looks on before the Serie A match between Bologna FC and SS Lazio at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on August 24, 2026 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) He will now be looking to hurt Juventus again, this time wearing the shirt of his boyhood club.

item.title: "It would be important to find the path that allows us to string together victories."
item.description: "It would be important to find the path that allows us to string together victories." After completing the last session before the match, Girona FC coach Quique Álvarez has assured that the team arrives with good feelings for tomorrow's duel against Andorra at Montilivi. "The team has trained very well and is eager to play at Montilivi in search of a new victory," explained the coach, who highlighted the importance of finding greater consistency in results. In this regard, he acknowledged that "it would be important to find the rhythm that allows us to string together victories. We have been inconsistent in some aspects, and we need to correct that." Quique Álvarez also focused on the team's ability to manage different moments of the matches. "We need to know how to take advantage of the good moments and manage the bad ones," he stated, convinced that this is one of the key aspects to take a step forward in the competition. Regarding the opponent, the Girona coach warned about the difficulty that Andorra will present. "Andorra is a difficult team to play against. Just recently, they beat Castellón, who had never lost before," he recalled. Even so, he expressed confidence in his players' chances and emphasized that "we will step up and compete for sure." Finally, Quique Álvarez analyzed the recent trajectory of the Andorran team, highlighting their recovery after a more challenging stretch of the season. "Andorra started the league dominating, had a bad streak, but in the last few matches, they have won two games and drawn one," he concluded.

item.title: Marc Bartra talks Pau Cubarsi, Golden Boy award, Raphinha, future Barcelona return: ‘The most decisive team’
item.description: Marc Bartra talks Pau Cubarsi, Golden Boy award, Raphinha, future Barcelona return: ‘The most decisive team’ Former Barcelona defender Marc Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award , while describing Hansi Flick’s side as the most decisive attacking team in world football ahead of Real Betis’ meeting with the Catalans. The 35-year-old, who now represents Betis, reflected on Barcelona’s remarkable attacking performances and the development of their young centre-back in an interview with SPORT . Bartra also singled out Raphinha’s extraordinary form and explained what it takes to contain Barcelona’s dangerous forward line. Having experienced Barcelona from inside the dressing room, the former Blaugrana defender offered a detailed assessment of the qualities that make Flick’s team so difficult to stop. Bartra backs Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award Bartra believes Cubarsi deserves the prestigious individual award because of his performances, consistency and maturity despite his young age. The Barcelona defender has established himself as a regular for both his club and the Spanish national team, something Bartra considers particularly significant for a player in his position. “I’d give it to him. He’s earned it through his performances, and especially the way he conducts himself on the pitch – tactically, technically and in terms of his character – despite his young age. “There are some very good players out there, but he’s a first-team regular at Barcelona and for the Spanish national team, and as far as I’m concerned, he’s the leading contender. “It’s not easy for a defender to be awarded this sort of prize. “When all these factors come together – with this generation of players, getting playing time and consistency – the football inside you can really flourish. Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi for Golden Boy award. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “It’s unusual to see a player of his age in this position. What he does is hugely valuable. “I always say that I played alongside Gerard Pique, and his situation is very similar to Cubarsi’s. “I haven’t played with Cubarsi, but we’ve faced each other, and who knows, perhaps one day we’ll meet up, whether for the Catalan or Spanish national teams, to learn from one another.” Bartra names Barcelona as the most decisive attacking team Barcelona’s attacking output has been one of the defining features of their campaign, with the Catalans averaging more than four goals per match. item.content:encoded: Marc Bartra talks Pau Cubarsi, Golden Boy award, Raphinha, future Barcelona return: ‘The most decisive team’ Former Barcelona defender Marc Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award , while describing Hansi Flick’s side as the most decisive attacking team in world football ahead of Real Betis’ meeting with the Catalans. The 35-year-old, who now represents Betis, reflected on Barcelona’s remarkable attacking performances and the development of their young centre-back in an interview with SPORT . Bartra also singled out Raphinha’s extraordinary form and explained what it takes to contain Barcelona’s dangerous forward line. Having experienced Barcelona from inside the dressing room, the former Blaugrana defender offered a detailed assessment of the qualities that make Flick’s team so difficult to stop. Bartra backs Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award Bartra believes Cubarsi deserves the prestigious individual award because of his performances, consistency and maturity despite his young age. The Barcelona defender has established himself as a regular for both his club and the Spanish national team, something Bartra considers particularly significant for a player in his position. “I’d give it to him. He’s earned it through his performances, and especially the way he conducts himself on the pitch – tactically, technically and in terms of his character – despite his young age. “There are some very good players out there, but he’s a first-team regular at Barcelona and for the Spanish national team, and as far as I’m concerned, he’s the leading contender. “It’s not easy for a defender to be awarded this sort of prize. “When all these factors come together – with this generation of players, getting playing time and consistency – the football inside you can really flourish. Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi for Golden Boy award. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “It’s unusual to see a player of his age in this position. What he does is hugely valuable. “I always say that I played alongside Gerard Pique, and his situation is very similar to Cubarsi’s. “I haven’t played with Cubarsi, but we’ve faced each other, and who knows, perhaps one day we’ll meet up, whether for the Catalan or Spanish national teams, to learn from one another.” Bartra names Barcelona as the most decisive attacking team Barcelona’s attacking output has been one of the defining features of their campaign, with the Catalans averaging more than four goals per match. Bartra believes their threat extends beyond individual talent, pointing to their movement, positioning and ability to attack in different situations. “Offensively speaking, Barcelona are currently, in my view, the most decisive team in the world. “Not just because of their physicality and talent, but also because of the way they position themselves in attack, how they find space, and how they attack—whether in set-piece situations or on the counter-attack. “They have a lot of possession, and when they attack, they do so whilst in excellent physical condition. “This allows players like Raphinha, Lamine and Olmo to reach their very best. “To stop them, you need a great deal of communication, leadership and character in defence, because it’s down to everyone, not just the centre-backs. Bartra has praised Barcelona’s performance under Hansi Flick. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “It’s about the team’s behaviour off the ball across all lines, and getting plenty of support: the centre-backs help the full-backs, the midfielders help the centre-backs, and you have to be more intuitive and focused than usual.” Raphinha becoming increasingly difficult to stop Raphinha’s current form has added another angle to Barcelona’s attack, and Bartra believes the Brazilian is operating at a level that makes him particularly difficult for defenders to contain. “At the moment, he seems unstoppable. He’s going through a brilliant spell – an absolutely stunning run. “You might be able to stop him in one moment, but in the next he’ll get past you with ease, using his dribbling and quick shooting. “He’s one of the players most capable of making a difference at the moment.” Bartra opens up on a possible Barcelona return Despite representing Betis, Bartra retains a strong emotional connection with Barcelona, where he developed as a footballer. Asked whether he could return to the Catalan club one day, the defender explained how supporters of both teams continue to make him feel appreciated. “People say that to me a lot on the street – a lot of Betis fans, but also when I go elsewhere, Barcelona fans remember me a lot, and that makes me feel very proud. “ After all, you know what Barcelona means to me. “ And I feel proud when people remember me in Barcelona as well as at Betis, because they’re two clubs I love with all my heart,” he concluded.

item.title: Braves News: Brett Wisely to 40-man roster, Tate Southisene, and more
item.description: The Atlanta Braves have already made some moves this offseason, according to the transaction log. Most notably, infielder Brett Wisely was selected to the major league roster. Outfielder DaShawn Keirsey Jr. was outrighted to Triple-A Gwinnett, and infielder Luke Williams elected free agency. Given his limited big league experience, the decision to add Wisely to the 40-man gives the Braves the option to use him in a later transaction. Atlanta will have plenty of decisions to make as it looks to improve the roster for 2027, and these early moves are a reminder that the team is already working to create flexibility for what comes next. More Braves News: Tate Southisene reached base four times in the recent Arizona Fall League matchup. More in the minor league recap. MLB News: Game 4 of the ALCS has been postponed to tonight due to inclement weather. Game 5 is slated for Sunday evening. From the Feed: Braves special assistant Martin Maldonado is headed to the Detroit Tigers as a quality control coach.

item.title: Eagles’ Jalen Hurts blood clot conspiracy theory recklessly spewed by NFL analyst
item.description: Michael Robinson , an NFL Network analyst, channeling his own version of Charlie’s ‘Pepe Silvia’ rant from “ It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia ,” said Thursday that Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is using a superficial blood clot to escape blame for a losing season. The team’s medical timeline and outside doctors undercut that claim. On “NFL Gameday Kickoff,” Robinson told viewers to “go Google ‘superficial blood clot’ as opposed to a ‘real blood clot.’” He then said Hurts was “ pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” MORE: Concerning Jalen Hurts blood clot note from former NFL team doctor What did Robinson say about Hurts? Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The former Seahawks fullback started by saying the Eagles appeared to be “trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts just so they could have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts.” He then argued that anyone in Hurts’ camp would respond, “Well, if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt too.” Robinson also picked up former Jaguars running back Maurice Jones-Drew’s phrase “lost season.” He used it to describe the quarterback’s absence as self-preservation. Robinson said “I don’t know anything” several times and added “I’m not a medical guy.” But in the same segment he told the audience to research the diagnosis themselves, so the disclaimers didn’t soften the accusation. The theory feeds off a rough stretch in Philadelphia. The Eagles are 2-3 after three straight losses. Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired abruptly on Oct. 6, and the team traded former Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens a day later. The guaranteed money on Hurts’ five-year, $255 million extension runs out after the 2027 season. How the Eagles found the clot The team’s statement lays out a timeline that doesn’t fit a player looking for an exit. Hurts was cleated in the calf during the Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, practiced in full that week and requested treatment after practice on Oct. 8. An ultrasound in London that Saturday revealed the superficial clot, and doctors there concluded “activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play.” The 28-year-old played every offensive snap in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars, riding a stationary bike between series and completing 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown. A quarterback trying to dodge blame for a losing season had an easy out that weekend and didn’t take it. The NFL also confirmed it communicated with the Eagles about the clot before kickoff in London. A follow-up ultrasound Wednesday night “revealed movement in the small blood clot,” and that finding is what ruled him out. item.content:encoded: Michael Robinson , an NFL Network analyst, channeling his own version of Charlie’s ‘Pepe Silvia’ rant from “ It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia ,” said Thursday that Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is using a superficial blood clot to escape blame for a losing season. The team’s medical timeline and outside doctors undercut that claim. On “NFL Gameday Kickoff,” Robinson told viewers to “go Google ‘superficial blood clot’ as opposed to a ‘real blood clot.’” He then said Hurts was “ pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” MORE: Concerning Jalen Hurts blood clot note from former NFL team doctor What did Robinson say about Hurts? Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The former Seahawks fullback started by saying the Eagles appeared to be “trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts just so they could have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts.” He then argued that anyone in Hurts’ camp would respond, “Well, if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt too.” Robinson also picked up former Jaguars running back Maurice Jones-Drew’s phrase “lost season.” He used it to describe the quarterback’s absence as self-preservation. Robinson said “I don’t know anything” several times and added “I’m not a medical guy.” But in the same segment he told the audience to research the diagnosis themselves, so the disclaimers didn’t soften the accusation. The theory feeds off a rough stretch in Philadelphia. The Eagles are 2-3 after three straight losses. Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired abruptly on Oct. 6, and the team traded former Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens a day later. The guaranteed money on Hurts’ five-year, $255 million extension runs out after the 2027 season. How the Eagles found the clot The team’s statement lays out a timeline that doesn’t fit a player looking for an exit. Hurts was cleated in the calf during the Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, practiced in full that week and requested treatment after practice on Oct. 8. An ultrasound in London that Saturday revealed the superficial clot, and doctors there concluded “activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play.” The 28-year-old played every offensive snap in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars, riding a stationary bike between series and completing 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown. A quarterback trying to dodge blame for a losing season had an easy out that weekend and didn’t take it. The NFL also confirmed it communicated with the Eagles about the clot before kickoff in London. A follow-up ultrasound Wednesday night “revealed movement in the small blood clot,” and that finding is what ruled him out. Left tackle Jordan Mailata said Hurts “persevered to play in that game for us.” MORE: Handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot will prove to be defining moment for Eagles Why doctors take the clot seriously The word “movement” is what worries former Chargers team doctor David Chao . Chao said a superficial clot can move and stay superficial. A clot that reaches a deep vein is a different situation. “If it’s a deep vein thrombosis, it starts to be measured in months, not weeks,” Chao said. If a deep vein clot breaks loose and reaches the lungs, it becomes a pulmonary embolism, which Chao said would end Hurts’ season. The strong anticoagulants used to treat it also carry bleeding risks. Chao said, “The big fear is, what if you have a brain bleed?” Temple Health vascular surgeon Andrea Lubitz said superficial clots are generally treated with compresses and painkillers, though some patients need more extensive care. The Eagles’ statement says the team is still determining “the appropriate course of treatment.” Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott called the situation “scary.” He added that “you’re talking about someone’s life, especially with the plane trip.” The Eagles haven’t set a timetable for the Super Bowl 59 MVP’s return. Tanner McKee will start Sunday when the Panthers visit Lincoln Financial Field. item.title: Saquon Barkley Injury Update: Eagles RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed
item.description: Saquon Barkley is battling a hamstring injury originally suffered against the Los Angeles Rams, and he will not play in Week 6. Originally entering the league as the second-overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft , the Penn State product hit the ground running, recording 1,307 yards and 11 touchdowns as a rookie for the New York Giants. He remained an elite running back during his five years with the club before joining the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, where he immediately led the league with 2,005 rushing yards while playing a key role in the team’s championship run. Through four games, Saquon Barkley has recorded a decent 182 yards and no touchdowns on 36 attempts. However, he won’t add to those numbers against the Carolina Panthers. Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during Week 4, and ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the team has officially ruled him out for Week 6. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor Saquon Barkley Injury Update: Eagles RB Didn’t Practice Wednesday The Last Word The Philadelphia Eagles are always at their best with Saquon Barkley in the lineup, but the team desperately needs him to return sooner rather than later. Backup running back Tank Bigsby is currently on the injured reserve, and third-string running back Will Shipley suffered a foot injury that could sideline him for weeks. Quite frankly, the Eagles are running out of bodies at the running back position. With Saquon Barkley sidelined, the team will likely turn to former Houston Texans running back Dameon Pierce to lead the backfield. A former fourth-round pick himself, the Florida product had a promising rookie season in 2022, finishing the campaign with 939 yards and four touchdowns on 220 attempts. However, it’s been all downhill for him since that date. The running back made his debut for the Eagles last week and finished with just 14 rushing yards on 11 attempts.

item.title: New Street Fighter Movie Ends on the Strangest Song Choice Possible
item.description: The soundtrack to Capcom and Legendary's new Street Fighter movie is nothing if not eclectic. The film's music choices skew heavily toward the '90s, during which Street Fighter is set, with songs like Tupac's "Ambitionz Az A Ridah," Soundgarden's "Black Hole Sun," and Meredith Brooks' "Bitch," but it's not afraid to dip into other decades. It's understandable why 50 Cent's "Many Men (Wish Death)" plays during a fight featuring boxer Balrog (who is played by 50 Cent), even if the song feels temporally out of place.

item.title: Cybercrims go beyond stealing data to attack physical building systems
item.description: Late Sunday night, a still-unknown cybercriminal or group hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of French grocery stores, spiking temperatures, spoiling food, and sparking fires. This is part of an ongoing trend of attacking physical systems that can do damage in the real world. In August, a ransomware attack disrupted building-management systems at a Canadian hospital, affecting door access controls, central HVAC monitoring, and the issuing of staff access cards. And three years ago, cyberattacks hit Las Vegas casinos, causing slot machines to go dark, preventing payment kiosks and ATMs from spitting out cash, and locking guests out of their rooms when the electronic keys stopped working. Not all digital intrusions remain in cyberspace, and attackers don’t need to encrypt files and steal data to cause chaos. Hitting physical systems often produces more severe consequences - and turns up the heat on executives to pay an extortion demand. “There was one gig where the customer was refusing to pay, and so the threat actor was like, ‘Hold my beer, have fun getting into your offices,’ and locked everybody out,” Tim Beasley, a senior incident response consultant at Semperis, told The Register. Beasley won’t name the customer, or provide any incriminating information, but said the incident response involved police smashing glass in addition to his team recovering compromised data. “The cops had to break in, and literally get into the building, breaking some windows, so the customer was able to finally get back in,” he said. We asked if the customer paid the ransom demand, and Beasley yelled: “Oh, hell, no!” A report published earlier this month by ServiceNow’s Armis Labs found increasing evidence of ransomware attackers using physical consequences as leverage in their intrusions. “Today’s BAS operate at the intersection of IT and OT worlds, creating unprecedented exposure,” the report said. Ransomware with physical consequences Building automation systems - BAS - are the critical systems that control and monitor facilities’ HVAC, lighting, energy usage, and water consumption. They also oversee badge readers, door locks, surveillance cameras, fire alarm control panels, and other physical safety equipment. As such, BAS make very attractive targets for ransomware operators looking for high-pressure ways to extort organizations into paying multi-million ransom demands. These systems also appeal to government-backed goons and hacktivists looking to ensure maximum psychological and physical impact during destructive cyberattacks. Armis Labs found 73 percent of organizations own BAS that have been used in ransomware attacks, and this same percentage have known exploited vulnerabilities in at least one of their building automation systems. item.content:encoded: Late Sunday night, a still-unknown cybercriminal or group hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of French grocery stores, spiking temperatures, spoiling food, and sparking fires. This is part of an ongoing trend of attacking physical systems that can do damage in the real world. In August, a ransomware attack disrupted building-management systems at a Canadian hospital, affecting door access controls, central HVAC monitoring, and the issuing of staff access cards. And three years ago, cyberattacks hit Las Vegas casinos, causing slot machines to go dark, preventing payment kiosks and ATMs from spitting out cash, and locking guests out of their rooms when the electronic keys stopped working. Not all digital intrusions remain in cyberspace, and attackers don’t need to encrypt files and steal data to cause chaos. Hitting physical systems often produces more severe consequences - and turns up the heat on executives to pay an extortion demand. “There was one gig where the customer was refusing to pay, and so the threat actor was like, ‘Hold my beer, have fun getting into your offices,’ and locked everybody out,” Tim Beasley, a senior incident response consultant at Semperis, told The Register. Beasley won’t name the customer, or provide any incriminating information, but said the incident response involved police smashing glass in addition to his team recovering compromised data. “The cops had to break in, and literally get into the building, breaking some windows, so the customer was able to finally get back in,” he said. We asked if the customer paid the ransom demand, and Beasley yelled: “Oh, hell, no!” A report published earlier this month by ServiceNow’s Armis Labs found increasing evidence of ransomware attackers using physical consequences as leverage in their intrusions. “Today’s BAS operate at the intersection of IT and OT worlds, creating unprecedented exposure,” the report said. Ransomware with physical consequences Building automation systems - BAS - are the critical systems that control and monitor facilities’ HVAC, lighting, energy usage, and water consumption. They also oversee badge readers, door locks, surveillance cameras, fire alarm control panels, and other physical safety equipment. As such, BAS make very attractive targets for ransomware operators looking for high-pressure ways to extort organizations into paying multi-million ransom demands. These systems also appeal to government-backed goons and hacktivists looking to ensure maximum psychological and physical impact during destructive cyberattacks. Armis Labs found 73 percent of organizations own BAS that have been used in ransomware attacks, and this same percentage have known exploited vulnerabilities in at least one of their building automation systems. Additionally, 91 percent of BAS communicate over insecure protocols - opening up an even bigger attack surface for cyber-miscreants wanting to cause physical harm. “The primary thing that we see with any attack on building management systems or physical systems: It’s a great place for the threat actor to hide,” Michael Freeman, ServiceNow’s senior director of threat research, told The Register. “It's easier for them to compromise, and it's easier for them to hide in.” BAS and operational technology (OT) in general have fewer security controls than IT systems. Most require continual uptime, which makes them harder to patch or even scan for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations as this may lead to outages. “One case in particular, against a very large financial institution, the threat actors were staying low and quiet by attacking their BMS systems, and then pivoting into the IT environment,” Freeman said. The intruders were routinely caught - and booted from - the financial institution’s IT systems, so they built backdoors into the BMS to ensure persistent access to both OT and IT networks. “We're also seeing threat actors using AI to understand more building automation systems, especially ones that are using obscure OSs like VxWorks, older Unix-type systems,” Freeman said. AI has entered the chat As multiple security experts have told us in previous interviews, security through obscurity is dead. Not only does AI make it easier for attackers to find bugs – some very obscure and decades old - but it also means criminals no longer need to be OT experts to carry out destructive cyberattacks on critical networks and facilities. Instead, they can use AI to learn all about the obscure protocols and proprietary hardware and software that historically made industrial control systems black boxes. “It’s easier to understand what the controls are,” Freeman said, using the example of an attacker trying to take down a plane, or some similar catastrophic cyberattack. Historically, even advanced, government-backed hacking squads would “be quiet, because you don't know what changing certain settings is going to do,” Freeman explained. “Now you can use AI to say, ‘If I compromise a weight and balance system for airlines, all I need to do now is move this number here to this number, and I just told the system to load heavy stuff on the right side of the plane instead of equal distribution.'” Freeman told us he has seen attackers break into airlines’ OT gear in the past. “But they didn’t know what they were getting into, and so they left them alone,” he said. “Those do cause me concern because in the past I've helped to kick people out of those types of systems.” Industrial orgs increasingly under attack OT security provider Dragos tracks ransomware groups’ claims against industrial organizations on the criminals’ leak sites, along with publicly disclosed intrusions affecting manufacturing and other critical sectors. To be clear: claims on leak sites aren’t always accurate or even true, and the claim itself doesn’t mean operations or control systems were hit. Since 2022, however, “the numbers have been consistently increasing,” Lexie Mooney, senior threat analyst at Dragos, told The Register. The cybersecurity firm tracked 995 ransomware attacks against industrial orgs in 2023, a 49.5 percent increase from 2022. That number jumped more than 87 percent in 2024. Active ransomware groups targeting industrial orgs also grew in 2024 to 80 groups, up from 50 the year before. Dragos tracked 119 ransomware groups impacting more than 3,300 industrial organizations in 2025, and the incidents have steadily increased every quarter this year: 1,020 incidents in the first quarter of 2026 and 1,140 incidents in Q2. “The vast majority of cases are opportunistic,” Abdul Alamri, a senior threat analyst at Dragos, told us. “In some of the cases that we have seen an operational impact, either physical systems or an OT operation, it’s just the nature of the opportunism on the part of those ransomware groups.” This is partially due to the complexity of OT systems, he added. “Ransomware groups want to disrupt operations, and put pressure on the victims to pay the ransom,” Alamri said. “They don’t want to invest that time and effort to target complex systems." It’s usually quicker and easier for financially motivated crims to affect operations via IT systems - as the extortionists did in the August 2025 Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) breach, which halted manufacturing and crippled business operations for months. Internet-connected OT: the next 'low-hanging fruit' The other side of this complexity, however, is that many organizations themselves still lack visibility into their OT environments. Dragos estimates that fewer than 10 percent of OT networks worldwide currently have sufficient network monitoring in place. Plus, in 30 percent of incidents the security firm responded to in 2025, the investigations did not begin with a detection alert, but with someone noticing that “something seemed wrong” in operations. This lack of visibility, combined with threats from AI, worries Alamri. “If you compare the risk that we have seen from humans, to

item.title: Sonay Kartal makes history by reaching biggest final of her career in Wuhan
item.description: Great Britain’s Sonay Kartal made WTA history as she defeated Jelena Ostapenko to reach the biggest final of her career at the Wuhan Open in China. Kartal began the tournament ranked No 170 in the world having missed six months of the season due to a back injury, but has made up for lost time superbly in what is just her second tour-level tournament since March. The 24-year-old has become the lowest-ranked WTA 1000 finalist since the format was introduced in 2009, with victory over former French Open champion Ostapenko adding to impressive wins against world No 6 Elina Svitolina , former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic and former Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini this week. It took another gutsy display from Kartal, who trailed in both sets against the big-hitting Ostapenko but prevailed in a rollercoaster encounter to win two tiebreaks 7-6 (11-9), 7-6 (7-5), saving all six set points she faced across the two-hour battle. Kartal, whose only career title came in the WTA 250 event in Monastir two years ago, will play either six-time grand slam champion Iga Swiatek or French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska in Sunday’s final, with the all-Polish semi-final taking place later on Saturday. “Wow! That was probably one of the toughest of matches I've played,” Kartal said after converting her second match point. “I knew exactly how she was gonna play. At times, she's unplayable, and sometimes you just have to ride that wave. “Mentally, I think this is one of the best performances I've had in my career, so, I’m very, very proud of that one.” More follows

item.title: England stunned by Tonga in World Cup opener
item.description: Tonga had lost their previous six meetings with England before triumphing here [Getty Images] England (0) 12 Try : Brimson, Young Goal : Savala 2 Tonga (10) 30 Tries : Olakau'atu 2, Utoikamanu, Koula Goals : Katoa 3 Penalties : Katoa 4 Four years ago, England were left shocked and shattered by Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals. Now in 2026, Tonga - another Pacific island nation - have done the same with a victory to put England's Australian campaign in immediate jeopardy. Tonga combined classy attacking play with staunch defence, mixed with a pinch of luck - while being cheered on by a ferociously partisan crowd in Perth - to cause a major upset. It was expected that Brian McDermott's team - ranked third in the world - would have enough to open their Group B-C campaign with victory over opponents ranked fifth. But they will now have to pick themselves up for coming group games against France and Papua New Guinea to try to secure a top-two finish in the combined six-team group table and secure a semi-final spot. England's day came apart amid seemingly endless mistakes, wastefulness and a few dodgy refereeing decisions. Arguably the turning point came on 22 minutes, when England got to within a few yards of the opposition line but Victor Radley knocked on after an absolute boneshaker from Tonga captain Jason Taumalolo. The ball was turned over, and the Tongans scored two minutes later. Stefano Utoikamanu streaked through after Isaiya Katoa's superb inside pass cut out George Williams and Kai Pearce-Paul, to the delight of the massed Tongan fans in Perth. For England, it seemed as if the universe was against them. The impressive Katoa converted two penalties given following debatable calls. First, Harry Smith was penalised for obstruction when Dallin Watene-Zelezniak ran into him. Then, Herbie Farnworth conceded a sloppy penalty on the verge of half-time when accidentally tripping Watene-Zelezniak off the ball. England badly needed half-time, and they came out refreshed. Their first flowing move of the home game led to a try for full-back AJ Brimson after being set up by a sensational driving run from Young, holding off two tacklers over 20 metres. Waves of England attacks began to crash on the Tongan defence, but Tonga stood firm and benefited from a moment of fortune as Haumole Olakau'atu pounced after his sketchy first grubber kick was kicked on behind the England line. And with England wobbling, Tonga landed a one-two punch when Tolutau Koula drove over the line. Young went over in the corner to give England false hope, but in front of their delirious fans Tonga scored their fourth try as Katoa's grubber kick exploited defensive gaps for Olakau'atu to touch down. In the day's other men's game - also in Group B-C - co-hosts Papua New Guinea defeated Lebanon 42-18.

item.title: Folorunsho Alakija Conferred With Honorary Doctorate By UK’s Buckingham University
item.description: Prominent businesswoman, philanthropist and Christian minister, Apostle Folorunso Alakija, has been conferred with an honorary doctorate by the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom. The honour was presented at a ceremony on Friday, in recognition of her achievements in business and contributions to society. Businesswoman, philanthropist and Christian minister, Apostle Folorunso Alakija, was conferred with an honorary doctorate by the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom on Friday, October 16, 2026. Alakija’s career spans banking, fashion, oil and gas, real estate and philanthropy, establishing her as one of Africa’s most prominent business figures. Beyond her commercial interests, she has supported charitable initiatives focused on education, women’s empowerment and vulnerable communities. Alakija and others at the honorary doctorate conferment by the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom on Friday, October 16, 2026. The ceremony brought together university officials and guests to celebrate her achievements and contributions to enterprise and philanthropy. The post Folorunsho Alakija Conferred With Honorary Doctorate By UK’s Buckingham University appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Mike Evans’ Friday Absence Signals Real Risk For 49ers Offense
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Mike Evans missed his second straight practice on Friday while dealing with ribs and Achilles soreness. Harrison Rich of The San Francisco Chronicle reported he is listed as a non-participant. The 33-year-old star is now questionable for Monday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. His absence creates a massive void in the passing game right when the team needs him most. The 49ers simply cannot afford to lose their best pass-catcher to the Injured Reserve list this year. Evans has not played all week, but the team is holding him back to avoid a longer absence. If he returns to the field on Saturday, his chances of playing on Monday improve significantly. This is a classic case of managing a veteran’s body to keep him on the field for the big game. The Injury Math Does Not Look Good Evans is fighting two different injuries at the same time. He has been battling a painful rib injury and is now dealing with soreness in his Achilles. These are two of the worst spots for a wide receiver to get hurt. Ribs make it hard to catch and block. Achilles issues destroy speed and cutting ability. The combination makes it very hard to trust he can go full speed on Monday. According to reports, the 49ers are trying to balance his health with the need to win. The team knows that missing practice is not ideal, but they are prioritizing his long-term availability. So far this season, Evans has captured 24 of his 34 targets, totaling 326 yards and three touchdowns. Those numbers show he is still a dominant force even while hurt. Losing those production numbers for even one game would hurt the offense badly. Deebo Samuel’s Absence Makes It Worse The timing of this injury is terrible because Deebo Samuel Sr. is also out. Samuel is expected to miss time due to a hamstring injury he suffered during the Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. This leaves the 49ers with a very thin group of healthy receivers. With Samuel out, Evans will see an even higher target share if active. The defense will focus entirely on him if he plays, or on the backup options if he does not. According to RotoBaller NFL , Evans remains a must-start WR2 in fantasy football despite these nagging injuries. His ability to produce while hurt shows his toughness. But toughness has limits. This season, the 49ers cannot afford for their best pass-catcher to join the list of wideouts on Injured Reserve. Consequently, he has not been practicing much during the week. The risk of playing too soon is too high. What Saturday Practice Means The final practice session of the week on Saturday will tell us everything. A return to practice on Saturday could give Evans a good chance of playing in Week 6. This is the key moment for fans and fantasy managers to watch. The team needs to see him move without pain before they clear him for the game. The 49ers are in a tough spot with their roster depth and injury list. item.title: Top 5 African countries with the most visa-free travel if you own their passport
item.description: African passports differ significantly in the number of destinations their holders can visit without obtaining a visa before departure, with Seychelles, Mauritius and South Africa leading the continent in international travel access. The Henley Passport Index, which uses data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA), ranks passports according to the number of destinations their holders can access without a prior visa. Its 2026 rankings place Seychelles among Africa’s strongest passports, followed by Mauritius and South Africa. Based on the 2026 rankings and available passport-mobility data, here are five African countries whose passports offer extensive international travel access. Seychelles Seychelles has one of Africa’s most powerful passports, giving its citizens broad access to destinations across the world without securing a visa in advance. The island nation retained its position as Africa’s leading passport in the 2026 Henley Passport Index, ranking among the top 25 passports globally in the July update. According to the Seychelles News Agency, the passport provided visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 155 destinations at that time. Its international mobility gives Seychellois citizens greater flexibility when planning holidays, business trips and other short-term journeys abroad. The country’s position reflects the benefits of its international relations and the travel arrangements it has established with other countries. Mauritius Mauritius ranks among Africa’s strongest passports, offering its citizens extensive travel opportunities across several regions. The country has consistently placed near the top of continental passport rankings, with access to numerous destinations in Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and other parts of the world. Mauritian citizens benefit from visa-free arrangements and visa-on-arrival facilities in a range of countries, making international travel more convenient for tourism and business. Its strong passport position also reflects Mauritius’s international engagement and the agreements that facilitate movement between its citizens and other countries. South Africa South Africa ranks third among Africa’s strongest passports in the 2026 rankings, providing its citizens with substantial international travel access. South African passport holders can visit a range of destinations without obtaining a visa beforehand, although entry conditions differ by country. The passport is particularly useful for regional travel within Africa, while also providing access to destinations in parts of Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean. Despite its relatively strong position on the continent, South African citizens still require visas for several major destinations, depending on the purpose and length of their visit. Its international mobility gives Seychellois citizens greater flexibility when planning holidays, business trips and other short-term journeys abroad. The country’s position reflects the benefits of its international relations and the travel arrangements it has established with other countries. Mauritius Mauritius ranks among Africa’s strongest passports, offering its citizens extensive travel opportunities across several regions. The country has consistently placed near the top of continental passport rankings, with access to numerous destinations in Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and other parts of the world. Mauritian citizens benefit from visa-free arrangements and visa-on-arrival facilities in a range of countries, making international travel more convenient for tourism and business. Its strong passport position also reflects Mauritius’s international engagement and the agreements that facilitate movement between its citizens and other countries. South Africa South Africa ranks third among Africa’s strongest passports in the 2026 rankings, providing its citizens with substantial international travel access. South African passport holders can visit a range of destinations without obtaining a visa beforehand, although entry conditions differ by country. The passport is particularly useful for regional travel within Africa, while also providing access to destinations in parts of Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean. Despite its relatively strong position on the continent, South African citizens still require visas for several major destinations, depending on the purpose and length of their visit. Botswana Botswana is among the African countries whose passports offer comparatively broad international travel access. Its passport provides entry to a range of countries without a prior visa, including destinations within Africa and selected countries beyond the continent. For Botswana citizens, these arrangements can reduce the paperwork and planning required for international holidays, visits and some business trips. Namibia Namibia rounds out the five African countries with strong passport mobility in several 2026 rankings. Namibian passport holders enjoy visa-free access to a number of destinations, alongside access to other countries through visa-on-arrival arrangements. The passport offers opportunities for regional travel in southern Africa and entry to selected destinations elsewhere in the world. Although Namibia does not provide the same level of access as Seychelles or Mauritius, it remains among the African countries whose citizens enjoy comparatively broad international mobility. item.title: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes already hang by a thread after brutal Tonga defeat
item.description: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes are hanging by a thread after a crushing 30-12 defeat by Tonga in their opening match of the competition in Perth. Brian McDermott’s men were undone by the brilliance of Dolphins half-back Isaiya Katoa who masterminded his side’s stunning win and contributed a crucial 14 points with the boot. It means England realistically now need Tonga to beat Samoa in a fortnight’s time to stand the slimmest chance of progressing to the semi-final stage. England failed to capitalise on some serious first-half momentum and the Tongans exposed their weaknesses after the break to gain emphatic revenge for their trio of test defeats in the UK in 2023. England’s flat pack were comprehensively out-muscled and full-back AJ Brimson – preferred to St Helens number one Jack Welsby – was turned inside out by Katoa, who will team up with England captain George Williams at his NRL club next season. For McDermott it was a massive wake-up call and he must now rebuild his shattered side for upcoming group games against Papua New Guinea and France, both of which are already in danger of being rendered irrelevant in the complicated cross-group system. England piled on the pressure for much of a high-octane first half but they failed to find a way through an heroic Tongan rearguard and it was the South Sea islanders who reached the interval 10-0 in front. Kai Pearce Paul was denied an early opener by a superb saving tackle from Latu Fainu, and Brimson was hauled back by Lehi Hopoate, and Tonga suffered a major blow when playmaker Fainu was forced off injured. But after soaking up half an hour of pressure, Tonga pounced when Katoa’s inch-perfect offload sent Stefano Utoikamanu galloping over for their opener. Tonga would stretch their lead into double figures through two kicks from Katoa, but McDermott’s men looked to have forced their way right back into the contest when Hugo Savala sent Brimson over within six minutes of the restart. Savala’s subsequent kick took England within four and they looked to have all the momentum until a needless penalty sent Tonga back up the other end of the field and they seized on a slice of fortune when Katoa’s kick ricocheted through and Haumole Olakau’atu touched down. It got much worse for England as a clever kick through by former Huddersfield man Tui Lolohea sent Tolutau Koula over for his side’s third. Katoa’s sixth successful kick stretched Tonga’s lead to 18 as the game edged beyond the hour mark. Dom Young gave England hope when he raced over on 63 minutes, but it was to prove a fleeting moment of hope as another Katoa kick sent Olakau’atu sent over for his second, and Tonga cruised through the final minutes to wrap up a richly deserved win. More follows

item.title: Celtics' Unusual Win Over 76ers Leaves Joe Mazzulla With Intriguing Decisions
item.description: Celtics' Unusual Win Over 76ers Leaves Joe Mazzulla With Intriguing Decisions originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics probably could not have designed a more unusual way to finish their preseason. Facing a Philadelphia 76ers team featuring Joel Embiid, LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey and former Celtics star Jaylen Brown, Boston decided to give its regular contributors the night off. Instead of using a conventional starting lineup, the Celtics opened with Chris Cenac Jr., Milos Uzan, Hayden Gray, Tucker DeVries and Gabe McGlothan. The result was a 125-120 overtime victory that gave Boston a perfect 4-0 preseason record. That final score is entertaining enough. But what happened during the game might be even more interesting for Joe Mazzulla and the Celtics' coaching staff. Boston's reserves did not simply survive against a more recognizable Philadelphia lineup. They found a way to win after falling behind late. For a team preparing to open the regular season, that is a pretty encouraging problem to have. MORE : Celtics Overcome Massive Depth Disadvantage to Beat 76ers in Preseason Finale Celtics Reserves Refuse To Follow The Script The 76ers had the recognizable names and the established star power. Boston had players competing for opportunities, developmental minutes and potentially roster positions. On paper, that looked like a difficult matchup for the Celtics. 4-0 preseason ✅ https://t.co/o0equnOnrl — Boston Celtics (@celtics) October 17, 2026 Philadelphia built a 10-point advantage in the fourth quarter, putting Boston in a position where a preseason loss would hardly have been surprising. Instead, the Celtics fought back and forced overtime before completing the victory. Hugo Gonzalez led Boston with 21 points, continuing to demonstrate why his development is worth watching. Tucker DeVries, Ron Harper Jr. and Dillon Mitchell also provided important contributions as the Celtics worked their way back into the game. The performance did not guarantee anybody additional regular-season minutes. Preseason basketball does not work that way. However, the effort gave Boston's coaching staff another opportunity to evaluate players in situations that cannot be completely replicated during practice. Late-game possessions, defensive assignments and decision-making under pressure all provide useful information. The Celtics received plenty of it Friday. However, the effort gave Boston's coaching staff another opportunity to evaluate players in situations that cannot be completely replicated during practice. Late-game possessions, defensive assignments and decision-making under pressure all provide useful information. The Celtics received plenty of it Friday. More Celtics Latest Celtics news TD Garden fan guide: What to know before you go Complete history of Celtics championships Sam Cassell Gets An Interesting Assignment Another unusual aspect of the evening involved the coaching staff. Mazzulla handed the sideline responsibilities to assistant coach Sam Cassell, continuing Boston's approach of allowing assistants to gain valuable experience during preseason games. Cassell was tasked with managing a lineup that looked considerably different from the one Boston expects to use during the regular season. That created opportunities for evaluation beyond the players themselves. Coaches must determine which combinations work together, which players understand defensive responsibilities and who can execute when the game becomes competitive. Friday offered an opportunity to make those assessments without the pressure of regular-season standings. Cassell's group responded with a victory. The result also reflected something that has become an important part of Boston's preseason identity: defensive activity and a willingness to compete regardless of the personnel on the floor. Those qualities will matter when the Celtics begin playing games that count. MORE: Celtics’ Joe Mazzulla Snubbed in GM Survey Despite Reigning COTY Status Boston's Real Decisions Begin Now The Celtics open their regular season Tuesday, October 20, against the Detroit Pistons. At that point, the focus will shift from experimentation to winning games. Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and Boston's other established contributors will command significant minutes. Opportunities for players farther down the roster will become more limited. That is why Friday's performance was meaningful. The coaching staff received another look at several players who may not have many chances to demonstrate their value once the regular season begins. Gonzalez's scoring performance was encouraging. The contributions from Boston's younger players were also worth noting. But the most impressive aspect of the victory might have been the collective response. The Celtics could have accepted a preseason loss against a Philadelphia team featuring several accomplished veterans. Instead, they continued competing and found a way to win. An undefeated preseason does not guarantee anything once the regular season begins. Boston knows that. What it does provide is evidence that the team's younger players are willing to compete, even when the matchup looks unfavorable. That should make the final roster evaluations considerably more interesting. And for Mazzulla, having too many players eager to prove they belong is a problem most coaches would gladly accept. item.title: Lions fans’ confidence on the rise; anticipate immediate impact from Brian Branch
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 4: Brian Branch #32 of the Detroit Lions stretches prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 04, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , and asked Detroit Lions fans two questions : Which Lions player returning from injury will have the biggest immediate impact? (weekly question) Are you confident the Lions are headed in the right direction? (recurring poll) Our weekly confidence polls have been a roller coaster ride throughout 2026. After entering the season on a high note, things dipped after they needed overtime to beat the Saints in Week 1, then fell below 50% for the first time in the Dan Campbell era after a bad Week 2 loss in Buffalo. After a Week 3 win over the Jets, confidence rebounded to nearly 80%, only to plummet to 12% the following week after a loss in Carolina. Now, after their third victory of the season, this time over the Cardinals, fans’ confidence in the team has rebounded again, though not quite to where it was before. Let’s take a look at the results of this week’s polls: As for our second question, there was a clear winner, as anticipated, but we wanted to give readers a chance to also comment and share their view on the potential impact of two key players returning from injury. But before we get to that, let’s take a look at the results from this survey: Let’s take a closer look at the comment section of our original article and The Feed post to see fans’ explanations for why they voted the way they did (lightly edited for clarity). Most approved/interacted with “right direction” comments: No Username : “Since a “yes” answer implies full confidence, I’ll stay with “no” until I see some consistency in the defense, and steady performance against better teams.“ Matt48912 : “I answered “no” because I am not confident right now, but I still think they might be. I need more than 3 quarters against a team struggling more than them on defense before I think they are getting back to where they were 2 years ago.” icd8u2 : “Once we acquire another good CB, then I will be fairly confident we are headed in the right direction. No matter what you think of Arnold, losing your first-round CB pick for nothing in return really hurt our CB room.” rbelieve : “I hope they’re headed in the right direction. But I am not “confident”. critical perspective : “I keep reminding myself that there isn’t a team out there who is firing on all cylinders in every aspect of their roster. […] The Lions have an elite offense and a much improved defensive front. The LBs and, to a great extent, defensive backs have struggled, and there just may not be a fix at corner for this season. But overall, there is so much talent on this team that you’d hope they can plug some holes and keep it rolling to at least be in the conversation come January

Most approved/interacted with “right direction” comments: No Username : “Since a “yes” answer implies full confidence, I’ll stay with “no” until I see some consistency in the defense, and steady performance against better teams.“ Matt48912 : “I answered “no” because I am not confident right now, but I still think they might be. I need more than 3 quarters against a team struggling more than them on defense before I think they are getting back to where they were 2 years ago.” icd8u2 : “Once we acquire another good CB, then I will be fairly confident we are headed in the right direction. But overall, there is so much talent on this team that you’d hope they can plug some holes and keep it rolling to at least be in the conversation come January.” Most approved/interacted with “Immediate impact returning player” comments: Izzo for POTUS : “Mays might play great, but he won’t be that much better than Scruggs. The offensive line is playing well without Mays, but the defense needs playmakers familiar with the scheme.” Newton82 : “I think the latest midweek mailbag addresses this question really well…Mays will probably do wonders, especially for the run game, but Branch, in theory, will allow the defensive backfield to do things they just can’t right now. item.title: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A former spokesperson to ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande has dismissed claims by Babachir Lawal that former President Muhammadu Buhari considered Osinbajo’s 2023 presidential ambition “highly immoral and distasteful”. Akande, who served as Osinbajo’s spokesperson from 2015 to 2023, described the allegation as false in a statement on Saturday, saying Buhari had personally offered to support the former vice-president’s ambition on at least four occasions. Osinbajo contested the All Progressives Congress presidential primary in 2022 but lost to Bola Tinubu, who went on to win the 2023 presidential election. Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, ADC, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, had alleged in a recent interview that Buhari would have found it difficult to support Osinbajo’s ambition because of his longstanding relationship with Tinubu, a former Lagos State governor. Reacting, Akande said he had watched the interview in which Lawal made allegations against Osinbajo and chose to respond because he was present when decisions concerning the former vice-president’s office were taken. He said Buhari had, on at least four separate occasions, personally offered to support Osinbajo, asking him, “If I don’t support you, who will I support?” “He was consistent. During the APC presidential primaries in 2022, while campaigns were underway, President Buhari openly commended Vice President Osinbajo at a Federal Executive Council meeting for the dignified, issues-based manner in which he was conducting his campaign across the country. He spoke in a laudatory tone. The entire Council witnessed it.” “That is not a President who found Osinbajo’s ambition distasteful. That is a President who broached it, encouraged and applauded it,” Akande added. Osinbajo contested the APC presidential primary in June 2022, finishing third with 235 votes, behind now president Bola Tinubu, who won with 1,271 votes, and Rotimi Amaechi, who scored 316. The post Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ex-Dolphins Pro Bowl guard shares honest Malik Willis assessment amid 0-5 start
item.description: The Dolphins entered their bye week 0-5 while carrying an NFL-record $182.29 million in dead cap, 60.5% of their total cap. Releasing Tua Tagovailoa accounts for $99.2 million of it, with Tyreek Hill’s release and the Jaylen Waddle trade to Denver adding most of the rest. Several early 2027 mock drafts already have Miami using the first overall pick on a quarterback to eventually replace Malik Willis. Willis signed a three-year, $67.5 million deal with $45 million guaranteed this offseason. Richie Incognito, the former Dolphins guard who now co-hosts the Initial Contact podcast with former NFL tight end Christian Fauria, weighed in on that plan in an interview with Covers.com. Dec 27, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Malik Willis (2) warms up prior to the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images “I think they got to get the rest of the team right. You’ve got to get a real serious offensive line. You’ve got to get some receivers on the edge that will threaten a defense or make things easier for a quarterback. They need so many more upgrades. So just throwing a quarterback into the mix, I don’t think it fixes their problem.” Incognito told Covers.com . Willis has completed 56.2% of his passes for 849 yards and two touchdowns, all of which rank last among starting quarterbacks , with four interceptions. His top pass catchers are Malik Washington and first-year players Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and De’Von Achane is out for the year with a torn ACL. The numbers belong to Willis, but the names around him explain a good share of them. “It’s tough to really pass judgment on Malik Willis because it’s up and down. I think the rest of the roster is really, really bad. They’re paying $180 million to guys that are no longer there. Overall, they’re just not a very good football team. There’s a lot of holes in the roster. Maybe they make a change at quarterback. It doesn’t matter.” Incognito said. Head coach Jeff Hafley has stuck with Willis through all five losses. “We’ve played five games and Malik is our quarterback. We need to be better. Malik needs to be better, OK? And that’s not the headline.” Hafley said Monday. Can the Dolphins avoid a winless season? Miami’s last two losses came by five points at Minnesota and seven at home against Cincinnati. The Dolphins return Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET at the 2-3 Jets, the first of two meetings with New York. The Chargers, also 0-5, visit Hard Rock Stadium on Dec. 27. Those three games come against opponents with a combined 2-8 record. Green Bay Packers quarterback Malik Willis (2) throws during the third quarter of their game against the Baltimore Ravens Saturday, December 27, 2025 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. “I could see them getting a win somewhere along the way. item.title: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Militao, Guler, Valverde ahead of Real Madrid vs Sevilla
item.description: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Militao, Guler, Valverde ahead of Real Madrid vs Sevilla Real Madrid once again had to fight against all odds to get a win when they travelled to the Italian capital to face AS Roma in their second UEFA Champions League game of the season. After going down 3-1 at one point in game, the Merengues fought their way back to a 3-4 win in the final few minutes of the match. This win would have significantly boosted the team’s morale, and there is plenty of reason for Los Blancos’ fans to hope that their performance in that game will help the team turn around their form. However, they face another difficult test, this time in La Liga, as they will host Sevilla on Sunday. As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed his customary press conference ahead of this league match. The Portuguese coach admitted that some of his players are tired, but assured that they will be ready for the upcoming game: “We are tired, but not tomorrow. From what I’ve seen in the medical department, the players who played the most minutes are tired. Tomorrow is another day. We have good options at home to make some changes and bring in fresh legs. Sevilla are doing well, and they have been competitive in the matches they have lost. Luis García is doing a great job. They survived last season. We want to win.” The midfield been one of the main areas of problem for Real Madrid, and the coach was asked about his plans for this position: “I ask midfielders to be midfielders. I expect them to do the work a midfielder is supposed to do. Someone who only defends is limited. If they only attack, they would be better off playing out wide or as a No. 10. It is a very difficult position to play. To be a top player, you need a different level of quality.” Mourinho was highly criticial of Javier Tebas after his recent comments comparing Real Madrid TV to Nazi propaganda machines: “You’ve already seen what I think. He has ventured into an area where the only excuse would be a clinical condition. Madrid fans understand what Real Madrid are up against. Even considering the enormous prestige Spanish football enjoys abroad, the World Cup and the most prestigious club in the world, it is better that he keeps those comments to himself.” While praising Arda Guler, the Merengue coach did not reveal what position he is planning to play him in: “There is work being done. You find it difficult to give credit for the work. It seems that the more negative things have someone to blame, while the positive things are attributed to failure or luck. Arda is a very talented player; we know that. Obviously, he is not yet a finished product because he is 21. He has the attributes to play in several roles.
