item.content:encoded: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Militao, Guler, Valverde ahead of Real Madrid vs Sevilla Real Madrid once again had to fight against all odds to get a win when they travelled to the Italian capital to face AS Roma in their second UEFA Champions League game of the season. After going down 3-1 at one point in game, the Merengues fought their way back to a 3-4 win in the final few minutes of the match. This win would have significantly boosted the team’s morale, and there is plenty of reason for Los Blancos’ fans to hope that their performance in that game will help the team turn around their form. However, they face another difficult test, this time in La Liga, as they will host Sevilla on Sunday. As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed his customary press conference ahead of this league match. The Portuguese coach admitted that some of his players are tired, but assured that they will be ready for the upcoming game: “We are tired, but not tomorrow. From what I’ve seen in the medical department, the players who played the most minutes are tired. Tomorrow is another day. We have good options at home to make some changes and bring in fresh legs. Sevilla are doing well, and they have been competitive in the matches they have lost. Luis García is doing a great job. They survived last season. We want to win.” The midfield been one of the main areas of problem for Real Madrid, and the coach was asked about his plans for this position: “I ask midfielders to be midfielders. I expect them to do the work a midfielder is supposed to do. Someone who only defends is limited. If they only attack, they would be better off playing out wide or as a No. 10. It is a very difficult position to play. To be a top player, you need a different level of quality.” Mourinho was highly criticial of Javier Tebas after his recent comments comparing Real Madrid TV to Nazi propaganda machines: “You’ve already seen what I think. He has ventured into an area where the only excuse would be a clinical condition. Madrid fans understand what Real Madrid are up against. Even considering the enormous prestige Spanish football enjoys abroad, the World Cup and the most prestigious club in the world, it is better that he keeps those comments to himself.” While praising Arda Guler, the Merengue coach did not reveal what position he is planning to play him in: “There is work being done. You find it difficult to give credit for the work. It seems that the more negative things have someone to blame, while the positive things are attributed to failure or luck. Arda is a very talented player; we know that. Obviously, he is not yet a finished product because he is 21. He has the attributes to play in several roles. I’m very happy with him.” The Portuguese tactician talked at some length about Vinicius Junior: “Let me ask you a question. Are your followers interested in what time we arrive at Valdebebas? Are people interested in that? And what about when we leave? It’s funny.” “Vinícius had a very difficult match. Gasperini was primarily responsible for that because he attacked us down just one flank, with three men against Cucurella and him. It is difficult to make changes as a manager when some of the information doesn’t come through properly. What annoyed me was the nature of the second goal, which came at a time when the match had settled down and was balanced. We knew how they pressed man-to-man, and Vini needed to protect the ball or win a foul in that situation. But that’s that. Nothing happened. I made five substitutions; it’s part of football. The intensity is extremely high, and it is difficult to play at 200 kilometres per hour for 90 minutes. “Vini’s future lies in working harder than those who get to play every match. Without making any promises, I think he will start on Wednesday in the Champions League. As for the four-match suspension, I’m happy because I thought he would receive a longer ban. I thought those hidden agendas would get him another one or two matches. We won’t discuss it any further.” Further commenting on the Brazilian forward, Mourinho assured that he is a very good individual to work with: “He is a spectacular young man, and it is very easy to have a good relationship with him. I like him a lot; he is fantastic. He has tremendous strength because he manages to live and survive with a smile on his face. If I were in his position, I probably wouldn’t still be here. This past summer, I would have forced a move to a country or a group of clubs and opponents where I would be respected. Out of love for the club and the city, and because he believes things can improve, he renewed his contract and continues to smile. People can affect him negatively because he is human, but I don’t think anyone will be able to take that joy away from him.” The Real Madrid coach also shared his thoughts on meritocracy in his team and rued that he cannot play all the players: “I think we sometimes struggle to give credit to people who do things well. You hammer them when things go wrong. The credit belongs to the young lad who came on and gave everything. Look at the three goals from corners and how we won those corners. In 10 minutes, we had around seven corners because we were overwhelming them with our football. “There are many players who deserve to play. More than 11 deserve to play — there are 15 or 16. Lunin deserves to play, and I’m not joking. He works every day alongside the best goalkeeper in the world, stays positive, and still doesn’t play. I can’t put both of them on the pitch. It is the same story with outfield players. “We can all agree that the five players who came on and changed the match deserve to play tomorrow. But what about the others? Doesn’t Diomande deserve to play? Doesn’t Cucurella deserve to play? Doesn’t Valverde deserve to play? Doesn’t Mbappé deserve to play? That is what makes a manager’s job difficult. My colleagues who manage teams with fewer resources will say I’m lucky. It is both a blessing and a curse to have journalists like you, who make things more complicated.” The Portuguese coach also shared some good news and assured that he does not want any new players: “Militão will be in the squad tomorrow. The good thing is that I don’t have to name the squad just yet. I’m not asking for signings; I’m happy. The players are improving, especially when we have time and peace. I have to develop them. I’m not in a position to ask for more players. I like having a small squad. For someone to come in, someone would have to leave. If the club’s management considers making a move, we will assess it, but I’m not taking the initiative to ask for players. I’m not asking for one or two signings.” When once again asked about Vinicius, Mourinho refused to reveal what he has told the player: “Those are private conversations. When I arrived, he renewed his contract and signed because he considers Madrid his home. He was excited about continuing to make history and win trophies. He gets along with everyone in the dressing room and brings a lot of joy. I have serious doubts that I would have had the strength to stay here with all the offers he had.” The Real Madrid coach also kept his cards close to his chest when asked about the positions of Guler and Valverde: “I’m here to do what I believe is best for the team. The day will come when polls or artificial intelligence pick the teams and managers are limited to working on the pitch. For now, we are still the ones who select the teams. “I’m not talking about criticism or opinions; I don’t consider those opinions more valuable than the manager’s. A manager who is not open-minded is limited. At the same time, I believe a manager who simply follows polls and opinions is not really a manager. I’m not stubborn. I’m open to the opinions of my staff and to analysis. Can I change my mind? Yes, but I can do so based on my own analysis and work. I always want to improve. A match lasts 90 minutes and has m

item.title: Liverpool made €50m offer to sign Serie A forward
item.description: Liverpool made €50m offer to sign Serie A forward Liverpool Transfer News: Francisco Conceicao Bid Highlights Right-Wing Uncertainty Liverpool’s reported pursuit of Francisco Conceicao has opened up another line of scrutiny around the club’s planning on the right flank. According to TuttoMercato , Liverpool saw a €50m proposal turned down, with Juventus and the player both declining the move. That detail matters. When a club of Liverpool’s scale reaches that level financially and still cannot advance discussions, it tends to suggest interest was not matched by conviction on all sides. In this case, the report points to a deal that never gained the necessary alignment, despite the size of the offer. Francisco Conceicao Interest Underlines Liverpool Recruitment Concerns Conceicao has long been regarded as a technically sharp wide option, capable of carrying the ball and attacking defenders in one-v-one situations. Even so, the wider context is difficult to ignore. Liverpool spent much of the market assessing right-sided attackers and, by the end of it, still had no clear addition in that area. The same broad pattern was seen with other names linked during the window, including Ismaila Sarr, Yankuba Minteh and Ibrahim Mbaye. Yan Diomande was also described as a leading objective earlier in the summer. None of those moves materialised, which leaves the impression of a search that remained active but inconclusive. Photo: IMAGO Right-Wing Replacement Debate Continues The central issue is less about one individual target and more about what the sequence says regarding Liverpool’s market strategy. A reported €50m offer for a player who scored three Serie A goals last season would naturally prompt debate, especially in the context of replacing a major attacking departure. Liverpool’s squad construction has also become part of that discussion. The imbalance referenced by many observers, with several options more comfortable from the left and none regarded as a natural senior answer on the right, has lingered beyond the close of the window. If the Conceicao report is accurate, it reinforces the sense that Liverpool were willing to move decisively for a solution, but without landing one. That leaves the club facing familiar questions about recruitment clarity, role definition and whether the right-wing position was addressed with enough certainty when it mattered most. Our View From a Liverpool perspective, this is one of those reports that feels plausible enough to be uncomfortable. If the club really did put €50m on the table for Conceicao, then it suggests there was genuine anxiety late in the process. That does not automatically mean he is a poor player, far from it, but it does hint at a market where Liverpool were reacting rather than dictating. The biggest concern is the profile of the search. Supporters can accept missing out on elite targets because that happens to every club. What becomes harder to accept is a window where several names emerge, non

Francisco Conceicao Interest Underlines Liverpool Recruitment Concerns Conceicao has long been regarded as a technically sharp wide option, capable of carrying the ball and attacking defenders in one-v-one situations. Even so, the wider context is difficult to ignore. Liverpool spent much of the market assessing right-sided attackers and, by the end of it, still had no clear addition in that area. The same broad pattern was seen with other names linked during the window, including Ismaila Sarr, Yankuba Minteh and Ibrahim Mbaye. Yan Diomande was also described as a leading objective earlier in the summer. None of those moves materialised, which leaves the impression of a search that remained active but inconclusive. Photo: IMAGO Right-Wing Replacement Debate Continues The central issue is less about one individual target and more about what the sequence says regarding Liverpool’s market strategy. A reported €50m offer for a player who scored three Serie A goals last season would naturally prompt debate, especially in the context of replacing a major attacking departure. Liverpool’s squad construction has also become part of that discussion. The imbalance referenced by many observers, with several options more comfortable from the left and none regarded as a natural senior answer on the right, has lingered beyond the close of the window. If the Conceicao report is accurate, it reinforces the sense that Liverpool were willing to move decisively for a solution, but without landing one. That leaves the club facing familiar questions about recruitment clarity, role definition and whether the right-wing position was addressed with enough certainty when it mattered most. Our View From a Liverpool perspective, this is one of those reports that feels plausible enough to be uncomfortable. If the club really did put €50m on the table for Conceicao, then it suggests there was genuine anxiety late in the process. That does not automatically mean he is a poor player, far from it, but it does hint at a market where Liverpool were reacting rather than dictating. The biggest concern is the profile of the search. Supporters can accept missing out on elite targets because that happens to every club. What becomes harder to accept is a window where several names emerge, none arrives, and the underlying need still exists. That creates doubt over whether the recruitment team were fully aligned on the level required. There is also a broader issue around messaging. Liverpool are expected to plan ahead, especially in key attacking positions. If there was no settled right-wing solution ready to go, then fans are entitled to wonder why such an important area appeared to be left so open. At the same time, there is a case for caution before going too far. Plenty of reported bids look different once the full picture emerges. Yet if this account is close to the mark, supporters will see it as another sign that Liverpool entered a crucial market need without enough certainty, and paid the price for it.

item.title: Amorim to skip pre-match press conferences for Milan games against Atalanta and Udinese
item.description: Amorim to skip pre-match press conferences for Milan games against Atalanta and Udinese Ruben Amorim will not hold his usual pre-match press conference ahead of Milan’s Serie A clash with Atalanta at San Siro on Sunday. He will skip next Saturday’s briefing before the trip to Udinese too. According to MilanNews24 , there is nothing unusual behind the decision. The arrangement was planned well in advance with the club and is purely down to Milan’s packed schedule across Serie A and the Europa League. REGGIO NELL’EMILIA, ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Ruben Amorim Head Coach of AC Milan looks on during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and AC Milan at Mapei Stadium – Citta’ del Tricolore on October 11, 2026 in Reggio nell’Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Milan boss Amorim prioritises Milanello work amid Europa League schedule Amorim already faced the media on Thursday night in Salzburg, after Milan’s Europa League fixture . The same will happen next week, when he speaks in Bournemouth following the third round of the league phase against the Cherries on 22 October. With those European commitments falling so close to the domestic fixtures, the Portuguese coach has chosen to use the extra time on the training pitch at Milanello rather than in front of the cameras. ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Ruben Amorim, Manager of AC Milan, looks on before the Serie A match between AC Milan and US Lecce at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 20, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Amorim, who is usually expansive on tactics and wider talking points in his pre-match briefings, will still speak to the media after both games, against Sarri’s Atalanta and in Udine.

item.title: What does a Tri-series mean in cricket? Format, rules, points system and how it works
item.description: What does a Tri-series mean in cricket? Format, rules, points system and how it works originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: A tri-series is a short event where three teams play each other and the top two reach the final. Points are usually two for a win and one for a tie or no result, and net run rate often separates teams that finish level. Afghanistan , Bangladesh and Zimbabwe begin a tri-series in the UAE on October 17, and Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka begin one in Pakistan on October 18. What is a tri-series in cricket? A tri-series is an international cricket series played among three teams. It is neither a two-team affair like the bilateral series nor a big tournament like the World Cup. It sits between the two. Three teams play each other in one short tournament, and the top two meet in a final to decide the winner. Tri-series are almost always played in either the ODI or T20I format. They are also called tri-nation or triangular series. Boards use them to give teams extra matches before major tournaments. The format has a long history. Australia held a tri-series every summer from 1979-80, and other countries have used the idea too. This month, two ODI tri-series begin in Asia, one in the UAE and one in Pakistan. Both finish before the end of October. MORE: GOAT in ODI cricket: Ranking the 10 greatest One Day International cricketers ever Tri-series: Rules, format and points system A tri-series has two stages. In the league stage, each team plays the other two. Some series play each pair once, while others play each pair twice. The top two teams after the league stage meet in the final, and the third team is out. Finals are usually a single match. Australia's old tri-series often used a best-of-three final instead, where the first side to win two matches took the trophy. A few years even used a best-of-five final. The rules can change from series to series. Points are simple in most series. In the 2014 Zimbabwe tri-series, a win earned two points, a tie or no result earned one point, and a loss earned none. Some series also add bonus points, so the exact rules can differ. MORE: Who will win the trophy if the series decider is washed out by rain? Points system in a tri-series Result Points Win 2 Tie 1 No result 1 Loss 0 Net run rate, or NRR, is used when teams are level. item.content:encoded: What does a Tri-series mean in cricket? Format, rules, points system and how it works originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: A tri-series is a short event where three teams play each other and the top two reach the final. Points are usually two for a win and one for a tie or no result, and net run rate often separates teams that finish level. Afghanistan , Bangladesh and Zimbabwe begin a tri-series in the UAE on October 17, and Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka begin one in Pakistan on October 18. What is a tri-series in cricket? A tri-series is an international cricket series played among three teams. It is neither a two-team affair like the bilateral series nor a big tournament like the World Cup. It sits between the two. Three teams play each other in one short tournament, and the top two meet in a final to decide the winner. Tri-series are almost always played in either the ODI or T20I format. They are also called tri-nation or triangular series. Boards use them to give teams extra matches before major tournaments. The format has a long history. Australia held a tri-series every summer from 1979-80, and other countries have used the idea too. This month, two ODI tri-series begin in Asia, one in the UAE and one in Pakistan. Both finish before the end of October. MORE: GOAT in ODI cricket: Ranking the 10 greatest One Day International cricketers ever Tri-series: Rules, format and points system A tri-series has two stages. In the league stage, each team plays the other two. Some series play each pair once, while others play each pair twice. The top two teams after the league stage meet in the final, and the third team is out. Finals are usually a single match. Australia's old tri-series often used a best-of-three final instead, where the first side to win two matches took the trophy. A few years even used a best-of-five final. The rules can change from series to series. Points are simple in most series. In the 2014 Zimbabwe tri-series, a win earned two points, a tie or no result earned one point, and a loss earned none. Some series also add bonus points, so the exact rules can differ. MORE: Who will win the trophy if the series decider is washed out by rain? Points system in a tri-series Result Points Win 2 Tie 1 No result 1 Loss 0 Net run rate, or NRR, is used when teams are level. It is the runs a team scores per over, minus the runs it concedes per over, across the whole league stage. A team that is bowled out is treated as having faced its full quota of overs. What happens if teams finish level on points? If two teams are level, the series rules decide who goes through. In most cases, the first check is the number of wins. Next comes the wins against the other tied team, then bonus points, and finally NRR. A three-way tie is harder. Say each team wins two matches and loses two in a six-match series. All three finish on four points with the same number of wins, so NRR decides. The table below is only an example, and the team with the lowest NRR goes out. Example of a three-way tie on points Team Played Won Lost Points NRR Outcome Team A 4 2 2 4 +0.40 Reaches the final Team B 4 2 2 4 +0.15 Reaches the final Team C 4 2 2 4 -0.55 Out A washed-out match gives each team one point and no win. That can change a close race for second place. Some series also have rules for the final. A tied final can go to a Super Over, and the trophy can be shared if rain stops play. What if every league match is washed out? Each washed-out match gives both teams one point. If every league match in a tri-series is washed out, all three teams finish on the same points with no wins. NRR also stays at zero because matches with no result are left out of the calculation. The rules of past tri-series do not solve this. The 2014 Zimbabwe series went from wins to bonus points to NRR. The 2018 Trans-Tasman T20 series went from NRR to fours to sixes. With no balls bowled, all of those are zero, so the organisers could turn to ICC team rankings to decide the top two. MORE: Prediction: South Africa vs. Australia 2nd Test lineups and pitch report Famous tri-series in cricket history Tri-series have given cricket some of its best-known matches and rule changes. Some are remembered for one innings, others for a controversy or a famous chase. Here are seven that people still talk about, from Australia in 1979-80 to Pakistan in 2025. 1979-80 Benson & Hedges World Series Cup (Australia) – England beat the West Indies by two runs after captain Mike Brearley sent all his fielders to the boundary for the last ball. Fielding restrictions came in the next season. 1980-81 Benson & Hedges World Series Cup (Australia) - Trevor Chappell bowled the last ball underarm against New Zealand at the MCG on February 1, 1981, to stop a six that would have tied the game. The ICC banned underarm bowling afterwards. 1983-84 Benson & Hedges World Series Cup (Australia) - The second final between Australia and West Indies at the MCG ended level on 222 each, the first tied ODI. West Indies won the series. 1998 Coca-Cola Cup (Sharjah) - Sachin Tendulkar's Desert Storm 143 against Australia took India into the final, where he made 134 on his birthday and India won. 2002 NatWest Series (England) - India chased 326 against England in the final at Lord's, with Yuvraj Singh and Mohammad Kaif adding 121. Sourav Ganguly waved his shirt from the balcony after the win. 2007-08 Commonwealth Bank Series (Australia) - India beat Australia 2-0 in the best-of-three finals, with Tendulkar making 117 not out in the first at Sydney. It was India's only title in the Australian tri-series. 2025 Pakistan Tri-Nation Series - Pakistan chased 353 against South Africa, their highest successful ODI chase, with hundreds from Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha. New Zealand won the title by beating Pakistan in the final. Upcoming tri-series in 2026 Tri-series Teams Dates Afghanistan ODI tri-series (UAE) Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe October 17 to 23, 2026 Pakistan ODI tri-series (Pakistan) Pakistan, England, Sri Lanka October 18 to 31, 2026 To keep up to date with all the latest cricket news and share your opinion on the biggest topics, visit our Facebook , Instagram and X (Twitter) pages.

item.title: Broncos K Wil Lutz clarifies ‘shush’ celebration with message to Denver fans
item.description: Wil Lutz ended Thursday night’s game against the Seattle Seahawks with a 53-yard field goal in overtime, giving the Denver Broncos a 17-14 win at Empower Field at Mile High. His celebration drew nearly as much attention as the kick, because Lutz turned toward the home crowd with a gesture that looked like a shush. Denver led 14-3 entering the fourth quarter before Seattle tied it on Jason Myers’ 34-yard field goal with seven seconds left in regulation. Sam Darnold then threw an interception to Ja’Quan McMillian on the first possession of overtime, and the Broncos took over at Seattle’s 43-yard line before Lutz finished it. Jan 25, 2026; Denver, CO, USA; Denver Broncos place kicker Wil Lutz (3) prepares to kick a field goal against the New England Patriots during the first half in the 2026 AFC Championship Game at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images NFL aggregator Dov Kleiman claimed Lutz was facing “severe backlash” from Broncos fans, and plenty of fans answered that post by defending the kicker. Lutz went to X early Saturday to settle it himself. 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚: Broncos kicker Wil Lutz is facing severe backlash from Denver fans after he did the shush celebration at home after his game-winning kick. We have never seen anything like this. https://t.co/ikBNchCErk — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) October 16, 2026 To clarify any misunderstanding….We have the best fans and home field advantage in the NFL ,I’ll continue to voice that my entire time as a Bronco. The critics and all the noise we as a team, and personally, face can cause the emotion to come out sometimes. It’s such a cool moment to be able to hit big kick in that setting for this team, in front of our fans…it’s what we live for. I love the support of our fans and the standard you all hold us to, it’s why we want to win for this city and fan base! We all play with a chip on our shoulder, and I hope that makes everyone proud! Onward and upward! — Wil Lutz (@wil_lutz5) October 17, 2026 “To clarify any misunderstanding… We have the best fans and home field advantage in the NFL, I’ll continue to voice that my entire time as a Bronco. The critics and all the noise we as a team, and personally, face can cause the emotion to come out sometimes. It’s such a cool moment to be able to hit big kick in that setting for this team, in front of our fans… it’s what we live for. I love the support of our fans and the standard you all hold us to, it’s why we want to win for this city and fan base! We all play with a chip on our shoulder, and I hope that makes everyone proud! Onward and upward!” Lutz wrote. Why Lutz had critics to answer before Thursday’s kick Lutz entered Thursday having missed a field goal in each of Denver’s previous three games: a 43-yarder against the Rams, a 58-yarder against the 49ers and a 42-yarder in the fourth quarter of the Week 5 win over the Chargers. That left him 8 of 11 on the season, after he made more than 80% of his kicks last year. Nov 10, 2024

Nov 10, 2024; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Denver Broncos place kicker Wil Lutz (3) attempts a field goal with one second back that is blocked by Kansas City Chiefs defensive end Mike Danna (51) (not pictured) during the second half at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. We show up every day, we work, we try to figure out what’s going on, and at the end of the day it’s one kick at a time.” Lutz said. The 53-yarder was the 22nd game-winning kick of his career , the most in the league since he entered it as an undrafted free agent in 2016. “It’s hard to really explain the emotional side of it, the good and the bad. Like I said, I think anybody in my position, anybody on this team, lives for those moments. Glad we were able to put it through.” Lutz said. The make moved him to 9 of 12 this season. Denver, now 4-2, visits the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25, and the Broncos return home Nov. 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs. item.description: Tennessee vs. Alabama radio coverage: Station, channel, streaming to listen live to college football game broadcast originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's the third Saturday in October, which means it's time for Tennessee vs. Alabama. The 14th-ranked Vols host the No. 6 Crimson Tide on Saturday in a key matchup for each team's College Football Playoff resume. Each has one blemish on its record in the form of a 20-17 home loss to one of the top two teams in the country at the time of the game — Tennessee falling to then-No. 1 Texas three weeks ago and Alabama to No. 2 Georgia last weekend. There's no shame in either of those defeats against elite opposition, but this is a critical bounceback opportunity for both. It should be a good one in Knoxville. Here's how to follow all the action live if you aren't able to watch. item.title: Bruins' Comeback Win Creates Fascinating Question Before Kings Game
item.description: Bruins' Comeback Win Creates Fascinating Question Before Kings Game originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins could have walked away from Anaheim with plenty of excuses Friday night. They were playing on the road, surrendered two goals late in the opening period, and needed a comeback against a Ducks team that had seized the early momentum. Instead, the Bruins produced another victory, defeating Anaheim 4-2 and extending their winning streak to four games. David Pastrnak reached another impressive career milestone. Frederic Brunet scored his first NHL goal. Elias Lindholm delivered the winner, and Matthew Poitras provided insurance. But perhaps the most interesting part of the evening was what happened in Boston's net. Michael DiPietro earned his first NHL victory with 25 saves, giving the Bruins another encouraging development as they prepare for Saturday night's matchup against the Los Angeles Kings. Michael DiPietro Gives Bruins Something To Think About DiPietro was not handed an easy assignment. Anaheim generated opportunities early, and the Bruins allowed two goals in the final minute of the opening period. Suddenly, Boston needed its goaltender to prevent the game from getting away while the offense searched for answers. #NHLBruins WIN!!!! https://t.co/jZHrRmsEtd — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 17, 2026 DiPietro did exactly that. He stopped the Ducks from adding to their lead and gave Boston enough time to work its way back into the contest. The performance was not necessarily a statement that the Bruins should change their goaltending hierarchy. Jeremy Swayman remains an important part of the team's plans. However, DiPietro demonstrated something valuable. Boston can receive a competitive performance from another goaltender when circumstances require it. That matters during a long NHL season, particularly when a team is navigating consecutive games and extensive travel. A goaltender's first NHL victory is a personal milestone. For the organization, it can also provide an encouraging indication of its available depth. Young Bruins Continue Making An Impression Boston's comeback was not simply the result of its established stars taking over. Brunet scored his first NHL goal during the second period, cutting Anaheim's lead to 2-1 and giving the Bruins an important lift. James Hagens assisted on the goal and later helped set up Poitras' insurance tally. Those contributions are significant because the Bruins are trying to establish a winning identity while integrating younger players into meaningful situations. Veterans such as Pastrnak and Lindholm will continue carrying major responsibilities. That is expected. The more interesting question is whether Boston's younger contributors can consistently make a difference when games become uncomfortable. Friday provided an encouraging example. Brunet delivered a goal when the Bruins needed a response. Hagens contributed to multiple scoring

Anaheim generated opportunities early, and the Bruins allowed two goals in the final minute of the opening period. Suddenly, Boston needed its goaltender to prevent the game from getting away while the offense searched for answers. #NHLBruins WIN!!!! https://t.co/jZHrRmsEtd — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 17, 2026 DiPietro did exactly that. He stopped the Ducks from adding to their lead and gave Boston enough time to work its way back into the contest. The performance was not necessarily a statement that the Bruins should change their goaltending hierarchy. Jeremy Swayman remains an important part of the team's plans. However, DiPietro demonstrated something valuable. Boston can receive a competitive performance from another goaltender when circumstances require it. That matters during a long NHL season, particularly when a team is navigating consecutive games and extensive travel. A goaltender's first NHL victory is a personal milestone. For the organization, it can also provide an encouraging indication of its available depth. Young Bruins Continue Making An Impression Boston's comeback was not simply the result of its established stars taking over. Brunet scored his first NHL goal during the second period, cutting Anaheim's lead to 2-1 and giving the Bruins an important lift. James Hagens assisted on the goal and later helped set up Poitras' insurance tally. Those contributions are significant because the Bruins are trying to establish a winning identity while integrating younger players into meaningful situations. Veterans such as Pastrnak and Lindholm will continue carrying major responsibilities. That is expected. The more interesting question is whether Boston's younger contributors can consistently make a difference when games become uncomfortable. Friday provided an encouraging example. Brunet delivered a goal when the Bruins needed a response. Hagens contributed to multiple scoring plays. Poitras helped put the game away. That is precisely the type of production that can make a team more difficult to defend over the course of a season. MORE : How to Watch Bruins vs. Kings Tonight: Channel, Live Stream & Start Time for NHL Game Another Challenge Arrives Immediately The Bruins will not have much time to celebrate. Boston faces Los Angeles on Saturday at 9 p.m. ET, completing a back-to-back set in Southern California. That quick turnaround creates decisions involving goaltending, lineup management and energy. It also presents a different kind of test. The Bruins have demonstrated that they can recover from an early deficit. Now they must show they can maintain their intensity with limited recovery time. Friday's victory improved Boston to 6-2-0, an encouraging opening to the season. Four consecutive wins have created momentum, but the schedule will continue testing the team's depth. The power play played a major role against Anaheim, accounting for three of Boston's four goals. The Bruins cannot assume that level of production will arrive every night. They will need contributions at even strength, reliable defensive play and goaltending capable of keeping them competitive. DiPietro provided the latest example of that final ingredient. For a team hoping to build something sustainable, that might be just as important as another spectacular goal from Pastrnak. The Bruins have their stars. Friday suggested they might also have some intriguing answers behind them. More Bruins Latest Bruins news TD Garden fan guide: What to know before you go Complete history of Bruins championships

item.title: Cameroonian journalist shot in Bamenda
item.description: Cameroonian journalist Ambe Macmillan is recovering in hospital after being shot in the legs by gunmen in the north-western city of Bamenda. A young woman was also killed as the attackers opened fire on mourners attending a wake. The shooting has renewed concerns about the dangers facing journalists in Cameroon's English-speaking regions, after years of conflict between government forces and separatist groups.

item.title: Tinubu Builds His Coalition. Can The Opposition Build A Contest?
item.description: There is something revealing about the political events of this week. President Bola Tinubu is assembling a coalition that reaches beyond his party, while his opponents are still discussing how to work together. Both sides are pursuing the same objective: assembling enough political strength to win the 2027 presidential election. But they are approaching it from very different positions. The ruling All Progressives Congress has inaugurated its Presidential Campaign Council, published its campaign timetable and begun assigning responsibilities across the country. Meanwhile, six opposition parties have opened consultations involving Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde, Donald Duke and Adewole Adebayo. On the surface, these are routine election preparations. Look more closely, however, and they reveal the central struggle of the coming election. The APC is trying to turn its incumbency into an overwhelming political advantage. The opposition is trying to prevent its competing ambitions from becoming an overwhelming disadvantage. And somewhere between those two calculations are millions of Nigerian voters who may have a rather different set of priorities. An APC Campaign Council With An Unusual Guest List Wednesday’s inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council was more than a gathering of party faithful. Among those openly supporting Tinubu were Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo and Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke. The significance is difficult to miss. Wike remains a prominent figure associated with the PDP. Soludo leads an APGA administration in Anambra, while Adeleke’s political roots are in the PDP, although he has since moved to Accord. Yet all three have publicly committed themselves to Tinubu’s re-election. This is not necessarily a merger of political parties. Nor does it guarantee that their supporters will follow them into the APC’s electoral column. But it demonstrates how the President intends to fight the election: not simply by relying on the APC’s traditional structures, but by recruiting influential political actors wherever they can be found. item.dc:creator: Alexander Okere
item.content:encoded: There is something revealing about the political events of this week. President Bola Tinubu is assembling a coalition that reaches beyond his party, while his opponents are still discussing how to work together. Both sides are pursuing the same objective: assembling enough political strength to win the 2027 presidential election. But they are approaching it from very different positions. The ruling All Progressives Congress has inaugurated its Presidential Campaign Council, published its campaign timetable and begun assigning responsibilities across the country. Meanwhile, six opposition parties have opened consultations involving Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde, Donald Duke and Adewole Adebayo. On the surface, these are routine election preparations. Look more closely, however, and they reveal the central struggle of the coming election. The APC is trying to turn its incumbency into an overwhelming political advantage. The opposition is trying to prevent its competing ambitions from becoming an overwhelming disadvantage. And somewhere between those two calculations are millions of Nigerian voters who may have a rather different set of priorities. An APC Campaign Council With An Unusual Guest List Wednesday’s inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council was more than a gathering of party faithful. Among those openly supporting Tinubu were Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo and Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke. The significance is difficult to miss. Wike remains a prominent figure associated with the PDP. Soludo leads an APGA administration in Anambra, while Adeleke’s political roots are in the PDP, although he has since moved to Accord. Yet all three have publicly committed themselves to Tinubu’s re-election. This is not necessarily a merger of political parties. Nor does it guarantee that their supporters will follow them into the APC’s electoral column. But it demonstrates how the President intends to fight the election: not simply by relying on the APC’s traditional structures, but by recruiting influential political actors wherever they can be found. There is a familiar Nigerian political calculation at work here. A governor may belong to one party, a minister to another, and their supporters may carry several different membership cards. But when an election approaches, the question increasingly becomes who can deliver votes. That is the strength of Tinubu’s approach. It is also its potential weakness. An alliance assembled around personalities can be formidable on election day. Whether it produces lasting political coherence is another matter. Already, questions are being raised about the propriety of politicians campaigning for a presidential candidate outside their own parties. Atiku’s camp has supported calls for judicial clarification of the position. The dispute could become an early test of party discipline, constitutional rights and the increasingly fluid boundaries of Nigerian party politics. The Opposition’s Crowded Negotiating Table There is movement on the other side, too. The ADC, APM, NDC, SDP, PDP and PRP have reportedly held consultations involving five presidential candidates as they explore cooperation ahead of 2027. That is politically significant. But consultation is not consolidation. The opposition must still answer three difficult questions. Who leads? What does each participant gain? And how will supporters be persuaded to transfer their loyalty to a common electoral project? These are not minor details. They are the difference between a coalition that can compete and a coalition that exists mainly in communiqués. Atiku brings extensive political experience and established networks. Obi retains an identifiable reform-oriented following, particularly among younger and urban voters. Makinde has executive experience and a political base in the South-West. Other candidates bring regional relationships and alternative policy perspectives. Combining these strengths could create a more competitive presidential race. But political support is not automatically transferable. An Obi supporter may not necessarily vote for Atiku. A Makinde supporter may not automatically embrace Obi. And some voters attracted to smaller parties may reject any arrangement that appears to reproduce the political establishment they want to replace. The opposition’s challenge, therefore, is not merely to agree on a candidate. It is to create a proposition that voters find credible. For now, the ruling party has an organisational advantage. Whether that translates into electoral victory will depend on what happens between now and January. The Economy: Better Figures, Difficult Conversations Thursday brought some welcome economic news for the government. Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.63 per cent in September, compared with 15.39 per cent in August. For an administration that has defended difficult economic reforms, the figures offer further evidence that inflationary pressures are easing. But there is a complication. Food inflation remains at 19.59 per cent. And the distinction matters enormously. Economists understand that falling inflation means prices are rising more slowly. But the average family shopping in the market is less interested in the rate of increase than in the amount of money required to feed the household. This is where the government’s economic argument meets its political test. Tinubu can point to improving macroeconomic indicators, stronger growth and the prospect of greater stability. His opponents can point to the accumulated burden of high prices, expensive transportation and declining purchasing power. Both arguments may resonate with different sections of the electorate. The latest disagreement between the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress over when negotiations for a new minimum wage should begin adds another dimension. Labour wants talks to start now. The government considers an immediate review premature. That disagreement could become politically consequential if it develops into industrial action. For the APC, the challenge is to demonstrate that economic recovery is reaching households. For the opposition, the challenge is to move beyond criticism and explain how it would reduce hardship without undermining fiscal stability. Neither task is straightforward. Security: A Campaign Cannot Outrun Events While politicians prepare their rallies, the security situation is providing a sobering reminder that elections do not take place in isolation. Reports of an attack on a military base in Mairari, Borno State, with significant casualties among soldiers and civilian security volunteers, have again raised questions about the resilience of security operations in the North-East. The reported casualty figures have not been independently confirmed by the military. On Thursday, Tinubu directed security agencies to intensify operations against terrorists and kidnappers, while preparing a secure environment for the 2027 elections. There is also the continuing anguish surrounding the October 5 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash. Reuters reported today that families of some of the 25 people who died are still seeking clear information about the investigation, recovery efforts and support for relatives. These developments raise an uncomfortable political question. How effectively can a government campaign on security improvements when serious incidents continue to expose operational weaknesses? The opposition will undoubtedly make security part of its case against the administration. But it, too, must explain what it would do differently, how it would fund those changes, and how quickly Nigerians could reasonably expect results. Security should not become another contest in political exaggeration. The lives involved are too important. The 2027 Election Watch: Three Battlegrounds Are Emer

item.title: Ladd McConkey Injury Update: Chargers WR’s Week 6 Status Revealed
item.description: Ladd McConkey has battled injuries throughout the 2026 season, but he appears to be ready to go for Week 6. Originally entering the league as a second-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft , the Georgia product took the league by storm and immediately established himself as one of Justin Herbert’s most reliable targets. Starting in 14 games while making 16 appearances, the wideout finished his inaugural campaign with 82 receptions for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns on 112 targets. While he wasn’t quite as effective in Year 2, he remained a key part of the offense. Now entering Week 6, Ladd McConkey has been one of the few consistent weapons in the Los Angeles Chargers offense, and he may finally be able to help the team earn its first win of the season. The third-year wideout does not have an injury designation on the team’s official report , so he should be ready to go for Sunday. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor Ladd McConkey Injury Update: Chargers WR Misses Practice The Last Word It’s hard to overstate just how important Ladd McConkey is for the Chargers to have any shot at pulling an upset against the Kansas City Chiefs. At 0-5, the Chargers playoff hopes are all but over, and they desperately need to defeat their division rival if they want to keep even the slightest chance of playoff hopes alive. It’s hard to call any game a “must-win” this early in the season, but that’s exactly what Week 6 is for the Los Angeles Chargers. At 0-5, the team is already 4.5 games behind the Kansas City Chiefs, and their Wild Card chances are pretty much gone. There is no precedent for an 0-6 team to make the playoffs, and Ladd McConkey is pretty much the only shot this team has of moving the football. Kansas City has one of the league’s best defenses, and the Chargers will need their top receiver to play his best football if they want to come out on top. Main Photo: William Laing – Imagn Images

item.title: Prep talk: Dave Yanai continues to love watching basketball at 83
item.description: Former Fremont High and Cal State Dominguez basketball coach Dave Yanai is 83. (Eric Sondheimer / Los Angeles Times) The Southern California college basketball kickoff luncheon was held on Wednesday at the Downtown Athletic Club, and sitting at one of the tables dressed in suit and tie was someone as knowledgeable as any coach in the room. Former Fremont High, Cal State Dominguez Hills and Cal State Los Angeles coach Dave Yanai, 83, was there. He won the John R. Wooden Award’s Legends of Coaching honor in 2021. He was inducted into the City Section Hall of Fame in 2023. Asked if he’s still watching basketball, Yanai said, “A lot.” He was the first Japanese American to be a head coach in college basketball. His nephew is Harvey Kitani, a future City Section Hall of Fame basketball coach who was at Fairfax and now Rolling Hills Prep. Yanai still has much to offer. You just have to ask. This is a daily look at the positive happenings in high school sports. To submit any news, please email eric.sondheimer@latimes.com. Sign up for the L.A. Times SoCal high school sports newsletter to get scores, stories and a behind-the-scenes look at what makes prep sports so popular. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

item.title: Former Barcelona director backs Deco’s work but warns of Real Betis’ star-studded squad: ‘A team to beat right now’
item.description: Former Barcelona director backs Deco’s work but warns of Real Betis’ star-studded squad: ‘A team to beat right now’ Former Barcelona sporting director Ramon Planes believes Hansi Flick’s side are currently the team to beat in Spanish football, but has warned that Real Betis possess the quality and confidence to make their meeting with the Catalans a compelling contest. Planes has a personal connection with both clubs, having worked at Barcelona before later taking Ez Abde to Betis. That experience gives his assessment of the upcoming encounter added significance, particularly with Manuel Pellegrini’s side enjoying an impressive spell and Barcelona looking to maintain their winning momentum. Speaking ahead of the meeting, Planes praised Betis’ development while reflecting on the time he spent at Barcelona and the progress both clubs have made. “They are two clubs that I really have a lot of esteem for. My time at Barça is something I’m proud of. “Today Betis is at its best, one of the best in its history and I think it comes from the idea of Angel Haro and Jose Miguel Lopez Catalan, at the time, to build a modern Betis,” said Planes. Planes identifies Betis as a serious Barcelona threat Planes believes Barcelona enter the fixture in stronger form, but insisted that Betis have the players and tactical confidence to challenge the reigning champions. The Andalusian club has developed into a team capable of competing with Spain’s leading sides, making this encounter a significant test for Flick. Ramon Planes has praised Deco’s work at Barcelona. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) “If anyone can give them a run for their money, it’s the current Betis side; they’re in excellent form and brimming with confidence. “They’re consistently putting in top-class performances; they proved that last season against the big teams. “They’ve got a ‘star-studded’ squad, full of top-quality players, and I think it’s going to be a cracking match because both teams pack a real punch.” Planes praises Deco’s Barcelona rebuild Planes also praised Barcelona’s recent performances and the work of current sporting director Deco. In particular, he pointed to the comeback against Galatasaray in Istanbul as evidence of the team’s confidence and ability to respond under pressure. “It’s clear that Barça are in good form. They proved it in the match against Galatasaray – such a difficult ground, and with the score at 1–0 down – the second half, when they came back with absolute confidence, was key. Planes has warned Barcelona about Real Betis’ level. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) “I think Barça’s transfer business has been very good and Deco is doing a fantastic job. He’s injected a lot of dynamism into the team and strengthened the squad. “That makes them the team to beat right now,” added Planes. Barcelona face a crucial test before El Clasico With El Clasico approaching the following week, Barcelona sit at the top of the table, five points ahead of Betis and six clear

item.title: ‘So rare’: Riley Gaines heaps huge praise on Sophie Cunningham for not issuing a ‘groveling apology’
item.description: Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images Former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines has nothing but praise for Sophie Cunningham. Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham is back in the news for another controversy during the offseason following an early playoff exit. This time, Cunningham had a short yet powerful message for the girls of Washington High School. The girls reportedly refused to play against a boy who was pretending to be a girl. Cunningham praised the girls, and her ‘good work’ message had former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines applauding the Fever guard’s actions. Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images Riley Gaines commends Sophie Cunningham for standing her ground Over the past few months, Cunningham has been called out by several fans and analysts over her rigid stance on keeping biological men and boys out of women and girls’ sports. This dedication to her stance had Gaines impressed, as she had a solid message for the Fever guard’s ‘moral conviction.’ “Most people with large platforms cave and issue a groveling apology the minute they get a little pushback. Not Sophie Cunningham. Good for her. This type of moral conviction is so rare,” Gaines wrote on X . Even though Cunningham’s stance has led to many wanting the Fever to cut ties with her, she refuses to stand down. More importantly, as Gaines mentioned, Sophie is unapologetic about her actions as she believes in her viewpoint. Read more: Sophie Cunningham begs for ‘respect’ over Atlanta Dream’s WNBA Finals problem ‘One of us’ – Dan Dakich says Donald Trump has joined the Sophie Cunningham fan club ‘You can’t tackle’ – Sophie Cunningham expresses concern about Angel Reese’s physical playing style

item.title: Everton v Chelsea: Premier League – live
item.description: ⚽ Premier League updates from the 12.30pm BST kick-off ⚽ Live scoreboard | Tables | Top scorers | Email Scott Xabi Alonso speaks to TNT Sports. “We needed a win [against Bournemouth] but this was last week … one is not enough … we need to keep going, doing the right things, repeating and always improving game by game … [Reece James’ injury] makes it more limited but we have enough options … Romeo [Lavia] … [Valentin] Barco … they have played and now we have Mo [Caciedo] back and [Jordan Henderson] so we have more options … but for sure it’s a blow … we will need another big one in this stadium against Everton … tough opponent … they are in a good run so we are expecting a tough challenge.” Everton are currently in a good humour as well. Should they win this afternoon – and given how they’ve triumphed in this fixture in six of its last nine stagings, losing just the once, that’s very much a live prospect – they’ll move into fourth spot in the Premier League, for a couple of hours at least. Chelsea can do likewise. Continue reading...

item.title: NFL Trade Pitch Sees Seahawks Acquire Pro Bowl RB to Ignite Offense
item.description: CBS Sports's Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty Veteran running back Tony Pollard could be on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty CBS Sports's Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty The Seattle Seahawks are dealing with a turnover issue on offense. They have committed seven giveaways in their last two games, both of which were losses. But CBS Sports’s Jared Dubin doesn’t like what the Seahawks running game has shown either. For that reason, he proposed Seattle potentially change the Super Bowl race with a trade for Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. “The Seahawks cannot run the ball at all, as we have seen throughout this season and that was on full display on Thursday night against the Broncos,” wrote Dubin. “Pollard is no great shakes, but he’s got 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons and is at least a professional runner who can get what’s blocked and a bit more. “The Seahawks should be getting Zach Charbonnet back fairly soon, but we don’t know if or when Jadarian Price will return. Pollard would be an upgrade over Emanuel Wilson and/or George Holani as a complement to Charbs. It’s not the sexiest deal in the world and might not even be the best possible use of resources, but the Seahawks do need help in the backfield.” Pollard has 273 rushing yards and a touchdown in five games for the Tennessee Titans this season. The veteran made the Pro Bowl with the Dallas Cowboys during his first 1,000-yard season in 2022. Seahawks Urged to Acquire Titans RB Tony Pollard Getty Veteran running back Tony Pollard could be on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. item.content:encoded: CBS Sports's Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty Veteran running back Tony Pollard could be on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty CBS Sports's Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty The Seattle Seahawks are dealing with a turnover issue on offense. They have committed seven giveaways in their last two games, both of which were losses. But CBS Sports’s Jared Dubin doesn’t like what the Seahawks running game has shown either. For that reason, he proposed Seattle potentially change the Super Bowl race with a trade for Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. “The Seahawks cannot run the ball at all, as we have seen throughout this season and that was on full display on Thursday night against the Broncos,” wrote Dubin. “Pollard is no great shakes, but he’s got 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons and is at least a professional runner who can get what’s blocked and a bit more. “The Seahawks should be getting Zach Charbonnet back fairly soon, but we don’t know if or when Jadarian Price will return. Pollard would be an upgrade over Emanuel Wilson and/or George Holani as a complement to Charbs. It’s not the sexiest deal in the world and might not even be the best possible use of resources, but the Seahawks do need help in the backfield.” Pollard has 273 rushing yards and a touchdown in five games for the Tennessee Titans this season. The veteran made the Pro Bowl with the Dallas Cowboys during his first 1,000-yard season in 2022. Seahawks Urged to Acquire Titans RB Tony Pollard Getty Veteran running back Tony Pollard could be on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The Seahawks didn’t do that badly on the ground during Week 6 Seattle gained 113 rushing yards in Thursday’s contest versus the Denver Broncos . That production, though, came from a committee. Emanuel Wilson led the team with 52 rushing yards while George Holani and Velus Jones Jr. each had 20 rushing yards. Holani scored Seattle’s only rushing touchdown. Pollard would provide an upgrade over all three of those running backs. Last season, Pollard gained 1,082 yards on the ground with five touchdowns. It was his fourth straight 1,000-yard season. The running back has also registered at least 1,280 yards from scrimmage for four consecutive campaigns. With Pollard, the Seahawks could get back to their run-first mentality and take pressure away from quarterback Sam Darnold . The signal-caller has taken 10 sacks and thrown four interceptions in the past two losses. Seahawks Running Back Depth After Week 6 Getty CBS Sports’s Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Pollard could be a great upgrade for the Seahawks. But he could also still be an unnecessary addition. Before the regular season started, the hope in Seattle was the Seahawks could pair Zach Charbonnet with first-round rookie Jadarian Price this fall. Charbonnet hasn’t played yet this season while continuing to recovery from his January ACL injury. But head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters this past week the running back “looks tremendous.” Then on Friday, Macdonald described Price’s return to be happening “sooner-rather-than-later.” If those two are paired together on the field before the trade deadline on November 10, there would be little reason for the Seahawks to acquire Pollard. Having said that, Charbonnet is still only nine months removed from a serious knee injury. Price is also a rookie with three games of experience. At the very least, Pollard could provide backfield insurance in Seattle. But he also very well could be the boost the Seahawks offense really needs. item.title: Kwara APC: Oba leads peace committee to reconcile aggrieved members
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin Elder statesman and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ilorin, Prof. Oba AbdulRaheem, OFR, is leading a group of prominent Kwara indigenes to reconcile aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and mobilise support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group, known as the Kwara APC Peace Committee, held its inaugural meeting at AbdulRaheem’s residence in Ilorin on September 17, according to a statement made available to Vanguard by Oloriewe Raheem Adedoyin. The statement said the committee was committed to resolving disagreements arising from the outcome of the APC primaries and promoting unity among party members. AbdulRaheem, a former chairman of the Federal Character Commission, chairs the committee. Other members include Dr Johnson Adewumi, an educationist, entrepreneur and founder of Thomas Adewumi University, Oko; former minister and former Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Issa Bio Ibrahim; and former Secretary to the Kwara State Government and former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. AbdulGaniyu Cook Olododo. The committee also comprises Adedoyin, a veteran journalist and Africa representative on the Executive Board of the International Press Institute; former Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Ezekiel Issa; elder statesman and member of the Tinubu-Shettima Presidential Campaign Council, Pastor John Dara; and former Federal Character Commission member, Hon. James Jiya Kolo. According to the statement, the committee intends to serve as a voice of conscience among APC leaders by addressing internal grievances and promoting the achievements of the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq. It said the group had reached out to some aggrieved political leaders and influential stakeholders to encourage reconciliation and forge a common front ahead of the elections. The committee is also canvassing support for the APC’s governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Yakubu Danladi, and other candidates of the party in the state. The statement said the initiative was aimed at securing the backing of party stakeholders for the candidates and strengthening cohesion within the APC ahead of the general elections. The post Kwara APC: Oba leads peace committee to reconcile aggrieved members appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NFL Network analyst floats surprising theory about Jalen Hurts’ absence from Eagles
item.description: Michael Robinson floated a theory about Jalen Hurts’ absence on NFL Network’s “NFL GameDay Kickoff” on Thursday, the same day the Philadelphia Eagles ruled their quarterback out of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers. Hurts has a superficial blood clot in his calf, and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, speaking on “The Pat McAfee Show,” described his status as out indefinitely. The Eagles are 2-3 after three straight losses, and Tanner McKee is expected to make the start against Carolina. Robinson, the former Seahawks fullback, opened by admitting he had no inside information and framed his argument as playing devil’s advocate. He pointed to the draft picks Philadelphia has collected in recent trades and said the organization appeared to be tying the outcome of this season to Hurts, which in his view would give the team a reason to move on from him later. He also noted that Hurts’ guaranteed money runs out after the 2027 season, even though his extension runs through 2028. Dec 14, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) on the filed after win against the Las Vegas Raiders at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images “If I’m Jalen Hurts, or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp, I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season… he’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” Robinson said. Philadelphia listed 24 players on its Thursday injury report. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with hamstring injuries, and guard Landon Dickerson has been on injured reserve with a knee bone bruise for all but one game this season . Robinson’s point about the injury list checks out against that report, and the motive he attached to Hurts is the part the team’s own account of the past two weeks actually contradicts. “if I’m Jalen Hurts − or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp − I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ “To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season..he’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” https://t.co/nqw8J8emov — Jon Marks (@JonMarksMedia) October 17, 2026 What the Eagles’ timeline shows about Hurts stepping away Hurts was cleated in the Oct. 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and asked for treatment on his calf on Oct. 8, according to the statement the Eagles released on Thursday . A precautionary ultrasound in London found the clot on Oct. 10, before the Jacksonville game. The medical staff and doctors in London cleared him, the league office was kept informed, and Hurts played the entire loss to the Jaguars without limitation. He practiced in full on Wednesday. A follow-up ultrasound later that night showed the small clot had moved, and the team ruled him out on Thursday. “Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course

item.title: Patriots' Biggest Advantage Against Jets Might Not Be What Fans Expect
item.description: Patriots' Biggest Advantage Against Jets Might Not Be What Fans Expect originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots have spent much of the week answering questions about injured players, potential returns and how quickly their offense can get back to full strength. But heading into Sunday's AFC East matchup with the New York Jets, the biggest development might involve a player who will not be on the field. Jets running back Breece Hall has been ruled out of Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium. That creates an interesting opportunity for Mike Vrabel's defense, particularly with New England getting Christian Gonzalez back after the cornerback missed two consecutive games with a shoulder injury. The Patriots are 3-2 and riding a two-game winning streak. The Jets enter at 2-3, with several offensive injuries creating additional challenges for a team trying to establish consistency. For New England, the opportunity is obvious. The Patriots can make life considerably more difficult for the Jets by forcing their offense to operate without one of its most dangerous playmakers. Jets Lose An Important Offensive Weapon Hall's absence removes a player capable of changing a game without needing 20 or 25 touches. His ability to contribute as both a runner and receiver makes him particularly valuable to an offense that needs explosive plays. The Jets will turn to other options in their backfield, including Braelon Allen, who is coming off a strong performance against Cleveland. Allen rushed for a career-high 116 yards in that game, demonstrating that New York still has the personnel to establish a productive ground attack. TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr. are questionable for #NYJvsNE https://t.co/Zl9tJb1R7r — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 16, 2026 That means the Patriots cannot simply assume Hall's absence will eliminate the Jets' running game. However, the change could affect how New York approaches different situations. Hall's versatility presents challenges for linebackers and defensive backs, especially when he gets into space. Without him, the Jets may need to be more deliberate about creating favorable matchups. New York also ruled out wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and offensive lineman Dylan Parham, adding further complications to its offensive preparations. The Patriots should have opportunities to test those adjustments early. Christian Gonzalez Returns At An Important Time New England's secondary has its own injury problems. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III and Karon Prunty have been ruled out, while Channing Canada is questionable with a hamstring injury. Those absences make Gonzalez's return especially important. Gonzalez practiced fully Friday and carries no game-day injury designation. That does not mean the Patriots have suddenly solved every problem in their secondary. It does mean they are getting back one of their most important defensive players at a time when they need stability

The Jets will turn to other options in their backfield, including Braelon Allen, who is coming off a strong performance against Cleveland. Allen rushed for a career-high 116 yards in that game, demonstrating that New York still has the personnel to establish a productive ground attack. TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr. are questionable for #NYJvsNE https://t.co/Zl9tJb1R7r — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 16, 2026 That means the Patriots cannot simply assume Hall's absence will eliminate the Jets' running game. However, the change could affect how New York approaches different situations. Hall's versatility presents challenges for linebackers and defensive backs, especially when he gets into space. Without him, the Jets may need to be more deliberate about creating favorable matchups. New York also ruled out wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and offensive lineman Dylan Parham, adding further complications to its offensive preparations. The Patriots should have opportunities to test those adjustments early. Christian Gonzalez Returns At An Important Time New England's secondary has its own injury problems. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III and Karon Prunty have been ruled out, while Channing Canada is questionable with a hamstring injury. Those absences make Gonzalez's return especially important. Gonzalez practiced fully Friday and carries no game-day injury designation. That does not mean the Patriots have suddenly solved every problem in their secondary. It does mean they are getting back one of their most important defensive players at a time when they need stability. The Jets still have Garrett Wilson, and rookie pass catchers Omar Cooper Jr. and Kenyon Sadiq are working toward returning to the lineup. That combination creates an interesting matchup. New York is missing important offensive pieces but could regain receiving options capable of testing New England's depth. Gonzalez gives the Patriots more flexibility in how they handle those challenges. MORE : 2-Time Super Bowl Champ Says Patriots Are NFL's Best Team Patriots Have A Chance To Control The Game Early The most important part of Sunday's matchup might be what happens before either team scores. If the Patriots consistently stop the run on early downs, they can force New York into longer passing situations. That would create opportunities for New England's pass rush and reduce the Jets' ability to dictate the pace. If Allen establishes himself early, however, the Jets could prevent New England from concentrating on the passing game. The Patriots also have decisions to make on offense. A.J. Brown remains questionable, and the team must decide whether to activate him from injured reserve before Saturday's deadline. But regardless of Brown's availability, New England has an opportunity to put pressure on the Jets by controlling the line of scrimmage. The Patriots do not need a spectacular defensive performance to take advantage of New York's injuries. They need discipline, sound tackling and an ability to prevent the Jets from finding easy yards. Sometimes the biggest advantage in a divisional game is not having the most exciting player on the field. It is making sure the other team cannot use its most exciting player against you. item.title: Cowboys’ Mike Pettine Sheds Light on His New Midseason Role
item.description: New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team's coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Getty New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team's coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Getty The Dallas Cowboys defense doesn’t look much different in 2026 than it did last season when it was one of the worst units in the league. But the Cowboys now hope an addition to the defensive staff could change that. Dallas added veteran NFL coach Mike Pettine to its defensive staff this week. Pettine will hold the title of senior defensive assistant. That’s not a particularly specific title. Pettine provided more details on his exact role to reporters Friday. “Just clearly support, just advise [Christian Parker],” Pettine said. “I think we’ll build a lot of the stuff together. We’ll game plan along with the staff. I just feel like my experience there, having gone against a lot of these opponents over time and kind of built books on most of these offensive coordinators, just feel I’ll be able to help that way. “Game day, I’ll just be up top as another set of eyes for him to bounces things off of, offer suggestions. I think the role will just kind of grow as it goes.” Pettine’s first NFL coaching role was with the Baltimore Ravens nearly 25 years ago. He coached under Rex Ryan for more than a decade, serving as defensive coordinator under Ryan with the New York Jets . Pettine was also Buffalo Bills defensive coordinator under Doug Marrone for a season. From 2014-15, Pettine served as head coach for the Cleveland Browns . “I think I can help a lot,” Pettine said. “It’s funny, I have a big four-inch thick book of what not to do, and a very thin one of what to do. So I think that’s key, is to be able to learn from others mistakes. “As much as you think you’re prepared for it, you’re really not until you get into it. And I think that’s where I’ll be able to help him.” Mike Pettine Speaks out on Cowboys Role Getty New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team’s coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker appears to have a bright future in the league. The team’s brass, including owner Jerry Jones, still has a lot of confidence in Parker, who is in his first season as an NFL defensive coordinator. But Pettine has something Parker doesn’t — experience. A few years after his Browns head coaching tenure ended, he became a defensive coordinator again for three years with the Green Bay Packers . He was also an assistant head coach with the Minnesota Vikings from 2022-25. Pettine has previous experience with the Cowboys defensive coordinator as well. So I think that’s key, is to be able to learn from others mistakes. “As much as you think you’re prepared for it, you’re really not until you get into it. And I think that’s where I’ll be able to help him.” Mike Pettine Speaks out on Cowboys Role Getty New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team’s coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Parker’s first NFL coaching job was under Pettine in 2019 with the Packers. Parker is the reason Pettine accepted the role in Dallas. On Friday, the senior assistant described Parker as a friend in need. That should make things easier for the Cowboys to navigate the potentially complicated matter of an assistant who just arrived with the team calling for changes. “CP knows me well enough that when I say something, some other people might be a bit shocked by it, and he just knows who I am,” Pettine said. “He’ll understand where I’m coming from. I’ll make some suggestions, and when we get behind closed doors, if I need to have some tough conversations, we’ll do it as I’ve always done with him or with other coaches. I don’t see that part of it being an issue.” Pettine suggested the Cowboys defense might need a lot of changes. But he stressed they won’t happen all at once and a majority of them will be minor but crucial changes. “One thing I learned a long time ago is football’s a game of a million little things,” Pettine said. “There’s no one magic play to run, it’s a lot of the detail stuff. Just been taking a lot of notes. It’s not like it’s something that, ‘Hey, we’re going to do these 30 things different today.’ “But it’s things that need to get addressed.” Pettine will coach his first game with the Cowboys in Week 6.
