item.title: “Never just for me”: Dossena carries girls’ dreams at U17 World Cup
item.description: “Never just for me”: Dossena carries girls’ dreams at U17 World Cup Before joining the Brazilian national team for the U-17 Women’s World Cup, goalkeeper Isadora Dassena had already made her mark in football. Finding the back of the net was how she first developed a trademark of her own. First with São Paulo. Then with Ferroviária, where she became the club’s first goalkeeper to score from a free kick in an official competition. Two clubs, two unprecedented achievements, and a trait that helps explain who this young player from Irati, Paraná, is: a willingness to go beyond what is expected of someone in her position. At six, Dossena chose to play in goal in outdoor football. But at nine, she decided to play outfield while remaining a goalkeeper in futsal. It was only at 12 that she committed to playing in goal outdoors, after a coach told her about potential that perhaps even she had not imagined. The decision paid off. At 14, Dossena joined São Paulo. The following year, she moved to Ferroviária, where she won the Brazilian U-17 Championship and continued building a career that now takes her to a new stage: the World Cup. Dossena during a Brazilian U-17 national team training session in Rabat, Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Brazilian National Team Her first call-up to the Brazilian national team late last year was a dream come true. For Dossena, wearing Brazil’s famous yellow shirt means much more than representing a badge. "Being part of everyday life with the national team is an enormous privilege. Both the coaching staff and the players try to keep the atmosphere as relaxed as possible so we can perform at our best," she says. In Morocco, where she is experiencing her first World Cup, the goalkeeper has also discovered football’s reach beyond the pitch. Amid different cultures, languages and customs, she stresses the value of belonging to a group working toward the same goal. "Our national team has a very relaxed atmosphere, while other teams tend to be more reserved. It’s really interesting to experience everything the World Cup has to offer," she says. Isadora Dossena preparing for the U-17 World Cup opener in Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Making history means paving the way While Dossena has already learned to surprise people on the pitch, off it she has discovered that her achievements can reach places in ways only football can inspire. She recently returned to Irati, the city in Paraná where she began playing alongside boys, to visit a girls’ football program. item.content:encoded: “Never just for me”: Dossena carries girls’ dreams at U17 World Cup Before joining the Brazilian national team for the U-17 Women’s World Cup, goalkeeper Isadora Dassena had already made her mark in football. Finding the back of the net was how she first developed a trademark of her own. First with São Paulo. Then with Ferroviária, where she became the club’s first goalkeeper to score from a free kick in an official competition. Two clubs, two unprecedented achievements, and a trait that helps explain who this young player from Irati, Paraná, is: a willingness to go beyond what is expected of someone in her position. At six, Dossena chose to play in goal in outdoor football. But at nine, she decided to play outfield while remaining a goalkeeper in futsal. It was only at 12 that she committed to playing in goal outdoors, after a coach told her about potential that perhaps even she had not imagined. The decision paid off. At 14, Dossena joined São Paulo. The following year, she moved to Ferroviária, where she won the Brazilian U-17 Championship and continued building a career that now takes her to a new stage: the World Cup. Dossena during a Brazilian U-17 national team training session in Rabat, Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Brazilian National Team Her first call-up to the Brazilian national team late last year was a dream come true. For Dossena, wearing Brazil’s famous yellow shirt means much more than representing a badge. "Being part of everyday life with the national team is an enormous privilege. Both the coaching staff and the players try to keep the atmosphere as relaxed as possible so we can perform at our best," she says. In Morocco, where she is experiencing her first World Cup, the goalkeeper has also discovered football’s reach beyond the pitch. Amid different cultures, languages and customs, she stresses the value of belonging to a group working toward the same goal. "Our national team has a very relaxed atmosphere, while other teams tend to be more reserved. It’s really interesting to experience everything the World Cup has to offer," she says. Isadora Dossena preparing for the U-17 World Cup opener in Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Making history means paving the way While Dossena has already learned to surprise people on the pitch, off it she has discovered that her achievements can reach places in ways only football can inspire. She recently returned to Irati, the city in Paraná where she began playing alongside boys, to visit a girls’ football program. Standing before girls who dream of becoming players, she showed them her Brazilian U-17 Championship medal and realized that her own journey is already inspiring others. “I was the only girl who played in my hometown, which is small, with around 60,000 people. I played with the boys. Recently, I went back and was so happy to see that they had set up programs. I visited one of them, and there were lots of girls, all happy. It’s really nice to see younger generations believing it’s possible, especially in a small town that gets little attention," she says. "It warms my heart because we realize that all the effort is paying off both on and off the pitch. Knowing that I’m an inspiration to other people is a huge motivation, because it will never be just about me," she adds. Those words take on even greater meaning when the goalkeeper talks about the national team. Facing Canada in their World Cup opener, Brazil will take on a tough opponent and have the chance to start forging their path in the tournament. Dossena knows they will need to give their all in every respect, but she is confident in the work the group has done. "What motivates us most is knowing that we’ll give everything we have, regardless of the level or who our opponents are. We’ll represent Brazil on the pitch. We don’t just play for those who are here, but also for everyone who was part of our preparations, for the fans, our families and the coaching staff, who can’t be out on the pitch but help us all the time. We’re very focused on this opening match. We’ll give everything we can. We’ll do what’s possible, and what seems impossible too," she says. Brazil’s U-17 women’s national team kicks off its World Cup campaign this Sunday (18) at noon (Brasília time). Brazil faces Canada at the Women’s Football Complex in Salé, Morocco. The Group C opener will be broadcast live on Sportv and streamed on FIFA+ and CAZÉTV. item.title: Ex-Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. Has New Injury With Cowboys
item.description: Former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is back on the injury report ahead of Week 6. Getty Former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is back on the injury report ahead of Week 6. Getty Dallas Cowboys' Stephen Jones addressed new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. ahead of Week 6. Getty There’s a problem when one becomes the boy who cried wolf — no one believes you anymore. That’s an issue former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. seems to be experiencing early in his tenure with the Dallas Cowboys. Porter missed Week 5 with the stomach flu. Now entering Week 6, the Cowboys have Porter listed as questionable because of an ankle injury. The ankle ailment is a new development that some members of the Cowboys organization don’t appear to be acknowledging. But nonetheless, Porter was limited in practice Wednesday and Friday this week. This is notable because of the phantom back injury he had at the end of his Steelers tenure. Porter landed on the PUP list in late July because of his back. Then when the team failed to sign him to a contract extension, Porter continued to miss time because of his back problem. The cornerback sat out three games and was set to miss Week 4 before the Steelers traded him to Dallas. Porter made his Cowboys debut four days after the trade. But he missed the following game and is in danger of sitting out Sunday. Will Joey Porter Jr. Miss Cowboys Matchup vs. Packers? Getty Former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is back on the injury report ahead of Week 6. The Cowboys have made clear that the cornerback isn’t going to get a new contract before the offseason. That was an issue with the Steelers when the team ended negotiations when the regular season began. However, Porter explained to reporters upon arriving in Dallas he didn’t feel valued in Pittsburgh. Since no contract negotiations have taken place in Dallas, it’s unlikely the Cowboys have made him feel disrespected. Put sanother way, it doesn’t make much sense Porter would play four days after getting traded to Dallas and then resume his hold-in. If the contract was an issue, then Porter wouldn’t have played in Week 4 for Dallas. The cornerback only missed Week 5 because he came down with a terrible flu hours before the game. “I really just couldn’t hold anything down,” he told DallasCowboys.com . “You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn’t hold in deep down. “So that’s when they made the call to send me home.” Porter then told DallasCowboys.com’s Patrik Walker that he hoped to not be on a snap count this Sunday. It’s notable, though, that Walker reported Porter returned healthy and practiced Wednesday when he actually was limited. The Cowboys have made clear that the cornerback isn’t going to get a new contract before the offseason. It’s notable, though, that Walker reported Porter returned healthy and practiced Wednesday when he actually was limited. Porter was limited hours prior to Walker publishing his story covering Porter’s sudden Week 5 illness. The cornerback probably deserves the benefit of the doubt. But it’s also understandable if Steelers fans and others don’t want to give it to him. Stephen Jones Speaks out on Porter Getty Dallas Cowboys’ Stephen Jones addressed new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. ahead of Week 6. NFL fans will find out for certain whether Porter is sincere that he wants to move forward with the Cowboys this season on Sunday night. Stephen Jones, though, did his best to squash any concern during his radio appearance Friday. “Oh, absolutely. I think he’s all in,” said Jones, via The Athletic’s Jon Machota . “He wants to be out there; he was sick. He couldn’t play last week with the flu. But he obviously played in our first game, and I think he’s fired up about what he can do to help us win against the Packers . Like Walker, Jones didn’t acknowledge Porter’s new ankle issue. Porter didn’t register a statistic in his Cowboys debut, but he scored strong analytical grades. Porter played 25 defensive snaps versus the Houston Texans . item.title: ‘It’s an Indictment Against You’ — Stephen A. Smith Rips Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer Over Reaction to Player-Only Meeting
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a disappointing loss against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. The team’s defense was seen struggling throughout the game. The organization’s head coach, Brian Schottenheimer, has been facing criticism as he was seen praising the players for holding a players-only meeting to address their defensive struggles. Jun 5, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; Stephen A. Smith looks on before the game between the San Antonio Spurs and the New York Knicks in game two of the 2026 NBA Finals at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Stephen A. Smith Slams Cowboys Coach Over Meeting In a recent episode of ESPN’s “First Take”, ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith shared a very different view of what a players-only meeting tells him and said “It means the coach ain’t reaching you. So when I see a head coach, and he’s applauding the players only meeting, my attitude with him, ‘How are you okay with that?’ If you’re okay with that, you can point to players being accountable, and taking ownership, and all of those cliché kinds of things we may have heard, but ultimately it’s an indictment against you because it’s your job to reach them.” “You ain’t playing. What the hell are you doing?” Smith added. “If they got to reach themselves, if they got to rally amongst themselves, if they’ve got to something or gumption up whatever it is necessary to right the ship that is clearly wrong, then why aren’t you the person facilitating that? If you’re not the person facilitating that, why the hell are you the coach? That’s to me is what the problem was.” The controversy came to light when linebacker DeMarvion Overshown revealed that players had gathered without the coaching staff to discuss their performance and evaluate whether they were meeting the standards expected of the team. The organization’s recent performance has raised questions about the team’s defensive struggles. The franchise was not able to deliver its best performance and was seen struggling throughout the game, thus showing a lack of tackling, consistency, and the ability to limit opponents’ production, despite making personnel changes intended to strengthen the unit. It would be interesting to see whether Brian Schottenheimer will be able to address the team’s defensive struggles and help the organization get back on track. The head coach will need to find ways to improve communication, strengthen the team’s defensive strategy, and ensure that players are held accountable for their performances. The upcoming games will be crucial for the Cowboys as they look to overcome their recent setbacks. Schottenheimer will have to prove that he can lead the team through difficult situations and help the players deliver better performances on the field. It is good to see that the players have owned up to their mistakes and are trying to improve, but that does not mean the coaching staff can overlook the loss. item.title: ‘He’s the Next Man Up’ — Mary Kay Cabot Denies Rumored Shedeur Sanders Trade After Browns QB Hired an Agent
item.description: Cleveland Browns’ backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders has once again caught fans’ attention as the quarterback hired an agent for the first time since joining the league. The step taken by Sanders does not come as a shock, as after losing the QB1 battle to Deshaun Watson ahead of the 2026 season, fans and analysts began speculating about a potential trade to another team. Oct 1, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) and quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) before the game at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Mary Kay Cabot Dismisses Shedeur Sanders Trade Rumors In a recent episode of “92.3 The Fan”, Browns insider Mary Kay Cabot was seen talking about the young quarterback, explaining that the organization views him as an important part of its future, and said: “ Well, I think if you look back to the whole draft process, he did not have an agent. He did not have guidance in a professional manner in terms of being signed with an agency. And some people that I’ve talked to in the league think that hurt him in the process, just in some of his decisions about which visits he wanted to take or how he wanted to approach some of those interviews. And so I think this is just part of the process as you go through your NFL career and you try to navigate your situation. It’s probably a good idea for him to have some type of representation. And I know within the last six months, he’s also hired a marketing agency. “ “So I think he’s just taking charge of his career in ways that he might not have really known as much about when he was just coming out of school. I don’t know if that is the motive here or that is part of the agenda. I don’t have any idea. We haven’t really talked to Shador very much. He’s not in the locker room. And there really, you know, there really isn’t much reason to talk to the backup quarterback at this time of year when he’s not playing. So we haven’t talked to him about this yet. And I don’t know if there’s any type of, like I said, any type of an agenda here. But I know that the Browns don’t want to trade him. He’s next in line. He’s next man up. And they always need at least two quarterbacks a year. So I don’t know that you would want to go and ask for a trade when you’re one play away from getting in the game for the Cleveland Browns.” “I know that the Browns don’t want to trade him. item.title: ‘I Do Believe in Keelon Russell’ — Analyst Shows Faith in Alabama Star QB After Loss Against Georgia
item.description: The Alabama Crimson Tide suffered a disappointing 20-17 loss against Georgia. Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell put in an impressive performance and gave his best despite the setbacks he experienced against Georgia. College football analyst Joel Klatt believes that one difficult performance should not overshadow Russell’s overall potential or the progress he has made during his first season as Alabama’s starting quarterback. July 30, 2025; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Quarterback Keelon Russell throws during the first practice session of the preseason for the Alabama Crimson Tide. Joel Klatt Expresses Thoughts On Keelon Russel; and Alabama In a recent episode of “The Joel Klatt Show”, the analyst shared his views on the young quarterback and said: “I do believe in Keelon Russell, guys. Um, it wasn’t perfect, and there were certainly things that he was going to want back off of last week’s game, but trust me when I tell you this: I watched the entire film. It is very difficult to decipher Georgia’s defense.” “They hold their water, meaning that they disguise. They don’t tell you what you’re in pre-snap. You’ve got to decipher that post-snap. Very difficult for a young quarterback. He made some plays with his legs that are still, like, get-out-of-your-seat-style plays. This guy is a special player, folks. He really is. I like their defense. I thought that they ran it a lot better against Georgia than I anticipated, a lot better than they did a year ago.” Although the organization suffered a defeat, the performance given by the young quarterback will help identify areas for improvement as he continues developing at the college level. The young quarterback accepted his mistakes after the game, as he understood that missed throws had affected Alabama’s offensive execution. The young quarterback has shown remarkable positivity, as it is never easy to acknowledge your weaknesses and embrace them as opportunities for growth. With pressure on the field higher than ever, how a young quarterback responds to setbacks and carries himself through difficult moments can shape how an organization views his development and leadership. Alabama should take time to analyze its performance against Georgia and identify the areas that need improvement. The coaching staff can use the lessons from the Georgia game to help Russell recognize defensive schemes more quickly and make better decisions under pressure. Facing experienced defenses can be challenging for a young quarterback, but these experiences can also accelerate his development. If Russell continues to build confidence, improve his timing with receivers, and learn from his mistakes, he could become a more reliable leader for the Crimson Tide. The quarterback has given the organization a reason to believe in him, as he looks like someone who will continue to improve with time. His talent, determination, and ability to make difficult plays show that he has the potential to become a key player for Alabama. With Pressure

College football analyst Joel Klatt believes that one difficult performance should not overshadow Russell’s overall potential or the progress he has made during his first season as Alabama’s starting quarterback. July 30, 2025; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Quarterback Keelon Russell throws during the first practice session of the preseason for the Alabama Crimson Tide. Joel Klatt Expresses Thoughts On Keelon Russel; and Alabama In a recent episode of “The Joel Klatt Show”, the analyst shared his views on the young quarterback and said: “I do believe in Keelon Russell, guys. Um, it wasn’t perfect, and there were certainly things that he was going to want back off of last week’s game, but trust me when I tell you this: I watched the entire film. It is very difficult to decipher Georgia’s defense.” “They hold their water, meaning that they disguise. They don’t tell you what you’re in pre-snap. You’ve got to decipher that post-snap. Very difficult for a young quarterback. He made some plays with his legs that are still, like, get-out-of-your-seat-style plays. This guy is a special player, folks. He really is. I like their defense. I thought that they ran it a lot better against Georgia than I anticipated, a lot better than they did a year ago.” Although the organization suffered a defeat, the performance given by the young quarterback will help identify areas for improvement as he continues developing at the college level. The young quarterback accepted his mistakes after the game, as he understood that missed throws had affected Alabama’s offensive execution. The young quarterback has shown remarkable positivity, as it is never easy to acknowledge your weaknesses and embrace them as opportunities for growth. With pressure on the field higher than ever, how a young quarterback responds to setbacks and carries himself through difficult moments can shape how an organization views his development and leadership. Alabama should take time to analyze its performance against Georgia and identify the areas that need improvement. The coaching staff can use the lessons from the Georgia game to help Russell recognize defensive schemes more quickly and make better decisions under pressure. Facing experienced defenses can be challenging for a young quarterback, but these experiences can also accelerate his development. If Russell continues to build confidence, improve his timing with receivers, and learn from his mistakes, he could become a more reliable leader for the Crimson Tide. The quarterback has given the organization a reason to believe in him, as he looks like someone who will continue to improve with time. His talent, determination, and ability to make difficult plays show that he has the potential to become a key player for Alabama. With Pressure more than ever on field how you handle abd put yourself out there determines how q organization will eventually deal and treat uoi, it would be interesting to see how future look for keelon. item.title: Max Verstappen unveils special Texas-themed helmet for F1 United States GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has revealed a special helmet for the United States Grand Prix, giving his usual design an Austin, Texas, makeover ahead of the race at the Circuit of the Americas. The Dutchman unveiled the new design on social media. "Texas bound. I’ll be coming to Austin with this special helmet!" he posted alongside detailed photos of the new helmet. The main change is to the lion on the top of the helmet, which now wears a cowboy hat. The lion stands out in blue on a white background and the red, white and blue theme has been retained throughout the whole helmet. At the time of writing, Verstappen's post had already received more than 747,000 likes. "10s across the board - the lion with the cowboy hat is incredible," one fan commented, while another added: "The lion in the cowboy hat is brilliant haha." Further reactions included: "Oh this is gorgeous", and "Simply lovely that helmet." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Max Verstappen (@maxverstappen1) To complement the new helmet, Verstappen and his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar will also be wearing special all-white, vintage-style race suits. The new designs have sparked hope among fans that the Milton Keynes outfit could introduce an all-white livery for the race in Austin, but this is yet to be confirmed. Read Also: Red Bull reveals striking white F1 race suits for US GP as fans call for matching livery Verstappen heads to Austin after back-to-back wins at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and the Singapore Grand Prix. He currently sits fourth in the drivers' standings with 221 points, 119 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli. But while most drivers have a weekend off from racing after an intense triple-header, Verstappen is racing in the GT World Challenge Europe finale at Portimao this weekend in the Verstappen Racing #3 Mercedes-AMG with Chris Lulham and Ben Barnicoat. The United States Grand Prix takes place at the Circuit of the Americas from 23-25 October and kicks off the next triple-header in the championship, with the Mexican and Brazilian Grands Prix in the two weeks following. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed
item.description: Jeremiyah Love has battled an ankle injury throughout the season, and the ailment will keep the running back sidelined for Week 6. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it’s easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson and Detroit’s Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 6, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB OUT For Week 6 While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn’t lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven’t done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn’t looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will get the start. The former Atlanta Falcon has had similar struggles behind Arizona’s offensive line, recording just 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 attempts throughout the young season. Main Photo: David Brytus – Imagn Images

item.title: Zelensky says Trump waiving sanctions ‘rewards’ Putin, warns Moscow wants ‘blackout’ in Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday that US President Donald Trump’s decision to block Russia sanctions only “rewards” Russia’s Vladimir Putin and warned Moscow was trying to deprive “millions” of Ukrainians of heat and electricity before winter. Amid a clash with the Ukrainian wartime leader, Trump signed an executive order that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia’s energy revenues. The decision came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine — especially its capital, Kyiv – in the fifth year of its offensive, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions. The Lindsey Graham Act — named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill — targeted Russia’s energy and defence sectors, as well as Putin and the so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers used by Moscow to circumvent Western sanctions. Zelensky said the decision came the same day as Russia attacked 15 critical power generation facilities across Ukraine in “one of the largest” attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid. “It is important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening,” he said on social media. The Lindsey Graham Act, he said, was “supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end” adding that the act “could have helped enormously — and still can!”. “A U.S. sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin — all of this only encourages him to keep attacking,” he warned. The Ukrainian leader said Russia wanted to cause a “blackout” in Ukraine ahead of winter: “Russia is trying to leave millions of our people without electricity and heating.” He called on allies to keep up pressure on Moscow to “stop this.” Last winter saw hundreds of thousands in Ukraine consistently without heat and electricity in freezing temperatures. A day after Trump waived the sanctions, causing Europe and Kyiv to worry which side of the war the White House is on, Ukraine said at least two people were killed in Russian air strikes. Officials said one person was killed in the southern city of Kherson in an attack that also wounded 22 people, including two children, and that another was killed in the northeastern city of Sumy. – Russia hails Trump move as ‘historic’ – The Kremlin and Putin have not yet reacted to Trump, but several Russian officials celebrated the move as a win. “The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment,” Kirill Dmitriev, a Putin envoy, said on social media. Dmitriev said the act would have caused “serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets”. Trump’s waiver comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease existing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets. item.content:encoded: Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday that US President Donald Trump’s decision to block Russia sanctions only “rewards” Russia’s Vladimir Putin and warned Moscow was trying to deprive “millions” of Ukrainians of heat and electricity before winter. Amid a clash with the Ukrainian wartime leader, Trump signed an executive order that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia’s energy revenues. The decision came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine — especially its capital, Kyiv – in the fifth year of its offensive, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions. The Lindsey Graham Act — named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill — targeted Russia’s energy and defence sectors, as well as Putin and the so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers used by Moscow to circumvent Western sanctions. Zelensky said the decision came the same day as Russia attacked 15 critical power generation facilities across Ukraine in “one of the largest” attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid. “It is important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening,” he said on social media. The Lindsey Graham Act, he said, was “supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end” adding that the act “could have helped enormously — and still can!”. “A U.S. sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin — all of this only encourages him to keep attacking,” he warned. The Ukrainian leader said Russia wanted to cause a “blackout” in Ukraine ahead of winter: “Russia is trying to leave millions of our people without electricity and heating.” He called on allies to keep up pressure on Moscow to “stop this.” Last winter saw hundreds of thousands in Ukraine consistently without heat and electricity in freezing temperatures. A day after Trump waived the sanctions, causing Europe and Kyiv to worry which side of the war the White House is on, Ukraine said at least two people were killed in Russian air strikes. Officials said one person was killed in the southern city of Kherson in an attack that also wounded 22 people, including two children, and that another was killed in the northeastern city of Sumy. – Russia hails Trump move as ‘historic’ – The Kremlin and Putin have not yet reacted to Trump, but several Russian officials celebrated the move as a win. “The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment,” Kirill Dmitriev, a Putin envoy, said on social media. Dmitriev said the act would have caused “serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets”. Trump’s waiver comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease existing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets. He announced the executive order Friday, shortly after Putin appeared in military uniform and said Moscow aims to capture the rest of east Ukraine. US-led talks to end the war in Ukraine have not led to a breakthrough. Both Putin and Zelensky have frustrated Trump in the past with a lack of progress in halting the grinding war. Zelensky had rallied his allies Friday on a visit to Brussels for a European Union summit, urging them to keep financing Ukraine’s fight and insisting he was standing up for his country amid the row with Trump. – Putin vows more – Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defences ahead of winter. Russia controls large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine and Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine by force. “On the whole I see a positive trend in the operations of the troop groupings,” Putin told army leaders Friday, dressed in military attire. “Undoubtedly, one of the main objectives remains the liberation of the Donetsk People’s Republic,” he added, using the Kremlin’s name for the eastern Donetsk region. European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky Friday as he grappled with Trump. “This is no time to withdraw the support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions,” said European Council chief Antonio Costa. “Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure.” The post Zelensky says Trump waiving sanctions ‘rewards’ Putin, warns Moscow wants ‘blackout’ in Ukraine appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gervon Dexter Found His Fit in Atlanta. Did the Bears Miss the Signs?
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Gervon Dexter Sr. #95 of the Atlanta Falcons tackles Justice Hill #43 of the Baltimore Ravens in the second quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears are about to face a player who might make them question what they missed in him. Gervon Dexter Sr. was a second-round pick, a starting defensive tackle and a productive member of Chicago’s defensive line. Then, on August 30, the Bears traded him to Atlanta for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick. One month later, the Falcons handed Dexter a four-year contract extension worth $78 million, including $46.5 million guaranteed. Now, as the Bears prepare for Sunday’s matchup, Dexter arrives with something more interesting than a revenge narrative: evidence that a change of scenery can transform a player’s value. Atlanta didn’t just acquire Dexter. It appears to have unlocked him. What Changed for Gervon Dexter in Atlanta’s Defense? The numbers are difficult to ignore. Through five games of the 2026 season, Pro Football Focus has Dexter graded fourth among 133 interior defensive linemen, with 18 quarterback pressures and an 81.9 overall grade as of October 15. His pass-rush grade ranked seventh. Those are impressive results for a player who had barely been in Atlanta long enough to unpack. There is a tactical explanation worth exploring. Under defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, Atlanta has generated pressure without routinely sending extra defenders. Through its first three games, the Falcons recorded a 41.6% quarterback pressure rate while blitzing fewer than 20% of the time. Dexter produced 15 pressures during that opening stretch alone. That matters because pressure isn’t just about sacks. An interior defender who collapses the pocket can disrupt a quarterback’s timing, force hurried decisions and create opportunities for teammates. Dexter has the size and power to make life uncomfortable for offensive linemen, and Atlanta’s aggressive four-man rush appears to be giving him room to attack. Chicago’s Dennis Allen had a different defensive system, but it would be unfair to conclude that Allen simply didn’t know how to use him. Dexter was already a starter in Chicago, starting all 32 games across the 2024 and 2025 seasons and finishing second on the team in sacks in both years. The more revealing possibility is that Atlanta found a way to maximize qualities the Bears already knew he possessed. Sometimes it’s not simply about a player’s talent. It’s about the situation that makes better use of it. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons s
item.content:encoded: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Gervon Dexter Sr. #95 of the Atlanta Falcons tackles Justice Hill #43 of the Baltimore Ravens in the second quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears are about to face a player who might make them question what they missed in him. Gervon Dexter Sr. was a second-round pick, a starting defensive tackle and a productive member of Chicago’s defensive line. Then, on August 30, the Bears traded him to Atlanta for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick. One month later, the Falcons handed Dexter a four-year contract extension worth $78 million, including $46.5 million guaranteed. Now, as the Bears prepare for Sunday’s matchup, Dexter arrives with something more interesting than a revenge narrative: evidence that a change of scenery can transform a player’s value. Atlanta didn’t just acquire Dexter. It appears to have unlocked him. What Changed for Gervon Dexter in Atlanta’s Defense? The numbers are difficult to ignore. Through five games of the 2026 season, Pro Football Focus has Dexter graded fourth among 133 interior defensive linemen, with 18 quarterback pressures and an 81.9 overall grade as of October 15. His pass-rush grade ranked seventh. Those are impressive results for a player who had barely been in Atlanta long enough to unpack. There is a tactical explanation worth exploring. Under defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, Atlanta has generated pressure without routinely sending extra defenders. Through its first three games, the Falcons recorded a 41.6% quarterback pressure rate while blitzing fewer than 20% of the time. Dexter produced 15 pressures during that opening stretch alone. That matters because pressure isn’t just about sacks. An interior defender who collapses the pocket can disrupt a quarterback’s timing, force hurried decisions and create opportunities for teammates. Dexter has the size and power to make life uncomfortable for offensive linemen, and Atlanta’s aggressive four-man rush appears to be giving him room to attack. Chicago’s Dennis Allen had a different defensive system, but it would be unfair to conclude that Allen simply didn’t know how to use him. Dexter was already a starter in Chicago, starting all 32 games across the 2024 and 2025 seasons and finishing second on the team in sacks in both years. The more revealing possibility is that Atlanta found a way to maximize qualities the Bears already knew he possessed. Sometimes it’s not simply about a player’s talent. It’s about the situation that makes better use of it. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) The Ian Cunningham Connection Makes This More Than a Fresh Start The man who brought Dexter to Atlanta knew him before the trade ever happened. Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham was Chicago’s assistant general manager when the Bears selected Dexter 53rd overall in 2023. He had a firsthand look at the defensive tackle’s development, his strengths and the limitations that may have influenced Chicago’s roster decisions. That background makes the speed of Atlanta’s commitment particularly striking. The Falcons didn’t wait half a season to decide whether Dexter was worth keeping. After three games, they were prepared to invest $78 million in his future. Cunningham praised Dexter’s power and disruptive ability when announcing the extension, describing him as a young, ascending talent. The commitment also suggests Atlanta believes his early production is sustainable, rather than a brief hot streak. Bears coach Ben Johnson has offered a more diplomatic assessment. As reported by Sports Illustrated , Johnson called Dexter a “phenomenal football player” and described the trade as a win-win, pointing to the fresh start and a defensive scheme that matches his skill set. That’s an important distinction. Chicago had reasons to make the move, including its plans for the defensive-line rotation and its desire to add depth in the secondary. The Bears weren’t necessarily declaring Dexter a bad player. They were deciding he wasn’t the right fit for their plans. Still, there is a difference between believing a player can succeed elsewhere and watching another organization immediately commit major money to him. Atlanta’s decision raises a legitimate question about whether Chicago fully appreciated Dexter’s abilities. Will Sunday’s Game Could Expose the Cost Dexter now gets to test his former team on the field. For Chicago’s offensive line, the challenge is straightforward: contain an interior defender who has become one of the league’s more productive early-season pass rushers. Dexter knows the Bears’ personnel, while Chicago knows his tendencies. Neither side will have the luxury of treating this as an ordinary matchup. The Bears also have their own defensive concerns, including Montez Sweat’s two-game suspension and Dayo Odeyingbo’s injury. But Dexter’s departure is a separate issue, and the value of the trade won’t be decided by one afternoon in Atlanta. The Bears received Phillips and a future draft pick. The Falcons received a starting-caliber defensive tackle and quickly secured his future. Both sides may ultimately benefit, but the early returns are undeniably favorable to Atlanta. Dexter doesn’t need to celebrate a sack or deliver a pointed message to his former team to make a statement. If he continues to disrupt Chicago’s offense, the performance will speak for itself. The bigger lesson for the Bears may be uncomfortable: sometimes a team correctly identifies a player’s talent but fails to find the best way to use it. Atlanta appears to have found that way with Dexter. Sunday’s game won’t settle the argument, but it could offer Chicago a glimpse of what it gave up. item.title: Fake Linda and me: the Agatha Christie-worthy mystery of the fraudster who stole my byline
item.description: How a string of bizarre events led writer Linda Geddes to don her sleuthing cap and dig into a world of shadowy impersonators It started with an entirely ordinary interaction on LinkedIn. Someone had tagged me in a post, saying how much they’d enjoyed contributing to a New York Post article I’d written about “chronoworking”. As the author of a book about circadian rhythms, it was exactly the sort of subject I might write about. Except I’d never heard of this person, let alone interviewed them. I clicked on the link and my stomach dropped. There, above an article about people who organise their working lives around their biological clocks, was my name: Linda Geddes. Continue reading...

item.title: Uganda launches Ebola vaccine trial

item.title: Kenya reports third Ebola case, contact tracing continues
item.description: Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola, a relative of a man who died earlier this month after travelling from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The health ministry said the 65-year-old woman tested positive while in quarantine, where she has been since 5 October. The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, is in a stable condition. Health officials say there is no evidence of community transmission, as both individuals were under quarantine. However, three contacts have yet to be traced. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.

The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, is in a stable condition. Health officials say there is no evidence of community transmission, as both individuals were under quarantine. However, three contacts have yet to be traced. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.

item.title: Pope to return to Vatican after cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will leave the Rome hospital Saturday where he has been recovering from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said, after doctors deemed him “fit for discharge”. Leo, 71, has been at the Gemelli hospital north of the Vatican since Tuesday, where doctors removed part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour. “Considering the blood tests, the chest X-ray done this morning, and evaluating the clinical picture, the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge,” doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora wrote in a note published by the Vatican. The Vatican confirmed that “Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today”. “He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican. Tomorrow he will recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment,” the Vatican said. The Angelus prayer is typically given by the pope from the window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter’s Square. But in past years, former popes John Paul II and Francis similarly hospitalised at the Gemelli have delivered the prayer from the window of their hospital rooms. The Vatican’s press office said that Leo celebrated mass on Saturday, as he has in recent days, in a room on the 10th floor of the hospital where he has been recovering. – Up in air – News that the otherwise healthy and sporty pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung has rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics. But his doctors have said Leo’s recovery has been progressing normally as they await the results of tests that will determine the course of action to take. Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky. Up in the air, however, is a planned papal voyage to South America, scheduled for November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Pope watchers say that Leo — who spent two decades as a missionary in Peru — is anxious to make the long journey, but will likely follow the recommendations of his doctors. Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20. The pope himself announced to the public in St Peter’s Square last Sunday, following the Angelus prayer, that a routine medical examination had revealed a nodule that doctors recommended should be removed. The post Pope to return to Vatican after cancer surgery appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria commiserates with Saudi Arabia over terrorists’ attacks
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo ‎ ‎President Bola Tinubu has conveyed heartfelt condolences to the government and people of Saudi Arabia over the recent numerous attacks on the country by the Houthi militia from Yemen. ‎ ‎The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made this known when he received the Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Nigeria, Yousef bin Mohammed Al-Balawi, in his office during the week. ‎ ‎In the letter, President Tinubu strongly condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi militia and commiserated with the Prime Minister, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the government and people of Saudi Arabia on the attacks that have claimed many lives and destroyed physical infrastructure and critical installations in the country. ‎ ‎While delivering the letter to the Ambassador, the Minister noted that there was no alternative to peace, urging people in the region to eschew violence. ‎ ‎An obviously elated Ambassador Yousef expressed profound appreciation to President Tinubu for his kind words of solidarity, consolation and principled stance of strong condemnation and abhorrence of terrorists and rebel activists against legitimate governments while stressing his unalloyed commitment to regional and international peace and security. ‎ ‎The Special Adviser on Media and Strategic Communications to the Minister, Mr. Richard Elesho, made this known in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday. The post Nigeria commiserates with Saudi Arabia over terrorists’ attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I’d have left Real Madrid if I were Vinicius, says Mourinho
item.description: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Saturday if he were winger Vinicius Junior he would have left the club this summer. The Brazilian was sent off during Madrid’s win over Villarreal last weekend for hair pulling and was banned for four matches, meaning he will miss the Clasico clash against Barcelona on October 25. Vinicius, 26, has also been targeted regularly by opposition fans and been racially abused on many occasions since joining Madrid in 2018. “He’s a spectacular kid who it’s easy to have a good relationship with,” Mourinho told reporters. “He’s a fantastic boy, tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile… “If it were me in his place, probably I wouldn’t be here. In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league, a country, to somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him.” In the summer Vinicius signed a new contract with Real Madrid until 2032. Question marks remain over whether Madrid can line up with attacking superstars Vinicius, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham together, without losing balance. “Because he loves Real Madrid, for loving the club and the city, for believing that things can always improve, he renewed and he keeps on smiling,” continued Mourinho. “No one or nobody can… well, influence him negatively yes, because he’s human… but take away his joy of living and working and being with his team-mates, no, no one can do that.” Mourinho took Vinicius off during the 4-3 Champions League win at Roma on Wednesday, with the winger still struggling to return to the form that helped him win the competition twice under Carlo Ancelotti. Mourinho said he was happy that Vinicius’s ban was four matches, saying he thought some hidden figures at the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee “would give him one or two more”. – ‘There are limits’ – Madrid face Sevilla on Sunday aiming not to fall further behind league leaders Barcelona, who visit Real Betis later on Saturday. Hansi Flick’s Barcelona have won every single match this season and are six points ahead of fourth-placed Real Madrid. Los Blancos and Mourinho have blamed referees for some of their results, including the 2-1 derby defeat by Atletico Madrid in September. On Friday Real Madrid called for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels. Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with “those propaganda techniques” and not with the ideology of the Nazis. “I don’t want to talk about this, there are limits and there are limits. You can only excuse it if it’s a clinical case — otherwise there’s no excuse,” said Mourinho. “I don’t want to go down that road. Madrid and its fans understands what it is up against. “For the prestige that the league has abroad, for being the current world champions, it’s better if we try to keep this here and not let it get

item.title: PHOTOS: Shettima, Akpabio, Sanwo-Olu, Others Attend Oyebanji’s Second-Term Inauguration In Ekiti
item.description: The Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, was sworn in on Friday for his second term in office. The ceremony was attended by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who represented President Bola Tinubu; Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma; and other political leaders. Governor Oyebanji and Vice President Shettima waving to the crowd at the inauguration ceremony on Friday, October 16, 2026. Speaking in Ado-Ekiti during the inauguration ceremony, Oyebanji said his administration would focus on translating infrastructure projects and public spending into tangible economic benefits for households, farmers, artisans, entrepreneurs and young people. Ekiti State Governor Oyebanji waving to the crowd during his swearing-in for a second term on Friday, October 16, 2026. The governor acknowledged the economic pressures confronting families, particularly the rising costs of food, transportation, education and other essential needs, stressing that government policies must deliver practical relief and expand opportunities for citizens. Ekiti State Governor, Oyebanji, taking the oath of office during his second term inauguration on Friday, October 16, 2026. Oyebanji said the prosperity his administration seeks must be reflected in better livelihoods, stronger businesses, productive farms, improved public services and greater economic security for families. He explained that roads should enable farmers to transport their produce to markets before harvests are lost, while reliable electricity should support industrialisation, improve productivity and help small businesses remain operational. The post PHOTOS: Shettima, Akpabio, Sanwo-Olu, Others Attend Oyebanji’s Second-Term Inauguration In Ekiti appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Watch ‘Fishbone’, a 2020 Short Film by Anakle Films About Drug Counterfeiting
item.description: Years after its release, Fishbone remains relevant as Nigeria continues to grapple with counterfeit and substandard products. NAFDAC has repeatedly warned about falsified drugs and other products in circulation, including products that can lead to treatment failure, drug resistance and even death. Nigerians share their outcry on social media about their encounters with counterfeit products, from deodorant, chicken, toothpaste, to drinks, body and hair cream, soy sauce, palm oil, and many others. It is an ongoing public health concern. Released in 2020 by Anakle Films in collaboration with the US Mission in Nigeria and the US Department of Justice, Fishbone is a short film that explores the dangers of drug counterfeiting through the story of Mama T ( Shaffy Bello ), a respected philanthropist who secretly runs a counterfeit drug operation in Makoko, Lagos, and Inspector Cole ( Daniel Etim Effiong ), who is determined to bring her down. Beyond its crime-drama storyline, Fishbone explores the layers of counterfeiting, from the exploitation of vulnerable communities and the influence of wealth and social status to the devastating consequences of putting profit before human life. Its central message is particularly unsettling because the people who manufacture and distribute fake products can be deeply embedded in the same communities they endanger, without their knowledge. Rewatching Fishbone is an opportunity to remind ourselves how dangerous counterfeit products are. By showing how counterfeit drugs move through a community and affect people who may have no idea what they are buying, the film reminds viewers that awareness, vigilance and accountability matter. It is also a timely prompt to be more careful about where medicines are purchased and to report suspected falsified products to the appropriate authorities. Watch Fishbone again, and remember that behind every counterfeit product is a risk someone else may have to pay for with their life. The post Watch ‘Fishbone’, a 2020 Short Film by Anakle Films About Drug Counterfeiting appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
item.description: null The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower. Remember to use a trusted website like Time and Date to discover the exact moment of moonset for your location. Where should I look to see Orionid meteors? Orionid shooting stars will appear to originate from a patch of sky, or radiant, located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion , which glistens above the southeastern horizon for stargazers in the U.S. during the early hours of Oct. 22. For the best views look 40-90 degrees away from the radiant, where the glowing trains left in the wake of the fast-moving meteors will be at their longest. Be sure to head away from artificial lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to fully adapt to the dark for the best What causes the Orionid meteor shower? The Orionid meteor shower is active each year as Earth passes through the stream of debris left behind by Comet 1P/Halley , which was observed by a fleet of spacecraft when it last visited the inner solar system in 1986. Shooting stars become visible when particles of the ancient comet collide with our planet's atmosphere at 147,600 miles per hour (237,539 kilometers per hour), vaporizing in a spectacular display of natural fireworks. Hoping to catch a shooting star for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing meteor showers , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography . Editor's Note: If you would like to share your Orionid photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Gunmen storm Plateau community, kill four vigilantes
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed four vigilantes keeping watch over their community in Shurum village, Dorowa Babuje, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 11:56pm on Friday, when the attackers stormed the community and killed the vigilantes while they were on duty. A member of the community, Mr Bulus Bature, said, “They were watching over our community when the gunmen struck and killed them.” Lamenting the killings, Bature said, “It is painful that people who volunteered to protect their community could be attacked and killed while carrying out their duty.” The National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, BYM, Rwang Tengwong also confirmed the incident to Vanguard. Tengwong said, “We received information about the attack and can confirm that four people were killed by the gunmen.” He condemned the killings, saying, “It is unfortunate that our people, who were keeping watch over their community, were targeted and killed.” He added, “We are deeply saddened by this latest attack and call on the relevant security agencies to urgently investigate the incident and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.” Tengwong further said, “Our people cannot continue to live in fear while those volunteering to protect their communities are being attacked and killed.” “We appeal to the government and security agencies to strengthen security around the affected communities.” Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident were unsuccessful as of press time. The post Gunmen storm Plateau community, kill four vigilantes appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Everton vs Chelsea: All the talking points
item.description: Chelsea face their first away trip outside London this season when they travel to Merseyside to take on Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Saturday’s 12:30 p.m. Premier League fixture. The encounter marks Chelsea’s second visit to Everton’s new home, with the Blues eager to bounce back from their previous meeting at the stadium, where they suffered a disappointing 3-0 defeat earlier this year. Chelsea head into the contest in encouraging form following their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth last weekend. The result leaves them with one more win, four additional goals and two more points than they had at the corresponding stage of the previous campaign. The Blues have also developed a habit of scoring early this season, breaking the deadlock five times in the opening stages of their league matches. Their ability to strike quickly could prove valuable against an Everton side that has remained unbeaten so far this term. Everton, meanwhile, drew 2-2 with Hull City on Sunday, scoring the first league goals conceded by the Tigers at home this season. The match presents an intriguing contest between Chelsea’s potent attacking force and Everton’s impressive defensive record. The fixture has featured in every Premier League season since 1989, making it a familiar rivalry for both clubs. Chelsea have enjoyed considerable success in early Saturday kick-offs, remaining unbeaten in their last 10 matches played in the 12:30 p.m. slot, recording eight victories and two draws. Their most recent appearance in that time window ended in a 1-1 draw against Liverpool at Anfield in May. A victory on Saturday would see Chelsea move above Everton in the league standings and could lift them as high as fourth place, depending on the outcome of Brentford’s clash with Liverpool later in the day. Chelsea’s historical struggles at Everton Despite their recent form, Chelsea face a difficult challenge given their record on Everton’s home turf. Only Liverpool, where the Blues have suffered 50 league defeats, have proved a more troublesome away destination than Everton, against whom Chelsea have lost 44 times—the same number as against Arsenal. Goodison Park hosted most of those defeats, accounting for 43 of them. However, Chelsea’s 3-0 loss at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in March was their heaviest defeat away to Everton since a 4-1 reverse in October 1987. Before that setback, Chelsea had gone four matches without defeat against the Toffees, winning three of those encounters. Their most recent victory at Goodison Park came in August 2022, when Jorginho converted a penalty to secure the points and end a run of four consecutive defeats at the ground. Chelsea’s history at Everton stretches back more than a century. Their first league victory at Goodison came in April 1908, when George Hilsdon scored a hat-trick in a 3-0 triumph. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: Chelsea face their first away trip outside London this season when they travel to Merseyside to take on Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Saturday’s 12:30 p.m. Premier League fixture. The encounter marks Chelsea’s second visit to Everton’s new home, with the Blues eager to bounce back from their previous meeting at the stadium, where they suffered a disappointing 3-0 defeat earlier this year. Chelsea head into the contest in encouraging form following their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth last weekend. The result leaves them with one more win, four additional goals and two more points than they had at the corresponding stage of the previous campaign. The Blues have also developed a habit of scoring early this season, breaking the deadlock five times in the opening stages of their league matches. Their ability to strike quickly could prove valuable against an Everton side that has remained unbeaten so far this term. Everton, meanwhile, drew 2-2 with Hull City on Sunday, scoring the first league goals conceded by the Tigers at home this season. The match presents an intriguing contest between Chelsea’s potent attacking force and Everton’s impressive defensive record. The fixture has featured in every Premier League season since 1989, making it a familiar rivalry for both clubs. Chelsea have enjoyed considerable success in early Saturday kick-offs, remaining unbeaten in their last 10 matches played in the 12:30 p.m. slot, recording eight victories and two draws. Their most recent appearance in that time window ended in a 1-1 draw against Liverpool at Anfield in May. A victory on Saturday would see Chelsea move above Everton in the league standings and could lift them as high as fourth place, depending on the outcome of Brentford’s clash with Liverpool later in the day. Chelsea’s historical struggles at Everton Despite their recent form, Chelsea face a difficult challenge given their record on Everton’s home turf. Only Liverpool, where the Blues have suffered 50 league defeats, have proved a more troublesome away destination than Everton, against whom Chelsea have lost 44 times—the same number as against Arsenal. Goodison Park hosted most of those defeats, accounting for 43 of them. However, Chelsea’s 3-0 loss at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in March was their heaviest defeat away to Everton since a 4-1 reverse in October 1987. Before that setback, Chelsea had gone four matches without defeat against the Toffees, winning three of those encounters. Their most recent victory at Goodison Park came in August 2022, when Jorginho converted a penalty to secure the points and end a run of four consecutive defeats at the ground. Chelsea’s history at Everton stretches back more than a century. Their first league victory at Goodison came in April 1908, when George Hilsdon scored a hat-trick in a 3-0 triumph. The Blues also recorded a memorable 3-2 victory on Merseyside in August 1919, shortly after the resumption of football following the First World War. They repeated the scoreline three years later, although another 26 years passed before they claimed all three points there again, with Roy Bentley scoring in another 3-2 win. In October 1956, Chelsea secured a 3-0 victory through two goals from Les Stubbs. Further memorable successes followed, including a 2-0 win in March 1969, courtesy of goals from Alan Birchenall and Ian Hutchinson. Gordon Davies scored a hat-trick in a thrilling 4-3 victory in December 1984, while Steve Clarke helped Chelsea secure another win four years later. That same scoreline also featured in the Blues’ first Premier League visit to Goodison Park, with Robert Fleck making his mark. Chelsea later enjoyed a prolonged period of dominance over Everton, going unbeaten against them home and away in all competitions between 2001 and 2010. That run included their 2009 FA Cup final triumph and Didier Drogba’s dramatic late goal in a 3-2 league victory in December 2006. Two goals from Frank Lampard secured a 2-1 win just before New Year in 2012, launching a productive spell in which Chelsea recorded three victories across five visits. Other notable results included a thrilling 6-3 triumph in August 2014, when Diego Costa scored twice, and a 3-0 victory in 2017 after Chelsea scored three times in a 21-minute second-half spell. However, their 1-0 success in 2022 remains their only victory at Everton since that period. Key statistics ahead of the match Chelsea have several encouraging numbers to take into Saturday’s encounter. Both Chelsea and Everton have committed fewer fouls than any other Premier League side this season, with 50 and 44 respectively. Joao Pedro has converted five of his 13 shots into goals, while Chelsea boast the league’s second-best shot-conversion rate at 18.29 per cent, behind Manchester City’s 19.28 per cent. Everton have registered 14 high turnovers that resulted in shots, the highest tally in the division this season, although only one has led to a goal. Meanwhile, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer have combined to create 24 attempts on goal this campaign. Chelsea’s early scoring has been particularly remarkable. The Blues have scored six league goals within the opening seven minutes of matches, representing 40 per cent of their total. Four of those strikes came within the first three minutes, leaving the club one short of its record for an entire Premier League season, set during the 2014/15 title-winning campaign. Their recent victory over Bournemouth also produced an individual milestone. Jordan Henderson, aged 36 years and 115 days, became Chelsea’s oldest English goalscorer since John Terry scored against Watford in May 2017. Henderson also scored and assisted within two minutes and 29 seconds against Bournemouth. Only Emile Heskey, who achieved the feat against Derby County in April 1998 in less than two minutes, has completed the double more quickly in a Premier League match. With Chelsea’s attacking momentum and Everton’s defensive resilience set to collide, Saturday’s encounter promises to be a demanding test for both sides. The Blues will hope their improved form and early goals can help them overcome their difficult record on Merseyside and strengthen their push towards the top four. item.title: Amazon wants you to Bee-lieve wearable AI can recall it all for you
item.description: Amazon wants to ensure you have a personal AI that you can carry with you anywhere, listening in on your conversations so it can remind you of key details – and give you personalized shopping recommendations, of course. The global online bazaar has unveiled two new AI-based products from Bee, a startup in wearable devices that it acquired last year in a deal said to be worth $300 million. Bee’s original product for Amazon was tried out and sort of given approval by friend of The Register Corey Quinn, Chief Cloud Economist at Duckbill, earlier this year. One new gizmo, Bee Frontier, is designed to be worn like a watch or one of those fitness trackers, although to our mind it looks more like you are wearing a doorbell. The other, Bee Eclipse, is a slimline and lightweight device about the size of a credit card that attaches to the back of your phone magnetically, like a limpet. Both are intended to listen in to your conversations and help you remember important details, like when you are meeting your friend for a pint later and at which hospitality outlet. The devices take note of the details you might otherwise forget, and then turn them into useful conversation summaries, to-dos and reminders, Amazon says. The pair of devices feature a single button to turn on or off, and a visible indicator that lights up when one is listening in and its AI is summarizing the conversation. When enabled, the eavesdropper gathers context from your conversations to provide insights and recommendations. Summaries of your conversations can be accessed via a Bee mobile app on iPhone or Android (linked via Bluetooth), or an all-new desktop app. These can be organized using templates for things such as lectures, or users can just review memories from the past few days to see what you discussed. The Bee devices pick up on trends or themes that recur, and recommend personalized goals and actions. That sounds alarm bells for us, as it suggests the AI is designed to get to know you, and what you like. Along with the new hardware, Bee has now gained the ability to connect to Amazon’s Alexa+ AI assistant and Amazon.com, which means that you can ask Alexa for a meeting summary - or get personalized shopping recommendations from Amazon based on what your personal earwig has gleaned. However, Amazon says that the latest Bee products respect user privacy, as audio is processed into insights in real time and not stored, while transcripts are encrypted and only the user can access them. Bee Frontier is claimed to have IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, and has a USB-C charging port. Bee Eclipse also has a USB-C port but is said to last for more than 21 days of use from a single battery charge. Both devices come in a choice of colors, with Bee Frontier available now for $74.99 and Bee Eclipse due to be available shortly for $99.99. ®

Summaries of your conversations can be accessed via a Bee mobile app on iPhone or Android (linked via Bluetooth), or an all-new desktop app. These can be organized using templates for things such as lectures, or users can just review memories from the past few days to see what you discussed. The Bee devices pick up on trends or themes that recur, and recommend personalized goals and actions. That sounds alarm bells for us, as it suggests the AI is designed to get to know you, and what you like. Along with the new hardware, Bee has now gained the ability to connect to Amazon’s Alexa+ AI assistant and Amazon.com, which means that you can ask Alexa for a meeting summary - or get personalized shopping recommendations from Amazon based on what your personal earwig has gleaned. However, Amazon says that the latest Bee products respect user privacy, as audio is processed into insights in real time and not stored, while transcripts are encrypted and only the user can access them. Bee Frontier is claimed to have IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, and has a USB-C charging port. Bee Eclipse also has a USB-C port but is said to last for more than 21 days of use from a single battery charge. Both devices come in a choice of colors, with Bee Frontier available now for $74.99 and Bee Eclipse due to be available shortly for $99.99. ®

item.title: Oil tanker on fire after hitting mine in Hormuz – Iran’s Guards
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Saturday said an oil tanker was on fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a mine in the waterway at the heart of the Middle East war. Tehran seized control over Hormuz after the start of the war in late February, choking off the strait that normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. “A supertanker in violation of regulations, carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and attempting to pass illegally through the Strait of Hormuz, struck a mine, triggering an explosion and a fierce fire,” the Revolutionary Guards said. The statement did not specify the exact location of the incident. Flanked by Iran to the north and Oman to the south, the Hormuz strait is about 30 kilometres (20 miles) wide at its narrowest point. Since taking control of the strait, Iran has demanded that all ships seek its authorisation before transiting. “The tanker attempted to cross the strait with US support… by deactivating all its tracking systems,” the Guards added, also posting a video of a vessel in flames during the night. In response to Tehran’s blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, Washington has imposed its own naval counter-blockade on Iranian oil exports. This week, the Guards’ naval commander Admiral Ali Ozmai warned that any vessel that deactivated its navigation systems would be considered “hostile”. The post Oil tanker on fire after hitting mine in Hormuz – Iran’s Guards appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: We’ll rescue Jigawa from APC’s failures – Lamido vows
item.description: ‎By ‎Muhammad Inuwa ‎ ‎Former Jigawa State Governor, Sule Lamido, has vowed that the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) will rescue Jigawa State from what he described as the failures of the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration in the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎Lamido made the declaration while speaking at the inauguration of the PDP Campaign Council held at the party’s state headquarters in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital. ‎ ‎He accused the APC-led government of taking the state backwards, particularly in healthcare, education and other critical sectors, saying the PDP was determined to restore good governance. ‎ ‎”Unfortunately, Jigawa State has been taken backwards under the present administration. We are determined to restore the state to its rightful position in governance, development, unity and peaceful coexistence,” he said. ‎ ‎The former governor expressed concern over the difficulties facing residents, particularly in accessing basic healthcare services and quality education. ‎ ‎”Today, residents are facing serious challenges in accessing quality healthcare. Hospitals lack adequate medical services, education sector continues to deteriorate. Virtually every critical sector is facing serious challenges,” Lamido said. ‎ ‎He maintained that the PDP possessed experienced and competent individuals capable of addressing the challenges facing the state. ‎ ‎”The APC administration has failed the people of Jigawa State. We are determined to establish a transparent, accountable and people-oriented government because the PDP has experienced and competent individuals who understand the responsibilities of leadership and governance,” he stated. ‎He assured residents that the PDP would prioritise the welfare of the people and promote unity if returned to power in 2027. ‎ ‎”Our administration will be for all residents of Jigawa State, regardless of their political affiliations,” he said. ‎ ‎The former governor also pledged that the party would conduct peaceful campaigns based on mutual respect and understanding, without intimidation or personal attacks. ‎ ‎”Our campaigns will be conducted peacefully, with respect, unity and mutual understanding, without insults, intimidation or personal attacks. Our primary objective is to restore the dignity of Nigeria and Jigawa State,” Lamido added. The post 2027: We’ll rescue Jigawa from APC’s failures – Lamido vows appeared first on Vanguard News .
