item.title: SpaceX launches Falcon 9 Starlink mission for 1st time in more than 3 weeks (video)
item.description: null SpaceX just broke an uncharacteristically long Starlink launch drought. The company sent 27 of its Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) today (Oct. 12), launching them atop a Falcon 9 rocket from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:28 p.m. EDT (5:28 p.m. local time; 0028 GMT on Oct. 13) It was the first Starlink mission for a Falcon 9 since Sept. 19 , which was another 27-satellite liftoff from Vandenberg. For some perspective on this recent gap: Between Aug. 19 and Sept. 6, a span of 19 days, SpaceX launched seven Starlink missions with Falcon 9s. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a ship at sea shortly after the Oct. 12 launch. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX did loft a batch of Starlinks after that, but it wasn't aboard a Falcon 9. The company's Starship megarocket carried 26 next-gen Starlink V3 craft on its 14th test flight, which took place on Sept. 28. Starship reached orbit for the first time ever on Flight 14 , and it deployed the Starlinks successfully as well. This will happen many more times going forward, if all goes to plan: The Starlink V3 constellation will eventually consist of about 100,000 satellites , all of which will fly on Starship, Elon Musk has said. Indeed, SpaceX plans to sunset the Falcon 9 and its cousin, the Falcon Heavy , in the next few years, shifting their duties over to the fully reusable, far more powerful Starship, which remains in the test-flight phase. That shift will be a big one for the spaceflight community, for the Falcon 9 is the workhorse rocket of its generation. In 2025, for example, it flew 165 times — roughly the same number as the rest of the world's orbital launchers combined. Nearly three-quarters of those Falcon 9 launches were Starlink missions. Things have slowed down a bit in 2026. Today's flight was the 112th Falcon 9 liftoff of the year, and the 82nd in service of the Starlink megaconstellation, which currently consists of more than 11,100 active satellites . Previous Booster 1088 launches NROL-126 | Transporter-12 | SPHEREx | NROL-57 | USSF-366 | 14 Starlink missions All went according to plan on today's launch. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. It was the 20th launch and landing for this particular booster, which is designated B1088. The rocket's expendable upper stage, meanwhile, delivered the 27 spacecraft to LEO, deploying them there 62 minutes after liftoff, SpaceX announced via X .

item.title: SpaceX successfully launches 6,300 pounds of cargo to the International Space Station
item.description: null SpaceX launched its latest cargo mission to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday morning (Oct. 13). A Falcon 9 rocket launched a robotic Dragon capsule to the orbiting lab from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Tuesday at 6:35 a.m. EDT (1035 GMT). The launch kicks off the CRS-35 mission, so named because it will be the 35th that SpaceX flies under a Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA. A side by side view of a rocket engine in space and the interior of a rocket fairing containing cargo bound for the International Space Station. (Image credit: SpaceX, NASA) If all goes according to plan, Dragon will reach the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Oct. 15), docking autonomously to the space-facing port of its Harmony module at around 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT). You can watch the arrival here at Space.com as well; coverage will start at 9:15 a.m. EDT (1315 GMT). CRS-35 will deliver 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays (iROSAs), which will boost the orbiting lab's energy budget. There's also quite a bit of scientific gear heading up on the flight. Dragon "will deliver hardware to manufacture artificial retinas in microgravity to help restore vision on Earth and 3D heart tissue models to advance large‑scale drug testing on future missions," NASA officials wrote in a CRS-35 launch preview on Oct. 7. "The spacecraft will carry materials to study how a new type of glass forms in microgravity and brain organoids that could reveal treatment targets for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and multiple sclerosis," they added. Dragon will stay attached to the ISS for about a month, then head back down to Earth with scientific experiments and other hardware. It will splash down safely under parachutes in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast. SpaceX's Dragon is the only currently operational freighter that can carry cargo in the downward direction. The other three — Russia's Progress , Japan's HTV-X and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL — are all expendable, burning up in Earth's atmosphere after their time at the ISS is done. Editor's note: This story was updated at 6:59 a.m. EDT on Oct. 13 with news of a successful launch.

item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Welcome home, Sophie Adenot
item.description: Video: 00:02:54 After 237 days and over 3,700 orbits around Earth aboard the International Space Station, Sophie Adenot is back on Earth! Following a handover to Crew-13, Sophie and her Crew-12 crewmates undocked on 7 October and splashed down off the coast of California the next day. Now back in Europe, Sophie will begin her post-flight data collection and rehabilitation while readjusting to life on Earth after the longest mission in space by a European astronaut so far. Welcome home, Sophie!

It features TCL All Domain Halo Control Technology, up to 512 Precise Dimming Zones, a 144Hz native refresh rate, an AiPQ Pro Processor, a Matte HVA Panel and an ONKYO 2.1 Hi Fi audio system. Smarter Cooling Designed for Local Climate Needs With warm temperatures forming part of everyday life across Nigeria, cooling performance, energy management and convenience remain important considerations for households. TCL highlighted two air conditioning solutions designed to address these priorities, the FreshIN 3.0 and SaveIN AI Series 24K. TCL FreshIN 3.0 FreshIN 3.0 expands the air conditioning experience beyond temperature control by introducing fresh outdoor air into the room while supporting improved indoor air quality. Key technologies include FreshIN Technology, T AI Energy Saving, Smart Voice Control, QuadruPuri filtration, Visible Air Quality and Gentle Breeze. Combining No Frost cooling with inverter performance, the model has been designed around flexibility, capacity and convenience, responding to the needs of households looking for practical food storage alongside a premium kitchen aesthetic. Smarter Laundry for Busy Households with the TCL C5 Washer Dryer The TCL C5 washer dryer combines a 12 kg washing capacity with TCL Super Drum technology, providing additional washing space and improved fabric movement. Its feature set includes Auto Dose, jetBubble technology, Wi Fi connectivity, Steam Wash, activeFresh, Dynamic Rinse and quick wash programmes. The large capacity format is particularly suited to family households, while its connected features and automatic washing functions help reduce the effort required for everyday laundry and fabric care. Strengthening TCL’s Presence Across Nigeria The regional launch underlines TCL’s strategy to strengthen its presence across Nigeria through a broader product ecosystem and closer collaboration with local distributors, retailers, media and technology communities. By combining global product innovation with a stronger understanding of local consumer priorities, TCL aims to deliver products that are relevant across different areas of everyday life, from entertainment and cooling to food storage, laundry and connected displays. Daniel Ray added: “Our focus is to strengthen TCL’s presence market by market, with products that respond to the needs of the consumers we serve. item.title: “A Girl Who Learns Is a Girl Who Is Not a Bride” – Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili
item.description: A girl who learns is not a bride. Today, the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage ; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent. In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North, the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry. The cost of inaction is high . Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Centre for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress. Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly. Progress is possible . An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong: Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more. In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage. If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated. Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet, a girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out. Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija Features
item.content:encoded: A girl who learns is not a bride. Today, the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage ; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent. In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North, the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry. The cost of inaction is high . Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Centre for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress. Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly. Progress is possible . An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong: Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more. In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage. If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated. Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet, a girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out. Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has. At the Columbia launch, I said that community programmes and advocacy are not enough on their own. Governments must lead. On this Day of the Girl, Human Capital Africa calls on African governments to: Make foundational learning a girl-protection policy. Every girl should be reading with comprehension by age ten, using proven methods such as structured pedagogy and Teaching at the Right Level. Guarantee the move into secondary school. Remove fees, uniform and transport costs for girls, especially in rural communities with high rates of child marriage. Enforce 18 as the minimum age of marriage in law and in practice, in every state and every community, with traditional and religious leaders as partners. Fund this domestically. As foreign aid shrinks, African budgets and African philanthropy must take over. Measure and publish. Track girls’ learning, their transition to secondary school, and child marriage rates in national accountability systems. The AU Decade of Education gives Africa ten years and a continental mandate. As a member of its Steering Committee, I will press for girls’ learning and retention to be at the centre of how the Decade’s success is measured. A Decade that does not end child marriage will not have transformed African education. The Columbia report sets a realistic target: cutting child marriage prevalence from one in five to one in seven within five years. Africa can lead the way to that target, but only if we treat every girl’s classroom as the place where her childhood is protected. Any girl-child should be a student, not a bride. She should learn, then lead. The post “A Girl Who Learns Is a Girl Who Is Not a Bride” – Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Aspira Nigeria Celebrates Three Wins at Marketing Edge Awards 2026
item.description: Aspira Nigeria Limited, manufacturer of Viva detergent, Viva Dishwashing Liquid, and Oracare Toothpaste, among other household-care brands, has received three recognitions at the 2026 Marketing Edge Awards, with its brands recognised across the liquid dishwash, bar soap and detergent categories. The company received the Outstanding Liquid Dishwash Brand of the Year award, while Viva Multipurpose Soap was named Outstanding Bar Soap Brand of the Year. Aspira also received the Outstanding Detergent Brand of the Decade award, recognising its longstanding presence in Nigeria’s detergent category. The awards ceremony was held on Friday, September 25, at Ten Degrees Event Hall, Billings Way, Oregun, Ikeja, bringing together brands, marketing professionals and stakeholders from across Nigeria’s marketing, advertising and communications industry. The Marketing Edge Awards recognise brands and professionals across the marketing and communications sector, with categories covering different aspects of brand building, consumer engagement and industry performance. For Aspira, the three recognitions span different areas of its household-care portfolio. The liquid dishwash and bar soap awards recognise its presence in two competitive household categories, while the Detergent Brand of the Decade award acknowledges the longer-term journey of its detergent business. Speaking on the recognitions, Barbara Onianwah, Head of Marketing, Aspira Nigeria Limited, said the awards acknowledged the consistency required to build and sustain brands in a competitive market. “These recognitions are meaningful because they reflect the consistency and work that go into building brands that remain relevant to consumers. We are pleased that the awards recognise different areas of our portfolio, as well as the longer journey of our detergent business. For us, it is an encouragement to continue listening to consumers, learning from the market and evolving our approach,” she said. The recognitions come as brands in Nigeria’s fast-moving consumer goods sector continue to respond to changing consumer preferences and increased competition across household-care categories. With the three awards spanning liquid dishwash, bar soap and detergent, Aspira’s recognition at the 2026 Marketing Edge Awards reflects its presence across multiple segments of the household-care market, while the decade award highlights the longer history of its detergent business. The Marketing Edge Awards provided an opportunity for brands and industry professionals to come together and celebrate notable work and achievements within Nigeria’s marketing and communications landscape. item.title: Some of Ayra Starr’s Iconic Live Performances
item.description: Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London There are not many great live performers in music. Some artists are very good but are only comfortable in the studio, which is understandable because music, like writing, is a solitary work and would require extra force or pull to stand before an audience and perform. But there are also great live performers who, despite how good they are in the studio, are also comfortable bringing the music to a live audience. There is something special about that, watching an artist bring their music to life on stage. The vocals, the choreography, the stage presence, the connection with the audience — sometimes, a live performance makes you appreciate a song in an entirely new way. There aren’t many with the artistry in Afrobeats. But Ayra Starr has made herself one of Afrobeats’ most exciting performers, and has constantly used the stage as another place to show the world her sability . From commanding festival stages and performing at major international music events to delivering memorable renditions of her biggest hits, Ayra Starr has continued to prove that her talent extends beyond the recording studio. She knows how to bring her music, personality, and energy together in a way that keeps audiences watching. As her global profile continues to grow, with her recent 2026 NFL Halftime International Games performance in London, we’re looking back at some of Ayra Starr’s most iconic live performances: Ayra Starr – Rush | Glastonbury 2024 Ayra Starr & ZAYN – Heaven Baby (Live Performance @ All Points East 2026) Ayra Starr – Rush (Live Performance in Paris) Ayra Starr – Live at Global Citizen Festival 2025 (Full Performance) Ayra Starr | Live – Les Ardentes 2024 Ayra Starr Lights Up Eden Park with “Commas” | Coldplay’s Music of the Spheres Tour (Auckland) The post Some of Ayra Starr’s Iconic Live Performances appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Watch Ayra Starr’s 2026 NFL Halftime Performance!
item.description: Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London Since Ayra Starr emerged into the music scene with her debut EP, “Ayra Starr”, in 2021, she has gone on to break and set many records. But of all the records broken and set, none might top the feeling of being the first African artist to headline an NFL International Games Halftime Show. On Sunday, the 11th of October, 2026, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, Ayra Starr made the dream a reality. Before 61,322 people in attendance, Ayra dazzled on stage and not only made herself proud, but also made her country and language proud. She opened her performance with an emotional performance of “H eaven Baby”, her fan-favourite song featuring Zayn Malik , followed by a soulful performance of her Grammy-nominated song, “Rush.” She concluded the performance with songs from her latest album, “Starrgirl”, such as “D angerous,” “H ot Body,” and “Ms Paper.” Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London Watch the full performance below: The post Watch Ayra Starr’s 2026 NFL Halftime Performance! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.dc:creator: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: How to Watch Ayra Starr’s NFL Halftime Performance: Kick-Off Time and Where to Stream
item.description: Ayra Starr at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium ahead of her historic NFL halftime show performance in London. Ayra Starr is taking Afrobeats to the football field, and this time, we’re talking American football! The Nigerian superstar is set to make history as the first African artiste to headline an NFL international halftime show when she performs at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Sunday, 11 October 2026. And with the Philadelphia Eagles facing the Jacksonville Jaguars, football fans will have a little extra entertainment to look forward to during the break. For Ayra, whose music has travelled from Nigeria to audiences around the world, this is another exciting addition to her growing list of international performances. This time, she’ll be introducing even more sports fans to her music, with songs from her Starrgirl project making their way to one of the NFL’s biggest international platforms. And what can fans expect to hear? Well, we’re hoping some of our favourites make the setlist. Perhaps “ Hot Body ” and “ Tornado ”, or even “ Heaven Baby ”, her collaboration with ZAYN . Nothing has been confirmed about the songs she’ll perform, but we’re already curious to see what she has planned for the halftime show. Ayra Starr speaking at the NFL London Games press conference ahead of her performance. If you’re planning to watch from Nigeria, here’s what you need to know. The Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars game is scheduled to kick off at 2:30 PM British Summer Time (BST), which is 2:30 PM West Africa Time (WAT). In the UK, viewers can catch the game on ITV1 and Sky Sports NFL, while fans in Nigeria and other supported regions can watch through DAZN’s NFL Game Pass. Viewers in the United States can tune in on FOX. The halftime performance will take place during the match, so keep an eye on the game if you don’t want to miss Ayra’s set. From performing her songs on music stages to preparing for an NFL halftime show in London, Ayra Starr keeps finding new audiences for her music. And for Nigerian fans watching from home, there’s something particularly exciting about seeing one of our own take the stage at an international sporting event of this scale. *** Photo Credit: Ayra Starr/Instagram The post How to Watch Ayra Starr’s NFL Halftime Performance: Kick-Off Time and Where to Stream appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Chinazaekpere Chukwu’s First Feature Film Her Daughters’ Mother Heads to London for Film Africa 2026
item.description: Ejovwoke Obas Olikuntuyi delivers a powerful performance as Ejiro in Her Daughters’ Mother Nollywood is having an incredible global moment, and we couldn’t be prouder to cheer on our home-grown talents as they take their stories to the world. Filmmaker Chinazaekpere Chukwu is making her feature directorial debut with Her Daughters’ Mother , and the poignant Nigerian drama has been officially selected to screen at Film Africa 2026. Scheduled for an October 28 screening at the newly launched EbonyLife Place London, the 110-minute feature explores womanhood, sacrifice, and the enduring bond between mothers and daughters. Speaking on the emotional backbone of the project, Chinazaekpere Chukwu shared: It’s intended to feel like a juxtaposition of ‘ The Joys of Motherhood ‘ by Buchi Emecheta and ‘ Stay With M e’ by Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀ . It reaches deep into the rights of women, how their lives are decided for them until the end, first by their families/spouses and finally by their kids. Her Daughters’ Mother highlights the quiet resilience and domestic weight carried by women across generations. Set against the rich cultural backdrop of Benin and filmed early this year in English, Pidgin, Urhobo, and Bini, the story follows 33-year-old Ejiro (played by Ejovwoke Obas Olikuntuyi ). After being married off at the tender age of 16, Ejiro returns home in her thirties as a widowed mother of two daughters, determined to secure a brighter future for them. Faced with limited options, she enters a second marriage with Osato ( Philip Asaya ), a lorry driver who promises security and education for her girls in exchange for a male heir. However, when Ejiro struggles to fulfill his demands, Osato’s entitlement turns her life into a nightmare, leaving her longing for the freedom she last felt as a child. Meanwhile, her eldest daughter Ejaita ( Osas Okonyon ), a bright 16-year-old dreaming of becoming a doctor, struggles against her mother’s overprotectiveness, unaware of the immense sacrifices being made on her behalf. Osas Okonyon stars as Ejaita, a bright teenager whose ambitious dreams clash with her mother’s protective sacrifices. The film boasts an exceptional cast, including Najite Dede and Adeoluwa Akintoba . Behind the scenes, Chukwu —who wrote the screenplay alongside Sunday Melvin Iwinosa from a story by Efosa Ogbomo —collaborated with cinematographer Yinka Adegoke , executive producer and co-producer Efosa Ogbomo , and story consultant and editor Joshua Tsotso . Adeoluwa Akintoba in a scene from Her Daughters’ Mother, exploring youth and ambition. Chukwu’s transition to feature filmmaking follows her award-winning streak at the EbonyLife Creative Academy, where she graduated with the Best Director award for A Psalm for Abigail, as well as her standout short film Ti e Nbo , which screened in the Shorts category at AFRIFF in 2023. Produced by One Child Grace Studio in association with C.A.N.O Productions, Uncut Gem Productions, and Nka Pictures, Her Daughters’

item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: BBNaija Season 11’s Final Five Talked Boldness, Authenticity & What Comes Next With Guinness
item.description: BBNaija Season 11 finalists Sheba, Aikou, and winner Temi Nkem reflect on living boldly during their Guinness post-eviction sit-down. As intense as Big Brother Naija can get, nothing quite compares to the tension of finale night! Who will make it into the final five? Who will be among the last three standing? And when Ebuka Obi – Uchendu finally announces the first runner-up, whose name will he call as the winner? Now, imagine being one of the housemates standing on that stage, waiting to hear your name. The suspense alone! But making it that far is a story of its own. The final ten housemates had spent weeks navigating friendships, disagreements, nominations, wagers and all the surprises Biggie had waiting for them. Getting into the Top 10 meant they had played the game boldly, made decisions along the way and found ways to keep going, even when things didn’t work out as planned. And when the season finally wrapped up, we had a few questions for the last five standing. With Guinness, a brand that celebrates boldness and authenticity, powering our BBNaija Season 11 finale post-eviction interviews, we sat down with winner Temi Nkem and fellow finalists Aikou, Sheba, Tram and Bluethopia to talk about their time in Biggie’s house, the choices they made, the courage it took to stay true to themselves and what comes next. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Of course, we wanted to know how they managed to remain grounded while living with a houseful of distinct personalities under 24/7 camera surveillance. There were friendships to navigate, difficult decisions to make and times when speaking up or standing your ground took courage. So, what did living boldly look like for each of them? For Temi Nkem, the conversation explored the instincts and decisions that helped her navigate the competition all the way to the winning spot. Aikou, Sheba, Tram and Bluethopia also reflected on their individual journeys, how they approached the game and what they learnt about themselves along the way. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) And now that the cameras are off and life outside Biggie’s house has begun, what’s next? The finalists shared their plans for the future, the opportunities they’re looking forward to and how they hope to carry that same boldness into their next chapters. Powered by Guinness , these conversations gave us another chance to hear from the housemates after the competition, this time with the pressure of nominations and evictions behind them. After weeks of watching their stories unfold inside the house, we got to hear them tell those stories in their own words. item.title: From Kitchen Bowls to Task Battles: How Checkers Custard Powered BBNaija Season 11
item.description: Big Brother Naija Season 11 winner Temi Nkem poses with a jar of Checkers Custard Vanilla Flavour. Photo Credit: Checkers Custard/Instagram If there is one thing about life in Biggie’s house, it is that there is always something going on. Between the housemates’ conversations, their daily routines, the strategies and the tasks that kept them on their toes, BBNaija Season 11 had no shortage of activity. And through it all, Checkers Custard was right there, serving the housemates creamy custard throughout the show. Because even when you are busy navigating life with 23 other people, there is always room for a comforting bowl of custard! From breakfast before the day’s activities to kitchen catch-ups with fellow housemates, Checkers Custard was part of the everyday experience inside the house. Those kitchen visits were also a chance to catch up, share a laugh and take a breather before the next task or surprise from Biggie. With so much happening under one roof, having something creamy to enjoy was a welcome addition to the routine. And speaking of tasks, Checkers Custard had something special in store for the housemates, too. The Checkers Custard Task called for mental agility, physical endurance and teamwork, giving the housemates a chance to put their skills to the test. With Head of House Tram stepping in as Game Master, the house was split into two teams: Team Creamy and Team Tasty. Now, it was time to see which side could pull together and claim the win. Checkers Custard got the housemates running @CheckersCustard #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaijaS11 #BBNaija #BBNaijaxCheckersCustard https://t.co/geVfgwtZpz — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) September 12, 2026 First, the housemates had to tackle custom obstacle courses, scrambling to collect branded jars along the way. Then came fast-paced physical relays, followed by blindfolded directional challenges that required them to listen carefully and trust their teammates’ instructions. Imagine trying to find your way around without being able to see, while someone else directs your every move! You would need a good deal of patience, communication and teamwork to make it through. Both teams competed for points across the different games, and there was plenty to play for. When the scores were finally counted, Team Creamy came out on top with 140 points, beating Team Tasty to claim the win. Flora , Keivo , Aikou , Araga , Barry , Bells and Bluetopia made up the winning team, with Tram taking on the role of Game Master. That is a win worth celebrating. In the second task, they must select representatives who must pick a Checkers Custard jar as fast as possible when they hear the buzzer. They will be given tasks like ‘touch your ear, touch your toes’ before the buzzer sound. If they pick the jar before the buzzer, they lose a point. Between the housemates’ conversations, their daily routines, the strategies and the tasks that kept them on their toes, BBNaija Season 11 had no shortage of activity. And through it all, Checkers Custard was right there, serving the housemates creamy custard throughout the show. Because even when you are busy navigating life with 23 other people, there is always room for a comforting bowl of custard! From breakfast before the day’s activities to kitchen catch-ups with fellow housemates, Checkers Custard was part of the everyday experience inside the house. Those kitchen visits were also a chance to catch up, share a laugh and take a breather before the next task or surprise from Biggie. With so much happening under one roof, having something creamy to enjoy was a welcome addition to the routine. And speaking of tasks, Checkers Custard had something special in store for the housemates, too. The Checkers Custard Task called for mental agility, physical endurance and teamwork, giving the housemates a chance to put their skills to the test. With Head of House Tram stepping in as Game Master, the house was split into two teams: Team Creamy and Team Tasty. Now, it was time to see which side could pull together and claim the win. Checkers Custard got the housemates running @CheckersCustard #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaijaS11 #BBNaija #BBNaijaxCheckersCustard https://t.co/geVfgwtZpz — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) September 12, 2026 First, the housemates had to tackle custom obstacle courses, scrambling to collect branded jars along the way. Then came fast-paced physical relays, followed by blindfolded directional challenges that required them to listen carefully and trust their teammates’ instructions. Imagine trying to find your way around without being able to see, while someone else directs your every move! You would need a good deal of patience, communication and teamwork to make it through. Both teams competed for points across the different games, and there was plenty to play for. When the scores were finally counted, Team Creamy came out on top with 140 points, beating Team Tasty to claim the win. Flora , Keivo , Aikou , Araga , Barry , Bells and Bluetopia made up the winning team, with Tram taking on the role of Game Master. That is a win worth celebrating. In the second task, they must select representatives who must pick a Checkers Custard jar as fast as possible when they hear the buzzer. They will be given tasks like ‘touch your ear, touch your toes’ before the buzzer sound. If they pick the jar before the buzzer, they lose a point. The team with the most jar wins. #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaijaS11 #BBNaija #BBNaijaxCheckersCustard — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) September 12, 2026 From keeping the housemates supplied with creamy custard throughout BBNaija Season 11 to bringing everyone together for a task that tested their skills and teamwork, Checkers Custard was part of the experience in more ways than one. The housemates had their daily routines, their kitchen catch-ups and their competitive side, and the Checkers Custard Task gave them another chance to put their teamwork to the test. And with Team Creamy finishing on 140 points, there was a clear winner to celebrate. One thing is certain: life in Biggie’s house kept everyone busy, and Checkers Custard was there to make it a little creamier. Congratulations to our winners for winning the Big Brother Naija S11 Checkers Custard Task! Team Creamy Blue Kievo, Bells, Aikou, Barry, Araga, Flora, Bluethopia, and the Game Master Tram. You were all amazing! #BBNaijaXCheckersCustard #CheckersBBNaijaTaskDay #CheckersNaMyComfort #CheckersCustard #BBNaijaSeason11 — Checkers Custard (@CheckersCustard) September 12, 2026 The post From Kitchen Bowls to Task Battles: How Checkers Custard Powered BBNaija Season 11 appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Temi Nkem is officially crowned the winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Uganda, We’re Coming! BellaNaija Heads to ADCCE 2026 in Kampala
item.description: Funmilola Sanya and Dorcas Anya head to Kampala for the Africa Destination Celebrations Conference & Expo (ADCCE 2026) to cover the latest in African celebration tourism for BellaNaija. Hi BNers, we’re heading to Uganda! From October 12th to 17th, 2026, BellaNaija’s Funmilola Sanya and Dorcas Anya will be in Kampala for the Africa Destination Celebrations Conference & Expo (ADCCE 2026). With the theme “ Africa Unveils Events in the Wild ,” ADCCE 2026 brings together wedding and event professionals, tourism stakeholders, hospitality executives, creatives, cultural curators, and industry leaders to explore Africa’s potential as the Celebration Capital of the World. The conference and expo will take place on 12th and 13th October 2026 at the Speke Resort Munyonyo Convention Centre in Kampala, Uganda, followed by destination experiences and familiarisation tours from October 14th to 17th. The gathering aims to showcase Africa’s rich cultural heritage, breathtaking landscapes, unique destinations, and world-class hospitality while creating opportunities for collaboration, investment, and growth across the continent’s celebration and tourism industries. Despite Africa’s incredible destinations and creative talent, the continent remains underrepresented in the global destination wedding and celebration tourism market. ADCCE seeks to change that narrative by connecting African destinations and businesses with international industry professionals and creating greater visibility for the continent’s offerings. For BellaNaija, this is an opportunity to experience Uganda, connect with industry leaders, and discover the people, places, and experiences shaping the future of African celebrations. We’ll be bringing you along for the journey, sharing highlights from the conference, destination experiences, and the memorable moments that make Africa such a special place to celebrate. Stay connected with us on BellaNaija’s social media pages and follow the conversation using #ADCCE2026, #UnveilingDestinationAfrica, #BNTravels. Uganda, we’ll see you soon! The post Uganda, We’re Coming! BellaNaija Heads to ADCCE 2026 in Kampala appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation Partners with Nigeria Computer Society to Support 1,000 Tech Scholars Through Mentorship
item.description: The Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation ( LSEF ) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Nigeria Computer Society ( NCS ) to provide mentorship, technical training and real-world technology experience to the Nigerian whiz kids under the Foundation’s technology scholarship initiative. The 1000 scholarship scheme, which was first announced by Africa’s foremost technology entrepreneur and Chairman of Zinox Group , Leo Stan Ekeh , is designed to empower indigent but exceptionally gifted Nigerian students to study Computer Science and other technology-related disciplines in federal and state universities, as well as polytechnics, across the country. The scholarship reflects Dr. Ekeh’s philosophy of “one family, one tech-empowered person” and will support 1,000 students selected from all 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, irrespective of ethnic background. From their first year through graduation, beneficiaries will receive world-class technology training, skills development and monthly financial support. Each scholar will also have a dedicated mentor to provide guidance throughout their academic journey. Under the MoU, the NCS will provide technical support and practical learning through experienced and certified technology professionals. The programme will blend academic learning with real-world exposure, helping beneficiaries build technical competence, problem-solving skills and the confidence to apply their knowledge beyond the classroom. According to the Director of LSEF, Dr. George Emetuche , the programme will feature boot camps each semester, creating opportunities for students to learn beyond the classroom and gain practical experience. The objective, he explained, is to prepare beneficiaries not merely to graduate, but to become capable technology professionals who can solve real-world problems. Speaking at the ceremony, NCS President, Professor Muhammed Siraju Aliyu , described Dr. Leo Stan Ekeh as a nationalist who has consistently supported initiatives that create opportunities for Nigerians who may otherwise lack access. He noted that Dr. Ekeh’s relationship with the NCS predates the scholarship initiative and has contributed to the advancement of technology and human capital development. He also highlighted Dr. Ekeh’s technology innovation programmes, which identify young people with ideas, support them in developing their concepts and create opportunities for them to pitch to potential investors. Professor Aliyu expressed appreciation for Dr. Ekeh’s contributions to the NCS and reaffirmed the Society’s commitment to initiatives that support national growth and development. Representing the Zinox Group, Executive Director, Human Resources, Mrs. Chioma Nwoke , assured the Foundation and the NCS of the Group’s continued support for the initiative, cohort after cohort. Beyond the scholarship, the programme represents a long-term investment in Nigeria’s human capital. By helping 1,000 gifted young Nigerians

item.title: Watch Asake Trade Big Scenes for Studio Sessions in His “Oba” Music Video
item.description: Asake leans into his royal theme and signature high-steeze style, reflecting the confidence behind his hit track Oba. Photo Credit: Mr Money/Instagram Asake is keeping his foot firmly on the pedal, delivering fresh visuals for “ Oba ” from his latest project M$NEY . Directed by Director Buise, the newly released music video moves away from typical high-energy street setups to take fans directly inside the intimate, creative atmosphere of a late-night recording session. At its core, “Oba”—which translates to King in Yoruba—is a high-steeze anthem centred on royal status, relentless hustle, and staying grounded. Across the track, Asake leans into his “Mister Money” persona, blending Yoruba cultural references with reflections on his unstoppable work ethic. He balances bragging rights about his dominant position in the industry with street wisdom and gratitude, reminding listeners to remain vigilant and humble even as international success rolls in. On set for his Oba music video, Asake highlights his signature high-steeze look with a textured jacket and luxury travel accessories. Photo Credit: Mr Money/Instagram The visual brings this context to life, opening with a bass player laying down a rhythmic groove in a dimly lit studio before panning to Asake seated in the vocal booth. Clad in a green tracksuit over a white tank top, accessorised with thick gold chains, rings, and sunglasses, the YBNL star records his lines while surrounded by producers, engineers, and backing vocalists. The clip blends performance shots with real-time studio mechanics, showing engineers fine-tuning mixing boards, vocalists harmonising at the microphone, and producers triggering beats. Produced by long-time collaborator Magicsticks, “Oba” combines Asake’s signature log-drum rhythms with choir-backed harmonies. Rather than relying on large dance ensembles or cinematic storylines, the visual focuses on the pure craftsmanship behind the music, giving audiences a fly-on-the-wall perspective of how the hit came together in the studio. item.title: Permission to Call Nancy Isime Madam EP? The Actress Is Making Her Executive Producer Debut!
item.description: Nancy Isime steps into her new role as an executive producer wearing a metallic brown ensemble paired with a gold statement necklace. Permission to call Nancy Isime Madam EP? Because the Nollywood star has just announced that she is stepping into a new role, and this time, she will be calling some of the shots behind the camera. Nancy is making her debut as an executive producer, taking on a new side of filmmaking after years of entertaining us on screen. You know her from films and series such as Blood Sisters , Shanty Town , Kambili : The Whole 30 Yards , Superstar and Obama ‘ M . Now, Nancy wants us to follow her as she takes on the business of making a film, from the early meetings to sponsorship discussions and marketing. And she is letting us in on the process from the very beginning. In the video announcing the news, Nancy wore a brown outfit with an oversized collar, structured shoulders and gathered balloon sleeves. She paired it with a gold leaf statement necklace and finger-wave hair, looking ready for the boardroom before getting into the business of filmmaking. But beyond the outfit, it was what she had to say that got us listening. Nancy Isime marks her transition behind the camera as an executive producer in a custom metallic brown dress with a flounced hem. “Well yes, you’ve known me as an actor. But this time, I’m stepping into a completely new chapter. This is my first production as executive producer!” And while she is excited about the new role, Nancy is not pretending she has everything figured out. She admitted that taking this step comes with a few nerves, saying, “Oh my God, guys, I can’t lie… I’ve never… my heart is doing gbi-gbi-gbi-gbi-gbi. Can I do this? Can I do this? Am I ready? I think it’s about time. Me self don try, huh?” We love that she is bringing us along for the ride, because Nancy is not keeping this experience behind closed doors. She wants her audience to see what goes into getting a film made, including the meetings, sponsorship conversations and marketing decisions that happen long before a project reaches our screens. Official actor profile image of Nigerian actress and TV presenter Nancy Isime, known for starring roles in Blood Sisters, Shanty Town, and Superstar. Photo Credit: Nancy Isime/Instagram “But I need you guys. I really, truly need you,” she said. “So come with me on this journey. Let’s go behind the scenes. Let’s go to the meetings, the sponsorship… Let’s do some marketing… We’ll see how it goes, guys. So see what I do. But for now, I’m just really excited to announce this to you. So, let’s begin. Shall we?” The announcement also comes with glimpses of Nancy stepping out for corporate engagements, attending meetings, getting styled on set and speaking with camera operators. It looks like we will be seeing a lot more of what happens on the production side, rather than only the finished work on screen. And since she has invited us behind the scenes, we are curious to see how this first produc

She paired it with a gold leaf statement necklace and finger-wave hair, looking ready for the boardroom before getting into the business of filmmaking. But beyond the outfit, it was what she had to say that got us listening. Nancy Isime marks her transition behind the camera as an executive producer in a custom metallic brown dress with a flounced hem. “Well yes, you’ve known me as an actor. But this time, I’m stepping into a completely new chapter. This is my first production as executive producer!” And while she is excited about the new role, Nancy is not pretending she has everything figured out. She admitted that taking this step comes with a few nerves, saying, “Oh my God, guys, I can’t lie… I’ve never… my heart is doing gbi-gbi-gbi-gbi-gbi. Can I do this? Can I do this? Am I ready? I think it’s about time. Me self don try, huh?” We love that she is bringing us along for the ride, because Nancy is not keeping this experience behind closed doors. She wants her audience to see what goes into getting a film made, including the meetings, sponsorship conversations and marketing decisions that happen long before a project reaches our screens. Official actor profile image of Nigerian actress and TV presenter Nancy Isime, known for starring roles in Blood Sisters, Shanty Town, and Superstar. Photo Credit: Nancy Isime/Instagram “But I need you guys. I really, truly need you,” she said. “So come with me on this journey. Let’s go behind the scenes. Let’s go to the meetings, the sponsorship… Let’s do some marketing… We’ll see how it goes, guys. So see what I do. But for now, I’m just really excited to announce this to you. So, let’s begin. Shall we?” The announcement also comes with glimpses of Nancy stepping out for corporate engagements, attending meetings, getting styled on set and speaking with camera operators. It looks like we will be seeing a lot more of what happens on the production side, rather than only the finished work on screen. And since she has invited us behind the scenes, we are curious to see how this first production comes together. Madam EP, we are following! Finger-wave hair and glossy lip liner complement Nancy Isime’s structured brown outfit for her major career announcement. *** Photo Credit: Nancy Isime/Instagram The post Permission to Call Nancy Isime Madam EP? The Actress Is Making Her Executive Producer Debut! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Kimberly Jael’s Black, Yellow & Red Gown Is Her Fashion Tribute to Uganda’s Independence Day
item.description: Kimberly Jael posing in a black, yellow, and red evening gown for Uganda Independence Day. Black sequins, sunshine yellow and a long red train? Kimberly Jael has found a gorgeous way to wear Uganda’s national colours. The model and Miss Universe Uganda 2026 first runner-up marked the country’s 64th Independence Day on 9 October in a sculpted gown that takes inspiration from the Ugandan flag. Let’s start with that corset. The strapless black bodice is covered in sequins, with lace trimming the neckline, while canary-yellow fabric falls across her chest and shoulders. Then, at the hips, crimson-red fabric gathers before flowing into a fitted mermaid skirt that trails along the floor. Each colour has its place, and the long red train gives the look an extra flourish. Kimberly Jael featuring graphic black, yellow, and red cheek makeup with pearl accents and cowrie shell drop earrings. Kimberly carried the colour scheme into her beauty look, too, with graphic black, yellow and red makeup sweeping across her left cheekbone. Tiny pearl embellishments add detail to the face art, while her cropped natural afro leaves room for her large drop earrings, finished with traditional cowrie shells. But Kimberly’s choices go beyond matching her outfit to the flag. She explained the meaning behind the gown in a message celebrating Uganda’s independence, connecting its details to the country’s history, the sacrifices of previous generations and the hopes she has for its future. Independence is not just a date, it’s the chains that were broken and blood that was shed!!! The glam is intentional. The pearls are for every tear my ancestors shed. The sequins are for every star in our future. The red train is long because our journey was long. This is what 64 years of resilience looks like in high fashion. Happy Independence Day Uganda — we are not just free, we are FASHIONABLY FREE! The strapless black sequined bodice is trimmed with lace and contrasted by canary-yellow fabric across the chest. The explanation gives the gown another layer: the pearls represent the tears of her ancestors, the sequins speak to future possibilities, and the long red train reflects Uganda’s journey to independence. It’s a personal tribute expressed through the very details that make the outfit memorable. Kimberly also had quite a run at the inaugural Miss Universe Uganda 2026 pageant, where she won five titles, including Miss Afrikana and the People’s Choice award. Beyond pageantry, she is a youth mentor and advocate for community development and youth empowerment. For Independence Day, she put her love for Uganda on display through fashion, right down to the pearls and that sweeping red train. Kimberly Jael marks Uganda’s 64th Independence Day in a custom gown inspired by the national flag. *** Photo Credit: Kimberly Jael/Instagram The post Kimberly Jael’s Black, Yellow & Red Gown Is Her Fashion Tribute to Uganda’s Independence Day appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the wor

item.title: Wunmi Adelusi: How Much Balance Is Really Possible for Women Pursuing Their Careers?
item.description: A confident, stylish woman descends city stairs, embodying elegance and modern business fashion. Photo Credit: Ono Kosuki/Pexels How do you balance it? That is one of the first questions women ask when they meet another woman who seems to have it all: the career, the family, the side projects, the composure. I understand the question. I’ve asked it myself. But the longer I live, the more convinced I am that we are asking for something that does not exist. When we ask for balance, we are really asking for the two sides of the scale to weigh the same, all the time. Equal weight to work and home. Equal weight to ambition and rest. Equal weight to the people who need the self and us we are trying not to lose. A scale, perfectly level, held steady every single day. But nothing honest works that way. Consider this: every major system of thought humanity has ever built carries a trade-off; a cost baked into its benefit. Prioritise individual freedom, and you risk the collective; protect the collective, and you constrain the individual. There has never been a framework, political or economic or moral, that delivered every good thing at once with no side effect. That is why no government pleases all its people, and why even the most admired ideas have always had their critics. If perfect balance cannot be engineered into our grandest theories, why do we expect to achieve it in a single human life, lived in real time, with finite hours? Balance, I’ve come to believe, is a myth. Not a lie exactly, but a mirage. You cannot give one hundred per cent to everything simultaneously. Something always gives. The only real question is whether you are choosing what gives, or letting it be chosen for you. So I’ve stopped chasing balance. I’ve started practising seasons . In every season of life, the demands are weighted differently. There are seasons when work must take more. Seasons when family must. Seasons of building, and seasons of recovering. The wisdom is not in holding all things equal; it is in reading accurately which season you are in, and letting your energy follow it without guilt. Within each season, there is a second discipline, one borrowed from an analogy many will know: learning to tell your glass balls from your rubber ones. Some of the things we juggle are rubber. If you drop them, they bounce. The deadline that can shift. The event you can miss. The email that can wait till Monday. They feel urgent, but they recover. Others are glass. Drop them, and they crack, sometimes beyond repair. Your health. A child’s childhood. A marriage. Your integrity. Certain relationships and certain moments that do not come round again. The tragedy is how often we exhaust ourselves protecting the rubber balls, answering every message, meeting every expectation, saying yes to everything, while a glass ball slips from the other hand. Knowing the difference is the real skill. Not balance. Triage. So when someone asks me how I balance it all, my honest answer is: I don’t

item.title: Sliding Doors meets Biff’s Almanac: City saga stirs up a world of alternate histories | Max Rushden
item.description: Even New Romantics have a view but this long story will not be cut short amid endless hypotheticals and split narratives It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: Ogaga Ifowodo Wins the 2026 $100,000 NLNG Prize for Literature
item.description: Nigerian poet and lawyer Ogaga Ifowodo has won the 2026 Nigeria Prize for Literature, sponsored by Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG), for his poetry collection, Why Does God Need a Gun ? Ifowodo’s win adds to a distinguished literary career spanning several decades. His other poetry collections include Homeland and Other Poems , which won the 1993 Association of Nigerian Authors (ANA) Poetry Prize; Madiba , which won the 2003 ANA/Cadbury Poetry Prize; The Oil Lamp , which won the 2005 ANA/Gabriel Okara Poetry Prize; and A Good Mourning , which was shortlisted for the Nigeria Prize for Literature in 2017. The 2026 edition of the Nigeria Prize for Literature focused on poetry and attracted 223 submissions. Ifowodo’s winning collection emerged from a final shortlist that included James Ngwu Eze ’s Unbind Me Now and Tares Oburumu ’s Flora’s Love Colony . NLNG’s Nigerian Prize for Literature is the biggest literary award on the continent, and the award comes with a $100,000 cash prize. Why does God need a gun? by @OgagaIfowodo wins The Nigeria Prize for Literature 2026. item.title: FOLA Appreciates Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie and 2Baba for Their Contributions to His Sophomore Album
item.description: Nigerian singer FOLA has expressed his appreciation for renowned author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie and music legend 2Baba for their contributions to his sophomore album , 9 . On the album’s second track, how many , FOLA samples a portion of Adichie’s Harvard speech, in which she reflects on the relationship between fear, self-doubt, and creativity. “Procrastinating is a form of fear, and it is difficult to acknowledge fear. But the truth is that you cannot create anything of value without both self-doubt and self-belief,” she says in the excerpt. The singer also samples 2Baba’s popular song, If Love Is A Crime , on crime , the 11th track on FOLA’s second album, paying homage to one of Nigeria’s most influential musicians and his enduring contribution to the country’s music scene. Taking to X (formerly Twitter), FOLA shared his gratitude to both figures, writing, “Today, I’m beyond grateful to Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie and the legendary 2Baba for their contribution to the arts, their blessings on my sophomore, and for leaving my generation multiple standards to aspire to.” Today, I’m beyond grateful to Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie and the legendary 2Baba for their contribution to the arts, their blessings on my sophomore, and for leaving my generation multiple standards to aspire to. https://t.co/fm4p5o4wPe — FOLA (@Folapondis) October 9, 2026 The post FOLA Appreciates Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie and 2Baba for Their Contributions to His Sophomore Album appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: BNXN and FOLA Are a Music Match Made in Heaven
item.description: Sometimes, when two artists find themselves together in a studio, they find it difficult to spark a connection. They can make a song together, but it might feel like climbing a cliff if they try to make another song. Meanwhile, some artists have that connection, that synergy, that whenever they find each other in the studio, they produce magic. They make beautiful, sweet music. For instance, Wizkid and Asake , who have not only featured one another on each other’s albums, Morayo and Lungu Boy , respectively, but have also released a joint project, an EP. As Wizkid puts it in their interview , they have had “successful collaborations.” There are artists like that who find creativity in the other’s creativity. So are BNXN and FOLA , whose music, when carefully compared in terms of lyricism, could be considered the same. They do not sound the same; no, two artists can never sound the same, but you could always imagine BNXN on a FOLA, and vice versa. And they have shown their fans that whenever they find each other on a song, there is always a synergy. Actually, FOLA sang in “ how many “, off his sophomore album , ‘ 9 ‘, “Mo Korin bi BNXN,” which means, I sing like BNXN. The journey began with the remix of FOLA’s hit song, Alone , and BNXN was featured. The collaboration introduced listeners to what would become one of the more interesting musical partnerships in Nigerian Afrobeats. BNXN brought his familiar, soulful delivery to the song, complementing FOLA’s smooth vocals and emotional approach to music. Then came Very Soon , a song on BNXN’s 2025 album, Captain , which featured FOLA. This time, FOLA joined BNXN on his own record, returning the favour and showing that their connection was not limited to one artist’s sound. They could find each other on either side of a collaboration and still make it work. Their musical relationship continued with Shamaya , another joint recording on BNXN’s Still in Charge EP. Now, the two artists have reunited on my type , a song on FOLA’s sophomore album, 9 , released on October 9, 2026. But for listeners who have followed BNXN and FOLA’s journey together, “My Type” is another opportunity to enjoy a pairing that has consistently found room for both artists to shine. BNXN and FOLA have given their listeners reasons to always look forward to what they might create together next. If their collaborations so far are anything to go by, this is one musical partnership worth keeping an eye on. For now, fans will enjoy BNXN’s latest EP, Still in Charge and FOLA’s sophomore album: the 14-track project that features other notable Nigerian and African artists, including Davido , Ayra Starr , Darkoo , Bella Shmurda and Zlatan . You will find favor in the sight of God and man. 4/4 , no misses. @Folapondis Love you and congratulations again! https://t.co/j7ihOuLCPA — Benson (@BNXN) October 9, 2026 The post BNXN and FOLA Are a Music Match Made in Heaven appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

But for listeners who have followed BNXN and FOLA’s journey together, “My Type” is another opportunity to enjoy a pairing that has consistently found room for both artists to shine. BNXN and FOLA have given their listeners reasons to always look forward to what they might create together next. If their collaborations so far are anything to go by, this is one musical partnership worth keeping an eye on. For now, fans will enjoy BNXN’s latest EP, Still in Charge and FOLA’s sophomore album: the 14-track project that features other notable Nigerian and African artists, including Davido , Ayra Starr , Darkoo , Bella Shmurda and Zlatan . item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: WalkHeartOn Turns 10, Bringing 11,896 Nigerians Together for Heart Health
item.description: Ten years ago, Power Oil invited Nigerians to take a step for their hearts in celebration of World Heart Day. A decade later, that step has become a movement. The 10th edition of WalkHeartOn , held on October 1, 2026, at The Stables Sports Ground , Surulere, Lagos, brought together thousands of people for a day centred on fitness, heart health, community and fun. The milestone edition recorded 25,536 registrations, with 11,896 people physically attending . From early-morning fitness activities and health checks to music, games, refreshments and entertainment, WalkHeartOn 10.0 created an experience that showed that prioritising your health does not have to be boring. Commenting on the milestone, Roland Akpe , Marketing Manager, Oils and Fats Portfolio at Tolaram , said, “For 10 years, WalkHeartOn has been a reflection of Power Oil’s commitment to helping Nigerians live healthier lives, reminding us that caring for our hearts goes beyond what we eat. It is also about staying active, moving more and making healthier choices every day. As we celebrate World Heart Day and a decade of WalkHeartOn, we are proud to have created a platform that brings Nigerians together to take meaningful steps towards healthier hearts.” For many attendees, it was a chance to exercise with friends and family. For others, it was an opportunity to meet new people, enjoy performances and simply step away from the usual routine. But beneath all the excitement was the message that has driven WalkHeartOn for a decade: every step towards a healthier lifestyle matters. Over the years, the annual walk has evolved from a fitness event into a community-driven platform that encourages Nigerians to make heart health part of their everyday lives. item.title: Women Innovators Building Smarter Ways to Live, Eat and Stay Healthy in Africa
item.description: Across Africa, some of the most interesting solutions to everyday problems are being built by women who have experienced those problems up close. A doctor sees patients struggling to access cardiac screening and builds an AI-powered ECG device. A nurse watches patients lose hours navigating the healthcare system and creates a digital platform to make it easier. A food entrepreneur sees farmers lose the value of their harvest and builds the processing infrastructure they need. An agronomist looks at Morocco’s water crisis and asks a different question: what if we could grow more food with far less water? These are the stories behind five of the 15 women named as 2026 Bayer Foundation Women Entrepreneurs Award winners globally, powered by the Impact Hub Network. The five African awardees come from Kenya, Ethiopia, Nigeria and Morocco, joining 10 other women entrepreneurs selected from across Latin America and Asia. From Kenya and Ethiopia to Nigeria and Morocco, their businesses are rethinking how communities access healthcare, preserve food and adapt to a changing climate. Each will receive €25,000 in non-dilutive funding alongside a six-month accelerator designed to help them strengthen their businesses and take their solutions further. Meet the women behind the ideas Dr. Alice Muhuhu of Aurora Health Systems , Kenya Alice started Aurora Health Systems after seeing patients arrive at the hospital with advanced heart conditions that could have been detected much earlier. Her answer is an AI-powered, portable ECG device designed to work offline and in low-resource clinics. It can detect more than 50 cardiac conditions and is already being used across more than 100 clinics in Kenya. But Alice is also tackling another problem in healthcare: whose data gets represented. Less than 1% of global ECG data comes from African populations, so Aurora is building a large-scale African cardiology dataset to help develop technology that better reflects the people it is intended to serve. Beamlak Alemayehu of Medanit Digital Health , Ethiopia For Beamlak , the healthcare problem was not always whether treatment existed. Sometimes, it was simply finding it. The former clinical nurse and social worker founded Medanit after seeing patients travel long distances, wait hours, and move between hospitals and pharmacies just to find the right care. Medanit brings those services together through an app, website, and low-bandwidth call centre, allowing people to connect with doctors, medication, and mental health services without requiring everyone to have the same level of internet access or digital literacy. In 2025, the platform reached more than 58,000 users and onboarded over 500 doctors and 60 healthcare partners.
